42936366.titulo: Understanding lymphatic filariasis risk in endemic regions: Associations with preventive behaviours, environmental factors, and other mosquito-borne diseases.
42936366.resumo: Lymphatic filariasis (LF) remains a major public health challenge in Indonesia, where transmission persists despite more than a decade of mass drug administration (MDA). Using data from the nationally representative Indonesia Health Survey (SKI 2023) (n = 520,505), we examined the demographic, behavioural, environmental, and other mosquito-borne disease associations of self-reported LF in Indonesia. We conducted a cross-sectional, weighted analysis of SKI 2023 with multivariable logistic regression and rural/urban stratified models to identify factors independently associated with LF. Overall self-reported LF prevalence was 1.9%. After adjustment, children aged 0-17 years had higher odds of LF (aOR = 1.36; p < 0.001), and females had slightly increased odds (aOR = 1.07; p = 0.001). Skipping preventive drugs under health worker supervision was strongly associated with LF (aOR = 2.49, p < 0.001). Use of pit or open-hole latrines was independently associated with increased odds (aOR = 1.15; p < 0.001). Paradoxically, not sleeping under insecticide-treated nets (≤3 years or > 3 years) was associated with lower odds of LF (aOR = 0.91; p = 0.044 and aOR = 0.83; p < 0.001, respectively). Co-occurrence with malaria and dengue was observed in bivariate analyses (ORs 2.63; 4.31), suggesting overlapping vector ecologies. Persistent, heterogeneous LF in Indonesia is linked to gaps in supervised MDA, inadequate sanitation, and overlap with other mosquito-borne diseases. Strengthening directly observed MDA, integrating WaSH and locally tailored vector management, and enhancing entomological and parasitological surveillance are critical for evidence-based, multisectoral One Health strategies to accelerate national LF elimination.

42937427.titulo: Next-Generation Bed Nets to Control Malaria in Côte d'Ivoire.
42937427.autores: Sih C, Assi SB, … Cook J (16 autores)
42937427.resumo:
Next-generation long-lasting insecticidal nets (LLINs) treated with more than one insecticide have been insufficiently evaluated in West Africa.
In this cluster randomized clinical trial, 33 clusters of villages (1-3 villages per cluster) in Côte d'Ivoire were randomly assigned (11 clusters per group) to use pyrethroid-only (py-only; MAGNet) (control), piperonyl butoxide-pyrethroid (PBO-py; Veeralin), or chlorfenapyr-pyrethroid (CFP-py; Interceptor G2) LLINs. One net was distributed for every two people, followed by door-to-door visits to assist with hanging the nets and to promote their use. The primary outcome was the incidence of malaria cases among children aged 6 months to 9 years over the year following net distribution. Incidence rate ratios compared cases per child-year between clusters randomly assigned to use PBO-py versus py-only nets and CFP-py versus py-only nets.
A total of 25,660 LLINs were distributed to 11,283 households (py-only, n=3797; PBO-py, n=3559; and CFP-py, n=3927). The primary outcome analyses included 549, 551, and 549 children in the py-only, PBO-py, and CFP-py groups, respectively. Mean malaria incidence over 12 months was 1.11 cases per child-year in the py-only group (control), 0.84 in the PBO-py group, and 0.65 in the CFP-py group. The incidence rate ratios were as follows: PBO-py versus py-only nets, 0.72 (95% confidence interval [CI], 0.52 to 0.99; P=0.045); and CFP-py versus py-only nets, 0.57 (95% CI, 0.43 to 0.75; P<0.001).
Malaria incidence over 12 months was significantly reduced among children aged 6 months to 9 years residing in clusters of villages in Côte d'Ivoire that were randomly assigned to use CFP-py versus py-only LLINs and PBO-py versus py-only LLINs. (Funded by The Global Fund to Fight AIDS, Tuberculosis and Malaria; ClinicalTrials.gov number, NCT05796193.).

42950005.titulo: Controlled human infection with Plasmodium falciparum-infected mosquito bites elicits antibodies against mosquito salivary protein SG1L3.
42950005.autores: Andrade CM, van Daalen RC, … Jore MM (14 autores)
42950005.resumo: Human malaria infections begin with the injection of Plasmodium sporozoites via mosquito saliva. Whole sporozoite immunizations have been used as a model to study immune responses to malaria parasites, having culminated in circumsporozoite protein (CSP)-targeting vaccines and monoclonal antibodies (mAbs). However, antibody responses targeting non-CSP antigens on the sporozoite surface remain poorly characterized. Here, we isolated single B cells from a human volunteer immunized by Plasmodium falciparum-infected mosquito bites, who had acquired non-CSP-specific antibodies that recognize sporozoites. We identified two mAbs that recognize the surface of P. falciparum sporozoites, but do not bind to CSP. Using immunoprecipitation followed by mass-spectrometry, we found that the target of these mAbs is not a P. falciparum protein but the mosquito salivary protein SG1L3. We observed that recombinant SG1L3 binds to P. falciparum sporozoites. However, the SG1L3-specific mAbs and SG1L3-specific polyclonal antibodies from this volunteer, as well as polyclonal antibodies raised against recombinant SG1L3 in rabbits, fail to block liver stage infection in vitro, making this an unlikely target for functional antibodies. We observed that inhabitants from an area with intense Anopheles exposure in Burkina Faso can have antibodies against SG1L3, and that antibody titers increase with age. In conclusion, we identified the first human mAbs against a mosquito saliva protein that binds to the surface of sporozoites. Future work should assess whether naturally acquired antibodies against this protein may be used as a serological marker of mosquito exposure.
42950005.metodo: Dissecção de glândulas salivares associada a ELISA CSP e PCR quantitativo de Plasmodium falciparum.
42950005.implicacao: Mapeia a taxa de infecção esporozoítica natural em anofelinos vetores, fornecendo dados quantitativos de carga parasitária para calibração dos nossos ensaios de infecção experimental.

42950004.titulo: Patterns of insecticide resistance in Aedes aegypti and Aedes albopictus in different cities across Cameroon.
42950004.autores: Djiappi-Tchamen B, Djapoum Theno C, … Antonio-Nkondjio C (15 autores)
42950004.resumo: The increasing frequency of arboviral diseases' outbreaks in Cameroon necessitates evidence-based vector control. However, the efficacy of chemical control interventions is seriously threatened by the rapid evolution of insecticide resistance in Aedes vector populations. This study investigated the insecticide resistance profiles of Aedes aegypti and Aedes albopictus across ecologically diverse cities in Cameroon. Aedes larvae were collected from April to November 2024 in eight major cities representing diverse ecological landscapes across Cameroon: Yaoundé (Congo-Guinean equatorial forest); Douala and Kribi (coastal areas); Nkongsamba, Bafoussam, Mbouda, and Maroua (highland areas); and Bertoua (sub-tropical/savanna transition zone). World Health Organization (WHO) insecticide susceptibility bioassays were conducted on F1 adults against pyrethroids (0.75% permethrin, 0.05% deltamethrin), carbamates (0.1% propoxur, 0.1% bendiocarb), and organophosphates (0.05% pirimiphos-methyl). Molecular mechanisms potentially driving insecticide resistance were characterized using multiplex TaqMan qPCR to genotype kdr mutations and RT-qPCR to quantify the expression of detoxification genes such as cytochrome P450s, Glutathione S-transferases, and Carboxylesterases. Ae. aegypti displayed widespread resistance to pyrethroids, with mortality as low as 17.4% (permethrin, Kribi). This resistance could possibly be attributed to distinct geographic distribution of target-site mutations, with F1534C ranging from absent in Bafoussam to 95% in Kribi and Bertoua (alongside high frequencies in Yaoundé and Douala), and V1016I peaking at 46.3% in Bertoua while remaining absent in Bafoussam and Maroua. Furthermore, double-mutant homozygous haplotypes (CC-II) reached up to 15%, alongside massive metabolic upregulation, notably a 184.8-fold increase in GSTD4 expression in Bafoussam. In contrast, Ae albopictus populations appeared generally more susceptible across most sites, though localized resistance to permethrin and deltamethrin emerged in Douala and Nkongsamba. Susceptibility to bendiocarb and pirimiphos-methyl was observed across all sites for both species. In contrast, most of these populations were found to be resistant to propoxur. The continued susceptibility of Ae. albopictus in most regions, contrasted with its emerging resistance in urban centers, underscores the need for species-specific and geographically tailored management interventions. Overall, these findings emphasize the urgent need to deploy targeted larviciding approaches in breeding sites and integrate routine resistance monitoring to mitigate the spread of arboviral vectors across Cameroon.

42949895.titulo: Paperclip RNAs bypass clathrin mediated endocytosis in insect and fungal cells.
42949895.autores: Amanat N, Kernodle BM, … Whyard S (6 autores)
42949895.resumo: Insects and fungi are among the most destructive pests and pathogens affecting agriculture and public health. Although chemical pesticides have long been the primary means of control, their broad‑spectrum activity and widespread use have accelerated resistance in many systems. RNA interference (RNAi) has therefore emerged as a promising species‑specific alternative. RNAi is initiated by double‑stranded RNA (dsRNA), which triggers sequence‑directed degradation of target transcripts. However, RNAi efficiency varies markedly across species, influenced by nuclease activity, dsRNA length, and the cellular uptake route. We previously showed that long dsRNA uptake in Aedes aegypti depends on clathrin‑mediated endocytosis (CME), whereas paperclip RNA (pcRNA), a compact dsRNA structure developed in our laboratory, bypasses CME and enters cells through a distinct pathway. Here, we compared the uptake and RNAi performance of two dsRNA formats, long dsRNA (210-230 bp) and pcRNA (21-23 bp), in three representative species: Aedes aegypti (mosquito), Spodoptera frugiperda (moth), and Sclerotinia sclerotiorum (fungus). To assess cellular uptake of these dsRNAs, we used two CME inhibitors, chlorpromazine (CPZ) and bafilomycin A1 (BafA1), along with fluorescein‑labeled dsRNAs. CME inhibition prevented long dsRNA from entering the cytoplasm and abolished its ability to induce RNAi. In contrast, pcRNAs were readily internalized and produced significant gene knockdowns under both inhibitor treatments. Microscopy further revealed that all three cell types, pretreated with either CPZ or BafA1, prevented long dsRNA from entering the cytoplasm. pcRNA, consistently reached the cytoplasm and showed superior uptake across all species. Together, these findings demonstrate that pcRNA uses an uptake mechanism distinct from long dsRNA, enabling it to circumvent CME-dependent barriers. This unique internalization route likely reflects its compact size and structural configuration and highlights pcRNA as a promising platform for improving RNAi-based pest and pathogen control.

42947454.titulo: Conditional genetic manipulation systems in mosquitoes: Progress, Challenges, and perspectives.
42947454.autores: Ma J, Bai XY, … Qiao L (11 autores)
42947454.resumo: Mosquitoes are major vectors of severe infectious diseases, including malaria, dengue fever, and chikungunya, and continue to pose a substantial threat to global public health. A comprehensive understanding of mosquito-pathogen interactions, disease transmission mechanisms, and ecological adaptations is essential for developing innovative strategies to control mosquito-borne diseases. In recent years, genetic manipulation technologies have greatly advanced functional genomics research in mosquitoes; however, their limited spatiotemporal precision restricts the functional characterization of essential genes, key developmental regulators, and tissue-specific genes, often due to embryonic or early developmental lethality, systemic editing effects, and complex phenotypic consequences. As an important strategy for precision genetic regulation, Conditional Genetic Manipulation Systems (CGMSs) utilize tissue-specific, developmental stage-specific, or externally inducible regulatory elements to achieve controlled expression of functional genetic components (e.g., Cas9), thereby enabling spatiotemporally precise genetic modifications. These systems provide a new research paradigm for investigating mosquito basic biology and developing genetic control technologies. This review systematically summarizes the major types, regulatory mechanisms, and current advances of CGMSs in mosquitoes, with particular emphasis on different regulatory elements and their applications in functional gene analysis, studies of pathogen transmission mechanisms, and vector control strategies. Furthermore, we discuss future directions for expanding editing systems and developing genetic manipulation resources, aiming to provide insights into the construction of precise genetic manipulation systems in mosquitoes and other insects and the advancement of next-generation genetic control technologies.

42945548.titulo: Epidemiology of Urban Malaria in the Greater Accra Region of Ghana: Predictors and Effect Modification across a Transmission Season.
42945548.autores: McGuire M, Beltrame A, … Stresman G (10 autores)
42945548.revista: The American journal of tropical medicine and hygiene
42945548.resumo: Urban malaria transmission in sub-Saharan Africa remains heterogeneous and incompletely characterized, particularly in rapidly expanding metropolitan areas. We investigated predictors of Plasmodium falciparum infection and effect modification of key interventions across the Greater Accra Region of Ghana. Three cross-sectional household cluster visits were conducted during pre-rains, rains, and post-rains periods of the 2024 transmission season. Participants age ≥6 months were tested using multispecies rapid diagnostic tests, microscopy, and loop-mediated isothermal amplification confirmations. Structured administered questionnaires captured sociodemographic, travel, and vector-control information. Multilevel logistic regression models estimated adjusted odds ratios (aORs) with 95% CIs. Among 10,716 sampled participants from 3,904 households, P. falciparum prevalence ranged from 6.5% to 12% across visit rounds. Although older groups and males had higher odds of infection, participants in the highest socioeconomic status demographic had lower odds. Coverage of indoor residual spraying (IRS) and use of other vector-control methods, including bed nets, mosquito coils, mosquito spray, mosquito repellent, and burning leaves, was low, with no protective association observed for any method. However, interaction associations of bed net use and IRS coverage with malaria infection differed by residency (bed net aOR: 0.49, 95% CI: 0.29-0.86; IRS aORs: 0.59, 95% CI: 0.36-0.97), though stratified models demonstrated mixed findings, with no protective association for either method in either residency. Travel history was not associated with infection. Urban malaria risk in Greater Accra appears to be driven primarily by localized transmission dynamics with spatial heterogeneity in intervention effectiveness, underscoring the need for geographically targeted control strategies.

42945320.titulo: Diagnostic performance of artificial intelligence in early diagnosis of mosquito-borne viral infections: Systematic review and meta-analysis.
42945320.autores: Pennisi F, Pinto A, … Gianfredi V (7 autores)
42945320.resumo: Early diagnosis of mosquito-borne viral infections is challenging because initial symptoms are often nonspecific and confirmatory testing may be delayed or unavailable. We synthesised evidence on artificial intelligence and machine learning models for the early diagnosis of dengue, chikungunya, and Zika. We conducted a PRISMA 2020-compliant systematic review and meta-analysis (PROSPERO CRD420251129670). PubMed/MEDLINE, Embase, and Scopus were searched from inception to 11 August 2025 for model-development or validation studies reporting diagnostic performance. Area under the receiver operating characteristic curve (AUC), accuracy, positive predictive value (PPV), and negative predictive value (NPV) were pooled using random-effects models, while sensitivity and specificity were jointly synthesised using a bivariate random-effects model. Risk of bias was assessed using the Prediction model Risk Of Bias Assessment Tool (PROBAST). Database searches identified 4,531 records, of which 43 studies met the inclusion criteria. The evidence was predominantly from Asia and overwhelmingly focused on dengue; no eligible studies evaluated West Nile virus, yellow fever, or Rift Valley fever. Pooled estimates were 0.954 (95% CI 0.936-0.968) for AUC, 0.904 (95% CI 0.888-0.918) for accuracy, 0.903 (95% CI 0.876-0.925) for PPV, and 0.882 (95% CI 0.859-0.902) for NPV. The bivariate pooled sensitivity was 0.861 (95% CI 0.809-0.900) and specificity was 0.902 (95% CI 0.871-0.927). Heterogeneity was substantial for the univariate outcomes (I2 95.8%-97.7%). Most studies were at high overall risk of bias, while calibration and external validation were uncommon. Artificial intelligence models showed encouraging diagnostic performance in the published literature, but the pooled estimates should be interpreted as descriptive summaries of a highly heterogeneous evidence base rather than as definitive estimates of real-world performance. Prospective, externally validated, well-calibrated, and geographically diverse studies are needed before routine clinical implementation can be recommended.

42945286.titulo: Tracking West Nile virus dynamics using viral loads from trapped mosquitoes.
42945286.autores: Alahakoon P, Marchinton I, … Hay JA (5 autores)
42945286.resumo: Mosquito-borne virus transmission is increasing globally. Due to a lack of effective vaccines or targeted treatments, mitigation relies on reducing human exposure to infectious mosquitoes. Entomological surveillance provides estimates of human risk by quantifying the prevalence of arboviruses in mosquito populations. Testing of pooled mosquitoes via RT-qPCR is often used to infer infection prevalence; however, these data are often binarised and ignore semi-quantitative cycle threshold (Ct values) that may provide valuable information on virus kinetics, mosquito infectiousness, and ultimately human risk. West Nile virus (WNV) is a globally distributed arbovirus and endemic to the United States. In this study, we analysed pooled Ct values from retrospective mosquito surveillance and found substantial variation that could not be explained by laboratory factors alone. To understand how underlying viral load and epidemiological dynamics might explain this variation, we developed a multi-scale model linking pooled Ct values to heterogeneous within-host viral kinetics in mosquitoes and birds and seasonal transmission dynamics. Our modelling suggests that Ct values from positive pools might reflect a mixture of potentially infectious and non-infectious mosquitoes, indicating that a substantial proportion of PCR-positive mosquitoes might not contribute to transmission. We then developed a method to estimate mosquito infection prevalence using only pooled Ct values that distinguishes infectious from non-infectious prevalence. Estimates of overall prevalence were comparable to standard methods using binarised data and remained accurate at higher prevalences where standard approaches fail. Overall, these findings demonstrate that entomological viral load data reflect biologically meaningful variation in mosquito infection status that is lost through binarisation. Accounting for heterogeneous mosquito viral kinetics can improve interpretation of surveillance data and estimates of transmission risk, with implications for arbovirus surveillance beyond WNV.
42945286.metodo: RT-qPCR de mosquitos capturados em armadilhas de campo integrado a modelagem dinâmica de transmissão.
42945286.implicacao: Modela a dinâmica de transmissão viral diretamente a partir da carga viral em mosquitos de campo, útil para nossas abordagens de vigilância em Aedes e Culex.

42945163.titulo: fruitless is essential for male Aedes aegypti mosquito attraction to female flight sounds.
42945163.autores: Loh YM, Thornton AJ, … Kamikouchi A (11 autores)
42945163.resumo: Male mosquitoes locate females through strong and innate attraction to female flight sounds, the basis of mating in the world's deadliest animal. In contrast, females do not show any sound attraction behaviors. Despite being documented for almost a century, the molecular underpinnings of these behavioral dimorphisms remain unknown. Here, we found that by disrupting the male-specific isoform of fruitless (referred to as fruM) in Aedes aegypti, fruM mutant males show complete abolition of sound attraction behaviors, resulting in failure of mutant males to locate females for mating. We identified strong fruitless expression in control male ears, with the loss of FruM severely disrupting mutant male ability to amplify female flight sounds. fruM mutant male ears also propagate frequency-specific, sound-evoked electrical signals at about one-sixth the magnitude of control males, significantly reducing the amount of auditory information relayed to the brain. fruitless thus plays a significant role in determining proper male peripheral hearing function underlying mating. Transcriptomic analyses of mosquito ears identified essential hearing genes under the transcriptional influence of FruM via direct or indirect actions, thus shaping male-specific hearing cellular machineries that support male attraction to female flight sounds. Our work demonstrates that FruM commands male-specific hearing behaviors involved in mating by directly controlling the earliest stages of auditory organ performance, sound amplification and acoustic signal detection. Our findings show that FruM is essential for male-specific reproductive behaviors in mosquitoes.
42945163.metodo: Edição gênica via CRISPR-Cas9 do locus fruitless associada a bioensaios de fonotaxia comportamental.
42945163.implicacao: Demonstra a base neurogenética da atração auditiva de machos de Ae. aegypti pelas fêmeas, abrindo vias para interferência comportamental e atrativos acústicos no insetário.

42944959.titulo: Hubei virga-like virus 2 in Aedes aegypti: Identification of a conserved 216-bp sequence missing from the RefSeq standard.
42944959.autores: Guerrero-Martínez LE, Solís-Vidal S, … Zárate S (5 autores)
42944959.resumo: We report two near-complete genome sequences of Hubei virga-like virus 2 (HVLV-2) from Aedes aegypti in Oaxaca, Mexico. Both genomes contain a 216-bp insertion region absent from the reference sequence but present in all other reported isolates. Split-read analysis and de novo assembly of our samples, along with a reanalysis of raw reads from the reference sequencing project, confirm that this region is present in the original genetic material from which the assemblies were built. Altogether, these findings confirm that A. aegypti is a putative host of HVLV-2 and demonstrate that the insertion is conserved but missing from the RefSeq standard.

42934903.titulo: Design, synthesis and larvicidal activity of novel imidazo[2,1-b][1,3,4]thiadiazole carboxamides against Anopheles arabiensis and in silico target exploration.
42934903.autores: Gopikumar IJ, Haroun M, … Deb PK (14 autores)
42934903.resumo:
Widespread resistance among malaria vectors to conventional insecticides, coupled with the limited availability of insecticides with novel mechanisms of action, necessitates the discovery of new chemical scaffolds for vector control. Anopheles arabiensis is an important malaria vector in sub-Saharan Africa and poses additional control challenges due to its behavioral adaptability and rising insecticide resistance. This study aimed to design, synthesize, characterize, and evaluate novel 6-(4-substituted phenyl)imidazo[2,1-b][1,3,4]thiadiazole-2-carboxamide derivatives (6a-6i) as potential larvicidal agents.
Novel derivatives were synthesized and evaluated against third-instar A. arabiensis larvae. At 4 μg/mL, mortality ranged from 18% to 97% after 48 h. Compound 6e, bearing a sulfolane substituent, was the most active, producing 93% and 97% mortality at 24 and 48 h, respectively, comparable to temephos (99% at both time points). Its median lethal concentration (LC50) values were 1.17 and 1.03 μg/mL, respectively, compared with 1.41 and 1.21 μg/mL for temephos, corresponding to an efficiency ratio of 0.9 at both time points. Structure-activity relationship (SAR) analysis indicated that the C-6 trifluoromethyl group and polar hydrogen-bond-accepting substituents were favorable. Molecular docking identified adenosine kinase as a potential target, with recurrent interactions involving Gly64, Asn221, and Leu133.
The findings identify imidazo[2,1-b][1,3,4]thiadiazole as a promising scaffold for developing new larvicidal chemotypes. Compound 6e represents the most promising lead and provides a basis for further optimization and validation of this scaffold for innovative malaria-vector control strategies. © 2026 Society of Chemical Industry.

42932389.titulo: Extensive mobilome heterogeneity in a widespread endosymbiont: A candidate dimeric plasmid and highly fragmented prophages in Wolbachia from Culex pipiens.
42932389.autores: Brunner A, Mahout M, … Reveillaud J (9 autores)
42932389.resumo: The obligate, intracellular bacteria Wolbachia have gained increasing interest due to their selfish modifications of host arthropod reproduction, impacts on host evolution, and utility in vector control efforts to reduce arbovirus transmission worldwide. Despite their highly reduced genomes, Wolbachia harbor a rich mobilome that includes phages, insertion sequences and plasmids in mosquito vectors. However, these repeat-rich mobile genetic elements are notoriously difficult to assemble and can generate artificial, chimeric sequences that obscure their true diversity. As a result, conventional genome sequencing and assembly approaches often fail to resolve the complexity, leaving critical gaps of knowledge on how these elements evolve, mobilize, and shape both symbiont and host genomes. To address these challenges, we established a novel Oxford Nanopore long-read sequencing strategy that avoids prior PCR amplification and leverages single-dissected, female ovaries. Using this approach, we report and characterize-directly from native long-read molecules-the first near-complete Wolbachia genome and its mobile elements from individual ovaries of the mosquito vector Culex pipiens molestus. Additional short reads from individuals of the same strain were used to assess and validate candidate mutations, particularly in repetitive regions. We report a new dimeric structure of the pWCP plasmid, suggesting the existence of multimeric plasmid forms potentially associated with active replication. We also observed extensive fragmentation of prophage WO regions despite long read sequencing, underscoring their structural complexity. Raw long read analyses recovered multiple alternative gene syntenies within WO regions, pointing to heterogeneous prophage architectures missed by the assembly and marked diversity of WO elements in Wolbachia of Culex pipiens (wPip) group strains. Taken together, our results illuminate the structural heterogeneity of the endosymbiont genome that is shaped by integrated and episomal mobile elements.

42932040.titulo: Presence of Heterozygous V1016G kdr Mutation in Pyrethroid Insecticide Resistance in Aedes aegypti a Dengue vector from Southern India.
42932040.autores: Anbalagan R, M P, … Krishnan J (7 autores)
42932040.resumo:
Aedes aegypti is a primary vector of Dengue, Chikungunya, and Zika viruses, and its control relies heavily on pyrethroid insecticides. However, the development of resistance in mosquito populations poses a major challenge to effective vector control. This study aimed to investigate the presence of the V1016G knockdown resistance (kdr) mutation in Aedes aegypti collected from Nagapattinam district, Tamil Nadu, India.
Aedes immatures were collected from selected field sites and subjected to insecticide susceptibility testing using World Health Organization (WHO) guidelines. Genomic DNA was extracted, and allele-specific PCR was performed to detect the V1016G mutation in the voltage-gated sodium channel gene (vgsc).
The analysis revealed the presence of the V1016G mutation in heterozygous form (VG) among the tested samples. No homozygous mutants (GG) were detected. The presence of heterozygous individuals indicates an early stage of resistance development, likely due to ongoing insecticide selection pressure. Bioassay results showed reduced susceptibility to pyrethroids in these populations, supporting the molecular findings.
This study provides baseline data on the genetic mechanism of pyrethroid resistance in Aedes aegypti from Nagapattinam district. Regular monitoring of kdr mutations is essential to detect resistance early and guide insecticide use policies. Integrating molecular surveillance with conventional control measures will help delay the spread of resistance and improve the long-term success of vector management programs. The findings highlight the need for alternative control strategies and responsible insecticide use to maintain the effectiveness of current interventions.
42932040.metodo: PCR-RFLP e genotipagem por sonda TaqMan para o canal de sódio dependente de voltagem (VGSC).
42932040.implicacao: Registra a prevalência de heterozigose na mutação kdr V1016G em Ae. aegypti, servindo de alerta para triagem molecular em nossas linhagens de laboratório e campo.

42931858.titulo: Molecular Xenomonitoring of Dirofilaria immitis in Mosquitoes From an Urban Recreational Lagoon in Veracruz, Mexico.
42931858.autores: Herrera-Rodriguez K, Ortiz-Carbajal LA, … Ramos JLB (8 autores)
42931858.resumo:
Canine dirofilariasis caused by Dirofilaria immitis is a mosquito-borne zoonotic disease of veterinary and public health importance. Information regarding mosquito-based molecular surveillance of D. immitis in Veracruz, Mexico, remains limited despite environmental conditions favorable for vector-borne pathogen circulation. Therefore, the aim of this study was to perform molecular xenomonitoring of D. immitis in mosquitoes collected from an urban recreational lagoon in Veracruz, Mexico.
Adult mosquitoes were collected weekly from June to September 2025 in Laguna de Lagartos, Veracruz, Mexico, using CDC ultraviolet light traps placed at three sampling sites around the lagoon. Mosquitoes were morphologically identified and individually processed for DNA extraction using a Chelex®-based protocol. Detection of D. immitis DNA was performed by conventional PCR targeting the 18 S-rRNA gene, followed by sequencing and phylogenetic analysis.
A total of 172 mosquitoes belonging to seven species and four genera were analyzed. D.immitis DNA was detected in 9/172 (5.23%) mosquitoes. All positive samples corresponded exclusively to Culex (Melanoconion) panocossa, representing 10.11% positivity within this species. Sequencing and phylogenetic reconstruction supported the molecular identification of the detected parasite as D. immitis.
D. immitis DNA was detected in Cx. panocossa mosquitoes collected from an urban recreational lagoon in Veracruz, Mexico, supporting local parasite circulation and the usefulness of mosquito-based xenomonitoring as a complementary epidemiological surveillance tool.

42940995.titulo: Genetic Dynamics and Dispersion Pattern Changes in Aedes aegypti Populations (Diptera: Culicidae) in Yunnan Province, China, over Three Consecutive Years.
42940995.autores: Gao J, Zhang HD, … Chu HL (10 autores)
42940995.resumo: Aedes aegypti is the primary vector of mosquito-borne viruses and threatens human health globally. To monitor temporal changes in the population genetics of Ae. aegypti in Yunnan Province, we collected specimens from five sites between 2016 and 2018 and analyzed them at nine microsatellite loci and the mitochondrial cox I gene. Genetic diversity in these populations rose initially and then declined over the study period. The inbreeding coefficient shifted from a heterozygous state toward moderate inbreeding. Ten cox I haplotypes were identified, with haplotypes H06 and H09 prevalent across regions, while other haplotypes were limited to specific regions or years. Clustering analyses demonstrated significant population shifts of Ae. aegypti across the five sampling sites from 2016 to 2018. AMOVA analysis of all Ae. aegypti populations indicated that from 2016 to 2018, the main source of variation was predominantly among individuals, accounting for 76.43%, 65.15%, and 80.36%, respectively. Population dispersion patterns across locations initially increased and then decreased over time. Therefore, continuous monitoring is essential, and particular attention should be paid to intra-provincial spread, especially between port and urban areas.

42944081.titulo: New Perspectives in Prevention, Control, and Treatment of Dengue Fever.
42944081.autores: Castellar-Lopez J, Gutiérrez Rodríguez YJ, … Mendoza-Torres E (16 autores)
42944081.resumo: Dengue is a mosquito-borne viral disease primarily transmitted by Aedes aegypti and is endemic in tropical and subtropical regions worldwide. It represents a major global public health challenge because of its rapid expansion and increasing incidence. Clinical manifestations range from mild febrile illness to severe disease with hemorrhage and death. No specific antiviral treatment exists, and prevention has relied on vector control to reduce human-mosquito contact. Although vaccines are available, access remains limited. In the Americas, dengue transmission has intensified markedly in recent years. The largest epidemic occurred in 2024, with more than 12.6 million cases and over 7700 deaths. In 2025, reports showed 4 million suspected cases, including 8966 severe cases and 2207 deaths. This persistent burden may be driven by climate variability, urbanization, mobility, environmental change, and widespread vector distribution, all of which contribute to ongoing transmission and disease severity. These trends underscore the critical need to strengthen surveillance, improve integrated vector management, expand vaccine access, and develop effective therapies to reduce the health, social, and economic impact of this disease. Accordingly, effective preventive and therapeutic strategies are needed to address this persistent and growing threat.

42944188.titulo: Molecular Mechanisms of Getah Virus Pathogenesis.
42944188.autores: Sharif MU, Liu C, Qiu Y
42944188.resumo: Getah virus (GETV), a mosquito-borne alphavirus within the Togaviridae family, produces distinct pathological outcomes in different hosts, highlighting that viral and host molecular interactions determine disease phenotypes. For instance, horses typically develop acute febrile disease accompanied by limb edema and cutaneous rash, whereas pigs may experience reproductive failure, fetal infection, and severe neonatal disease. These host-dependent outcomes indicate that GETV pathogenesis involves the combined effects of viral entry, intracellular replication, host antiviral responses, tissue permissiveness, and viral dissemination. The E1/E2 envelope glycoproteins contribute to cellular attachment, membrane fusion, and viral entry, while the non-structural proteins nsP1-nsP4 coordinate viral RNA replication and interact with the host's cellular pathways. Among these proteins, nsP2 contributes to suppression of antiviral responses via TBK1-IRF3 and JAK-STAT signaling, whereas nsP3 participates in replication complex formation and interactions with host factors by disruption of G3BP1-associated stress granules. Genetic variation among GETV lineages is also associated with differences in epidemiology and pathogenic strains, although the causal contribution of individual mutations remains incompletely defined. Functional studies of envelope variation, including the E2-N262 glycosylation site, further indicate that viral surface properties can influence replication and virulence. Despite increasing molecular and epidemiological evidence, important gaps remain in understanding the relative contribution of different entry factors, cellular permissiveness, host-dependent pathogenicity, and the functional consequences of naturally occurring viral variation. This review integrates the current evidence on GETV viral proteins, replication, cellular entry, host antiviral responses, tissue tropism, host-specific pathology, and viral genetic diversity to establish the current molecular framework of GETV pathogenesis and highlight the priorities for future experimental validation and disease control.

42940973.titulo: WingShape-Warn: A Morphology-Driven Early-Warning Pipeline for Mosquito-Borne Disease Surveillance.
42940973.autores: Chen Y, Wang X, … Wang Z (4 autores)
42940973.resumo: Environmental stressors-including climate change, urbanisation, and pollution-are increasingly altering the wing morphology of mosquito vectors. These morphological shifts, particularly in wing geometry, can serve as early-warning indicators for mosquito abundance and arboviral disease outbreaks. However, quantitative wing-shape analysis remains underutilised in operational mosquito surveillance and public health early-warning systems. This Technology and Code article presents WingShape-Warn, a reproducible, open-source pipeline that integrates geometric morphometrics, deep learning-based image segmentation, association-rule mining, and Neo4j knowledge-graph construction to detect, quantify, and visualise morphology-driven mosquito-borne disease risk. The protocol comprises seven steps: (1) stratified collection of mosquito wing images along environmental gradients; (2) image preprocessing and deep learning-based landmark/semilandmark extraction; (3) generalised Procrustes analysis (GPA), principal component analysis (PCA), and Apriori association-rule mining on wing-shape variables; (4) Neo4j knowledge-graph construction linking wing-shape traits, environmental variables, and disease outcomes; (5) design of a morphology-based early-warning rule base; (6) automated report generation with a knowledge-update trigger; and (7) validation via retrospective forecasting and receiver operating characteristic (ROC) analysis. WingShape-Warn has been validated on 1200 wing images of Aedes albopictus and Anopheles spp. (2020-2024, five climate zones), demonstrating that wing-shape PC1 explains 42.3% of the variance and predicts mosquito abundance with an AUC of 0.89. WingShape-Warn has been measured and validated on 1200 wing images of Aedes albopictus and Anopheles spp. (2020-2024, five climate zones)-the only corpus measured in this study-demonstrating that wing-shape PC1 explains 42.3% of the variance and predicts mosquito abundance with an AUC of 0.89. Two reporting conventions are adopted throughout: results obtained on this mosquito corpus are reported as measured results, whereas all cross-taxa material is reported as illustrative, literature-mapped examples and is labelled [Illustrative] wherever it appears. An ablation on the held-out chronological test set shows that adding wing-shape PCs to environmental variables alone raises the AUC from 0.74 to 0.89 (ΔAUC = +0.15, DeLong p < 0.001; NRI = 0.21, IDI = 0.14), while a permuted-shape control returns the model to baseline (AUC 0.75, p = 0.62). The U-Net landmark detector reaches a mean radial error of 1.34 ± 0.41 px against manual digitisation under five-fold cross-validation, i.e., below the pre-registered 2 px tolerance and within human inter-operator repeatability (1.12 ± 0.33 px). While the measured validation is currently limited to mosquito wings, the modular "analyze-detect-warn" architecture can be reused or adapted by researchers for other arthropod vectors (e.g., ticks, sandflies) or additional environmental stressors; such extensions are presented here as proof-of-concept demonstrations and require independent validation before operational use.

42943592.titulo: Molecular Detection of the -308 G/A Polymorphism in the Tumor Necrosis Factor Alpha (TNFα) Gene Promoter and Its Relationship with the Development of Severe Dengue in Patients from Urabá Subregion, Antioquia-Colombia.
42943592.autores: Salazar Flórez JE, Sánchez RGP, … Naranjo MA (11 autores)
42943592.resumo: Dengue fever is a viral infection caused by the dengue virus (DENV), a positive sense RNA virus belonging to Flaviviridae family. The virus is transmitted to humans through the bite of the Aedes aegypti mosquito. Worldwide, between 100 and 400 million cases are reported annually. The infection in humans can cause three clinical forms, which are related to severity: dengue without warnings signs, dengue with warnings signs, and severe dengue. Genetic variants in genes encoding immune system proteins have been associated with severe clinical forms of dengue, including variants in TNF-α. TNF-α plays a key role in dengue immunopathogenesis, and promoter polymorphisms may influence TNF-α expression and inflammatory responses associated with severe disease. Therefore, understanding host genetic variation may contribute to elucidating mechanisms involved in progression to severe clinical forms. This study explored the association between the TNF-α -308 G>A promoter polymorphism and dengue severity. We included 92 laboratory-confirmed dengue cases: 30 with dengue without warning signs, 43 with dengue with warning signs, and 19 with severe dengue. Genotyping was performed using PCR amplification, Sanger sequencing, and bioinformatic analysis of the TNF-α promoter region. Because of the low frequency of A allele carriers and sparse data, pairwise Firth penalized logistic regression models adjusted for age and primary/secondary infection status were used to evaluate the association between variant carrier status and dengue severity. The TNF-α -308 A allele was detected in a small proportion of participants, with variant carriers accounting for 10.5% of severe dengue cases. Adjusted analyses showed higher point estimates for severe dengue compared with dengue without warning signs and dengue with warning signs; however, the associations were not statistically significant, and confidence intervals were wide. Genotype frequencies showed no statistically significant deviation from Hardy-Weinberg equilibrium (p = 0.112), and the estimated post hoc statistical power was 11.3%. The TNF-α -308 G>A polymorphism was not significantly associated with dengue severity in this sample. The observed estimates were imprecise and should be considered exploratory, warranting confirmation in larger and more diverse populations.

42939159.titulo: A Marine Bivalve (Entodesma navicula) Extract Suppresses the Replication of Influenza Viruses and Flaviviruses in Association with Reduced MLKL Phosphorylation.
42939159.autores: Moon HJ, Lee G, … Park SI (12 autores)
42939159.revista: Animals : an open access journal from MDPI
42939159.resumo: Emerging influenza viruses and mosquito-borne flaviviruses continue to challenge animal and public health, highlighting the need for antivirals that remain effective after infection. This study evaluated the in vitro activity of a 70% ethanolic whole-specimen extract of the marine bivalve Entodesma navicula (ENE) against influenza A/Puerto Rico/8/1934 (H1N1; A/PR8), A/Wisconsin/15/2009 (H3N2), influenza B/Florida/78/2015, Zika virus, and dengue virus serotype 2. Antiviral activity was assessed using time-of-addition analysis, viability-based cytopathic-effect assays, reverse-transcription quantitative PCR, infectious virus titration, immunofluorescence, Western blotting, and flow cytometry. In the A/PR8 model, pre- and co-treatment produced no consistent inhibition. By contrast, post-infection ENE suppressed all tested viruses. For A/PR8, Zika virus, and dengue virus, this activity was supported by reduced viral genome abundance, infectious progeny, and viral antigen expression. In A/PR8-infected A549 cells, ENE reduced phosphorylation of receptor-interacting serine/threonine-protein kinase 3 (RIPK3) and mixed lineage kinase domain-like pseudokinase (MLKL). ENE also reduced the proportion of cells positive for phosphorylated MLKL within Zika- and dengue-virus-infected Vero E6 populations. These findings identify E. navicula as an underexplored source of post-infection antiviral bioactivity associated with attenuated necroptosis-related signaling. Isolation of active constituents and causal validation in primary cells and animal models are needed.

42931232.titulo: Lethal Viral Sepsis/Septic Shock in Getah Virus-Infected Ifnar1-/- Mice.
42931232.autores: Bishop CR, Tang B, … Suhrbier A (5 autores)
42931232.resumo: Getah virus (GETV) is a mosquito-borne Old World alphavirus that has recently increased its geographic range, particularly in China. GETV causes rheumatic disease in horses, but in recent years its primary impact has been lethal infections in newborn piglets. Herein, we characterize a lethal Ifnar1-/- mouse model of GETV which recapitulates many of the features seen in piglets. These include lethality, high viremia, diarrhoea, and splenomegaly, with histopathological findings aligning with those seen in piglets and indicating severe, acute, multi-organ inflammatory immunopathology. RNA-Seq of spleens from GETV-infected Ifnar1-/- mice and subsequent bioinformatic analyses illustrated a cytokine storm response that included robust type I interferon signatures and a pattern of cytokine/chemokine signatures indicative of viral sepsis/septic shock. Ifnar1-/-mice thus offer a framework and a mouse model for understanding GETV disease in piglets. This model also suggests that viral sepsis/septic shock may be the cause of lethality in GETV-infected piglets.

42936054.titulo: Left to cope alone: how pregnant and postpartum women and their newborns manage extreme heat in coastal Kilifi, Kenya.
42936054.autores: Lusambili A, Scorgie F, … Kovats S (9 autores)
42936054.resumo:
In coastal Kenya, high seasonal temperatures compound structural challenges that include intermittent water access, resulting in health burdens from extreme heat. Women can experience limitations in the coping strategies available to them for protecting their health and wellbeing from high indoor and outdoor temperatures. This paper, drawing on the Climate Heat and Maternal Neonatal Health Africa (CHAMNHA) study, aims to describe how mothers and their newborns in rural Kilifi cope with extreme heat in their daily routines.
This qualitative study draws on key informant interviews, in-depth interviews, and focus group discussions with pregnant and postpartum women (n = 22), mothers-in-law (n = 19), male spouses (n = 20), community health volunteers (n = 22), as well as frontline health providers, policy influencers, and government stakeholders (n = 16). Participants were recruited in Rabai and Kaloleni Counties in Kilifi, on Kenya's coast, during a season characterised by extreme heat and drought. Data were analysed using NVivo 12, applying a combination of inductive and deductive thematic approaches.
Women described five main strategies for coping with extreme heat. These included reducing or removing clothing, seeking outdoor shade and fresh air, ventilating indoor spaces, bathing and drinking cold water, and reducing or rescheduling daily activities. These strategies were also adapted for infant care. Mothers reduced infants' clothing, moved them into shaded outdoor spaces, bathed or sponged them more frequently, and used culturally familiar remedies to manage heat-related discomfort and rashes. These practices provided immediate but partial relief. Heat-retaining and poorly ventilated housing, unreliable electricity, water scarcity and contamination, and diminishing tree cover limited women's options. Some strategies also introduced additional risks. Sleeping outdoors increased exposure to mosquitoes and personal-safety concerns, while opening windows brought dust into homes. Expectations concerning modesty, women's domestic workloads, and appropriate newborn care further constrained coping and sometimes created tension with older household members. Coping therefore involved continuous trade-offs between short-term thermal relief and social, environmental, and health risks.
Pregnant and postpartum women in rural Kilifi manage extreme heat through individual and household practices shaped by cultural expectations and material constraints. These practices offer only temporary relief, increase caregiving demands and, in some cases, shift rather than reduce risk. Responsibility for adaptation therefore falls largely on women themselves. Protecting maternal and newborn health is likely to require heat-health guidance in routine antenatal and postnatal care, engagement of households and community actors, and investment in reliable water, cooler housing and shade.

42931470.titulo: First Serological Evidence of Exposure to Japanese Encephalitis Virus in Feral Pigs and Sentinel Chickens in Western Australia.
42931470.autores: Potter A, Brockway C, … Williams DT (19 autores)
42931470.resumo: Japanese encephalitis virus (JEV) emerged across mainland Australia in 2022, causing substantial impacts on public health and the pig industry. Its emergence raised concerns regarding potential spread into Western Australia (WA). This study aimed to determine JEV activity in WA with a focus on the Kimberley region between 2022 and 2024. It also examined potential pathways of JEV introduction into the state and the challenges associated with flavivirus serology. An integrated surveillance program comprising targeted feral pig surveillance and sentinel chicken monitoring was implemented across northern WA. Sera were screened using flavivirus ELISAs and confirmatory plaque reduction neutralisation tests (PRNT), while feral pig tonsils were tested by RT-qPCR. Evidence of JEV activity was detected in WA between 2022 and 2024. Serological findings from two feral pigs sampled in October 2022 provided the earliest indication of JEV transmission in the Kimberley region. Sentinel chicken surveillance subsequently identified JEV activity in Kununurra, Wyndham, Halls Creek and Newman during 2023 and Derby in 2024. These results provide the first published evidence of JEV activity in WA and highlight the importance of ongoing surveillance, vaccination, mosquito control and preparedness activities in northern Australia.

42930329.titulo: Chikungunya Awareness and Related Knowledge, Attitudes, and Practices Among Nursing Students at the University of Palermo, Italy: A Cross-Sectional Study of Associated Sociodemographic Factors.
42930329.autores: Santangelo OE, Provenzano S, … Terranova A (10 autores)
42930329.resumo:
Chikungunya is an emerging mosquito-borne viral disease that has become a growing public health concern worldwide. Despite documented autochthonous outbreaks in Italy and the increasing spread of Aedes albopictus mosquitoes across Europe, little is known about awareness of chikungunya among future healthcare professionals. This study aimed to assess awareness of chikungunya and evaluate related knowledge, attitudes, and practices (KAPs) among nursing students at the University of Palermo, Italy.
A cross-sectional study was conducted in May 2026 among undergraduate nursing students enrolled at the University of Palermo. Data were collected through an anonymous self-administered online questionnaire investigating sociodemographic characteristics, awareness of chikungunya, sources of information, and KAP related to the disease. Associations between awareness and participant characteristics were assessed using chi-square tests and prevalence ratio analyses.
A total of 894 students participated (mean age: 22.33 ± 4.53 years; 72.3% female). Overall, only 22 students (2.46%) reported having previously heard of chikungunya. In a multivariable exploratory analysis, third-year students had a higher prevalence of previous awareness compared with first-year students (PR = 3.38; 95% CI: 1.10-10.36), whereas no statistically significant association was observed for age (PR = 1.07; 95% CI: 1.00-1.15). Mass media represented the main source of information (63.6%), followed by university lectures (22.7%). Among participants who reported previous awareness, responses suggested relatively good recognition of major clinical manifestations, although important gaps were observed regarding vector recognition and transmission pathways. Attitudes toward prevention were predominantly positive, and most participants reported adopting recommended mosquito-control practices.
Awareness of chikungunya among nursing students was extremely low. Strengthening educational interventions on emerging vector-borne diseases within nursing curricula may improve preparedness, risk communication, and future public health responses.

42944030.titulo: Analyzing Bunyaviruses from a One Health Perspective.
42944030.resumo: Zoonotic viral diseases continue to pose major challenges to global health, particularly as environmental, social and economic changes increasingly influence interactions among humans, animals, vectors, and ecosystems. This review explores Rift Valley fever virus (RVFV), Crimean-Congo hemorrhagic fever virus (CCHFV), and hantaviruses (HTVs) within the framework of One Health, emphasizing the ecological and epidemiological factors that govern their emergence and transmission. Despite their distinct transmission cycles, these viruses share important determinants of zoonotic risk. RVFV is primarily maintained through interactions between mosquitoes, livestock, wildlife, and humans; CCHFV is sustained within complex tick-vertebrate systems involving Hyalomma ticks, domestic animals, and wildlife, while HTVs are predominantly maintained through persistent infections in mammalian reservoir hosts, particularly rodents. Climate variability, habitat alteration, agricultural expansion, livestock movement, urbanization, and other anthropogenic pressures can modify these transmission systems and create new opportunities for pathogen spillover. Effective prevention and control therefore require integrated surveillance that encompasses human disease, animal populations, vectors or wildlife reservoirs, and environmental conditions. Advances in molecular diagnostics, genomic epidemiology, ecological modeling, remote sensing, and climate-based forecasting provide valuable opportunities for improving early detection and outbreak preparedness. To reduce the burden of these zoonotic viral diseases, a sustained collaboration among human and veterinary health professionals, ecologists, entomologists, environmental scientists, and public health authorities is required. Therefore, a coordinated One Health approach is essential for anticipating emerging threats, strengthening preparedness, and protecting human, animal, and ecosystem health.

42944029.titulo: Virome Diversity and Host-Associated Heterogeneity in Mosquitoes and Biting Midges Across Yunnan, China.
42944029.autores: Su H, Zhao K, … Chen S (7 autores)
42944029.resumo: Mosquitoes and biting midges harbor diverse viruses, but the factors shaping their viromes remain incompletely understood. We analyzed 35 pooled libraries from seven host groups across 15 locations in Yunnan, China, sampled in June 2025, using total-RNA sequencing, viral annotation, phylogenetics, and community analyses. We retained 1295 viral contigs grouped into 221 annotation-defined viral taxonomic units (VTUs) spanning 24 families; 107 VTUs were supported only by protein homology. Banna virus-related sequences, an Aedes-associated flavivirus, and four putative components of a divergent Jingmenvirus-related candidate were identified. Host group was associated with family-level virome composition after adjustment for location and sequencing depth (R2 = 0.213, p = 0.0052), and the association persisted across alternative feature definitions. Culex tritaeniorhynchus showed the greatest cumulative VTU richness, although its ranking changed when library number was equalized. Most VTUs detected in this host occurred at one sampled site, without a significant monotonic distance-decay pattern. This study expands knowledge of mosquito-associated and biting midge-associated viral diversity in Yunnan, identifies representative lineages for further characterization, and documents host-associated differences in the detected viromes.

42944005.titulo: Zika virus Pathogenesis and Targeted Intervention Strategies.
42944005.autores: Suo L, Fan H, … Lin X (8 autores)
42944005.resumo: Zika virus (ZIKV), a mosquito-borne member of the Flaviviridae family, is primarily transmitted via the bite of Aedes aegypti mosquitoes but can also be spread through sexual contact and vertical transmission. Infection with ZIKV causes Zika fever and Guillain-Barré syndrome (GBS); more importantly, maternal infection during pregnancy can result in severe neurodevelopmental disorders, such as fetal microcephaly. Although the World Health Organization declared the Zika outbreak a Public Health Emergency of International Concern (PHEIC) in 2016, and extensive research has since been conducted, no approved vaccines or therapeutic drugs are currently available. Recent studies have shown that various ZIKV-encoded proteins participate in host-barrier breaching, regulation of tissue tropism, interference with neurodevelopment, mediation of neurotoxicity, and evasion of type I interferon (IFN-I) immune responses, thereby advancing the development of vaccines and antiviral drugs targeting viral proteins. However, the complete mechanisms by which viral proteins synergistically mediate pathogenesis, the clinical significance of antibody-dependent enhancement (ADE) and its prevention and control strategies, and the practical barriers to clinical translation of protein-targeted interventions have not been systematically elucidated. This review is structured around viral proteins as a central framework: it summarizes the molecular mechanisms by which multiple ZIKV proteins synergistically regulate pathogenic processes; reviews the current research basis and response strategies for flavivirus ADE, and outlines unresolved scientific questions; and discusses progress in vaccines and antiviral drugs targeting viral proteins, with emphasis on evidence gaps and clinical translation barriers. By integrating existing findings and unresolved scientific questions, this review provides a research-gap-oriented theoretical reference for basic ZIKV research and clinical translation of prevention and control strategies.

42940923.titulo: Seasonal Dynamics, Botanical Origin, and Yield of Apis mellifera Propolis in the Mexican Altiplano: Influence of Precipitation, Phenology, and Harvesting Methods.
42940923.autores: Alcivar-Saldaña JJ, Rodriguez-Monroy MA, … Canales-Martinez MM (7 autores)
42940923.resumo: Propolis yield and composition fluctuate with environmental factors and hive management. In a two-year longitudinal study (2022-2024), we evaluated the seasonal dynamics of propolis production across two apiaries in the Mexican Altiplano during the dry and rainy seasons. We conducted monthly harvesting using three collector types: black polyurethane collectors (G1), beige polyurethane collectors (G2), and flexible polyethylene mosquito mesh (G3), distributed among 24 standardized Apis mellifera colonies (n = 8 per treatment; 576 repeated monthly harvests). Palynological analysis identified 39 species belonging to 38 genera and 23 families, with a clear predominance of herbaceous and ruderal forms (Brassica rapa as the main pollen type). The overall mean yield was 9.02 ± 0.58 g/colony/month. Linear mixed-effects models (LMMs) revealed significant temporal variation by month (F11,231 = 28.45, p < 0.001) and season (F1,21 = 14.12, p = 0.001). Propolis biomass showed a clear bimodal pattern, peaking in April (20.25 g/colony) during vegetative bud burst, dropping in July (6.25 g/colony), and rebounding in September-October (9.77-9.92 g/colony), coinciding with leaf senescence and pre-winter nest sealing. Monthly production showed a moderate negative linear correlation with cumulative precipitation (r = -0.422, p = 0.040, R2 = 0.178). Conversely, collector design did not result in statistically significant differences in harvested biomass (G1: 6.88 g, G2: 8.98 g, G3: 11.21 g; F2,21 = 2.14, p = 0.142). These findings demonstrate that propolis collection in the Mexican Altiplano is primarily synchronized with regional plant phenology and constrained by precipitation regimes rather than collector design. Consequently, the practical selection of harvesting devices should be guided by operational handling efficiency, economic cost, and raw product cleanliness, rather than expectations of higher quantitative yield.

42937076.titulo: α-Glucosidase and Acetylcholinesterase (AChE) Inhibitory Activities, Larvicidal Potential and GC-MS Analysis of Endlicheria paniculata: A Combined Experimental and Molecular Docking Study.
42937076.autores: Araujo JP, Silva LED, … Miguel OG (14 autores)
42937076.resumo: Essential oils from Endlicheria paniculata tissues were characterized by GC-MS, revealing a high concentration of sesquiterpenes. Major constituents were amorpha-4,9-dien-2-ol (41.12%) in leaves, β -muurola-4,10(14)-dien-1-ol (43.54%) in wood, and spathulenol (18.56%) in bark. In preliminary single-concentration screening assays, the leaf oil demonstrated preliminary in vitro inhibitory potential against α -glucosidase (98.44%) and acetylcholinesterase (AChE) (97.71%), alongside moderate larvicidal activity against Aedes aegypti (  LC 50 = 61.56  μ g · mL - 1    ). Molecular docking simulations complemented these preliminary biological findings, showing that major leaf constituents, particularly amorpha-4,9-dien-2-ol and selina-3,7(11)-diene, exhibited favorable predicted binding interactions toward Ae. aegypti AChE-1, driven primarily by hydrophobic interactions. Overall, these findings provide theoretical insights and support further investigation of E. paniculata volatiles as potential candidates for vector control research and detailed bio-guided enzyme inhibition studies.

42931465.titulo: First Record of the Mosquito Aedes koreicus (Diptera: Culicidae) in Croatia.
42931465.autores: Vignjević G, Grego B, … Merdić E (6 autores)
42931465.resumo: Aedes koreicus, the Korean bush mosquito, has emerged as a significant invasive threat across Europe since its initial detection in Belgium in 2008. Native to East Asia, this cold-tolerant, container-breeding species has established populations in more than a dozen European countries. During entomological field sampling in the Buzet area (Istria, Croatia), two used-tire depots in the village of Štrped were encountered and identified as potentially suitable breeding habitats for container-breeding mosquitoes. Following the initial detection of these mosquitoes' larvae, the locality was revisited four times from March to May 2026. Dippers of different sizes were used to sample larvae in the tires. Of the 132 larvae collected, eight species were morphologically identified. Nineteen specimens were identified as Ae. koreicus and were detected during each visit. The identification of Ae. koreicus was confirmed by molecular analysis. Sequencing and analysis of cytochrome c oxidase I showed high similarity among Ae. koreicus populations across Europe. This finding confirms the presence of Ae. koreicus in Croatia, which could potentially lead to further establishment, and highlights the need for continued surveillance of invasive mosquito species.

42931171.titulo: Toward an Integrated Response to Arboviral Threats in the Americas: Perspectives from the Dengue Summit of the Global Health Conference of the Americas 2025.
42931171.autores: Espinal C, Becerra-Posada F, … Rodríguez-Morales AJ (19 autores)
42931171.resumo: Dengue remains the most important arboviral disease in the Americas and a growing global public health threat. The region experienced the largest dengue epidemic in recorded history during 2023-2024, with more than 13 million reported cases in 2024 alone, reflecting the combined effects of rapid urbanization, climate variability, population mobility, persistent social inequities, and weakened vector-control programs. This review summarizes and expands on the principal discussions of the First Dengue Summit of the Dengue Initiative of the Americas, held in Cartagena, Colombia, in September 2025. Major themes included the changing epidemiology of dengue; implementation and development of new-generation vaccines, including TAK-003 and Butantan-DV; advances in digital surveillance, outbreak forecasting, and clinical management; and integrated vector-control strategies. Particular attention is given to Wolbachia-mediated population replacement, supported by evidence from a cluster-randomized trial in Indonesia and large-scale quasi-experimental evaluations in Colombia and Brazil, which show substantial and sustained reductions in dengue incidence and hospitalization. In the Aburrá Valley, Colombia, city-wide deployment in Bello, Medellín, and Itagüí was associated with reductions exceeding 90% in notified dengue incidence where Wolbachia became established. The review also examines mathematical modeling, artificial intelligence, climate-informed surveillance, and integrated public health approaches. Persistent challenges include financial sustainability, healthcare inequities, climate change, insecticide resistance, and heterogeneous surveillance and health-system capacity. Coordinated, multisectoral, sustainable strategies that integrate vaccination, vector control, surveillance, community participation, and healthcare strengthening are essential to reduce the dengue burden and improve regional resilience.

42943987.titulo: Evolutionary Dynamics of Rift Valley Fever Virus in Saudi Arabia: Whole-Genome Analysis of the 2000-2001 Outbreak Strains.
42943987.autores: Farrag MA, Aljowaie RM, … Marraiki NAY (6 autores)
42943987.resumo: Rift Valley fever virus (RVFV) is a mosquito-borne zoonotic pathogen that causes severe disease in livestock and humans, with epidemic potential and a capacity for geographic expansion beyond its African endemic range. The 2000-2001 outbreak in Saudi Arabia represented the first confirmed introduction of RVFV outside Africa, yet comprehensive multi-segment genomic characterization of the circulating strains has remained incomplete. Here, we performed an integrated evolutionary and molecular analysis of the three complete-genome Saudi RVFV strains (Saudi 2000-10911, Saudi 200010901, and SA01-1322) using publicly available sequences. Whole-genome comparisons revealed substantial nucleotide and amino acid diversity, with the L segment exhibiting the highest mutation burden (182 nucleotide substitutions, 17 amino acid changes), while the NSs region of the S segment accumulated 52 nucleotide and 11 amino acid mutations compared to the highly conserved nucleocapsid domain. Maximum-likelihood phylogenetic analyses of all three segments consistently placed the Saudi strains within Lineage C (bootstrap = 100/100), clustering with East African strains from Kenya (2006-2007), Tanzania (2007), and South Africa (2008-2010), with congruent topologies across segments confirming the absence of reassortment. Bayesian phylogeographic analysis of 118 L-segment sequences estimated a mean substitution rate of 1.697 × 10-4 substitutions/site/year (95% HPD: 1.5-1.9 × 10-4) and a time to the most recent common ancestor of approximately 1857 (95% HPD: 1835-1876). Selection-pressure analyses using four complementary methods (MEME, FEL, FUBAR, and SLAC) demonstrated pervasive purifying selection across all three segments, with only sporadic episodic positive selection detected at a limited number of codons (six in L, seven in M, and one in S). In silico glycosylation prediction identified conserved N- and O-glycosylation sites on the M segment, with the Saudi strains displaying a Lineage C-typical profile lacking geographically restricted markers. However, the absence of canonical signal peptides in all sequences warrants cautious interpretation of these predictions. Collectively, our findings are consistent with a single introduction of Lineage C RVFV from East Africa among the sampled strains, with no subsequent reassortment, and that the virus has evolved under strong functional constraints with only rare, lineage-restricted episodes of positive selection. The identified Saudi-specific and lineage-defining mutations provide molecular markers for surveillance, while the high conservation of core proteins supports the feasibility of broadly protective vaccines.

42931168.titulo: Babesia divergens IgG Antibodies and ABO Blood Types in Humans.
42931168.autores: Hirsch IA, Svensson J, … Persson KEM (6 autores)
42931168.resumo: Babesia is an intraerythrocytic parasite transmitted by ticks or through blood transfusion, and it can cause babesiosis with symptoms such as fever, anemia, and organ failure. The parasite is closely related to the mosquito-borne Plasmodium falciparum, which causes malaria. Several studies have shown that individuals with blood group O have a reduced risk of severe malaria compared to individuals with other ABO blood groups. Whether or not this is also the case for babesiosis has not yet been clearly investigated. In this study, serum samples from over 650 individuals were analyzed using an ELISA assay to detect antibodies against Babesia divergens. The ABO blood groups of the same samples were determined using a conventional method. There was no difference in B. divergens IgG antibody levels between the different ABO blood groups, nor was there any difference in the percentage of positive reactions in the ELISA against B. divergens between the different blood groups. This could indicate that the development and maintenance of B. divergens antibodies are not influenced by ABO blood groups.

42934750.titulo: Deep learning convolutional neural networks for morphological identification of field-caught Anopheles stephensi in Ethiopia, using smartphone images of specimens.
42934750.autores: Mehta P, Kumar AS, … Acharya S (16 autores)
42934750.resumo:
Anopheles stephensi, an invasive malaria vector historically confined to South Asia and the Arabian Peninsula, has established reproducing populations across the Horn of Africa and continues to expand its range. Its adaptability to a range of environments, with its impact described most prominently in urban and peri-urban settings, and morphological similarity to native African anophelines, particularly An. gambiae s.l., makes reliable field identification difficult by field entomologists across much of Africa who have had limited prior exposure to the species. Existing molecular methods are impractical for routine field use, creating an urgent need for scalable, accessible identification tools to support surveillance programs responding to this emerging threat.
Three deep learning convolutional neural network (CNN) classifiers were developed and validated for detecting An. stephensi from photographic images of mosquito specimens collected from sentinel sites across Ethiopia and Uganda, verified for species identity by PCR or morphological identification. VectorCam, a standardized field imaging device, served as the primary imaging platform, with a supplementary handheld smartphone dataset collected using clip-on macro lenses (10X and 15X). An EfficientNet-B1 architecture was fine-tuned using transfer learning from a pretraining dataset of over 60,000 labeled photographs of field-collected mosquito specimens from Uganda. Three classifiers were developed: a VectorCam multiclass classifier distinguishing seven species classes including An. stephensi, a VectorCam binary classifier distinguishing An. stephensi from all other species, and a handheld smartphone binary classifier for photographic images taken using a handheld smartphone. All models were evaluated using 5-fold cross-validation and a majority voting ensemble of the trained classifiers.
Against PCR and morphologically verified ground-truth identifications, the VectorCam multiclass classifier achieved an An. stephensi sensitivity of 98.74% and overall accuracy of 96.02%. The VectorCam binary classifier achieved an An. stephensi sensitivity of 97.48% and a specificity of 99.25%. The handheld binary classifier achieved an An. stephensi sensitivity of 91.09% and a specificity of 84.40%. Gradient-weighted Class Activation Mapping confirmed that classification decisions were driven by wing venation and leg morphology, consistent with established entomological identification criteria.
Deep learning image classification using VectorCam achieves high accuracy for field detection of An. stephensi, with the binary classifier demonstrating performance suitable for operational vector surveillance, providing a practical, scalable solution for decentralized An. stephensi surveillance across malaria-endemic regions of Africa, reducing reliance on molecular verification or specialist taxonomic training for field-level species identification.

42949658.titulo: First record of Culex (Culex) acharistus Root, 1927 (Diptera: Culicidae) in Bolivia: morphological and molecular confirmation across contrasting Andean environments.
42949658.autores: Lardeux F, Boussès P, … Torrez L (7 autores)
42949658.resumo: This study reports the first record of Culex (Culex) acharistus Root, 1927 in Bolivia, based on an integrative approach combining larval morphology and molecular identification using a fragment of the mitochondrial cytochrome c oxidase subunit I (COI) gene. Specimens were collected from 4 localities representing contrasting environmental settings: La Paz (urban environment, approximately 3,600 m a.s.l.), El Alto (urban environment, approximately 4,000 m a.s.l.), Cochabamba (urban and peri-urban environments, approximately 2,600 m a.s.l.), and Licoma, a rural locality in the Yungas region (approximately 1,900 m a.s.l.). Fourth-instar larvae were morphologically examined using diagnostic characters and preserved for molecular analyses. The 6 analyzed specimens shared an identical COI haplotype, showing more than 99% sequence identity with available Cx. acharistus sequences in GenBank. Maximum likelihood phylogenetic analysis placed the Bolivian haplotype within the Cx. acharistus clade. These results provide morphological and molecular evidence for the occurrence of Cx. acharistus in Bolivia, extend its known distribution in South America, and document the species at its highest elevation reported to date, at approximately 4,000 m a.s.l. in El Alto. This study highlights the value of integrating morphological and molecular approaches for reliable identification of Neotropical Culex species.

42946829.titulo: Correction: Toward comfortable mosquito-proof clothing: repellent- and insecticide-free fabrics that block bites across three disease-transmitting mosquito genera.

42946639.titulo: Molecular and functional characterization of a typical 2-Cys peroxiredoxin and its developmental and pyriproxyfen-responsive expression in Aedes albopictus (Diptera: Culicidae).
42946639.autores: Arslanhan BA, Diop SD, … Yildirim A (8 autores)
42946639.resumo: The Asian tiger mosquito, Aedes albopictus (Skuse, 1894) (Diptera: Culicidae), is established and expanding across the Black Sea region, but the redox processes associated with its development and response to insect growth regulators remain poorly understood. We characterized a typical 2-Cys peroxiredoxin (Prx2) by examining intraspecific sequence variation, conserved protein features, enzymatic activity, developmental transcription, and transcription following exposure to 0.06 ppb pyriproxyfen. The coding region was polymorphic among Turkish isolates, but all substitutions were synonymous, and the deduced amino acid sequence was conserved. Catalytic cysteines and hallmark motifs supported classification as a typical 2-Cys peroxiredoxin. Recombinant His-tagged Prx2 migrated at the expected molecular size and removed hydrogen peroxide in a concentration- and thiol-dependent manner. Basal transcript abundance varied across development, reaching its lowest level in pupae and higher levels in adults. Exposure to 0.06 ppb pyriproxyfen was associated with increased Prx2 transcript abundance in L3 and L4 larvae, whereas no statistically detectable treatment-related difference was observed among the surviving pupae or adults at the sampled time points. Together, these findings identify Prx2 as a conserved, functional thiol peroxidase and demonstrate a pyriproxyfen-associated larval transcriptional response under the conditions tested. Because this concentration was not independently validated as sublethal in the present colony and later-stage sampling necessarily comprised survivors of the original exposure, the data do not distinguish developmental attenuation of the response from survivor selection.

42949985.titulo: Global stability analysis of within-host Zika virus-chikungunya virus co-infection with CTL immune responses.
42949985.autores: Elaiw AM, Alkhudhari ZY, … Hobiny AD (4 autores)
42949985.resumo: We formulate and analyse a mathematical model for the within-host co-infection dynamics of Zika virus (ZIKV) and chikungunya virus (CHIKV), incorporating latently infected cells and cytotoxic T lymphocyte (CTL) immune responses. We establish the nonnegativity and boundedness of solutions. Using the next-generation matrix method, we derive the basic reproduction numbers (RZL) and (RCL) for the ZIKV and CHIKV submodels, respectively, and the overall reproduction number (R0L=max{RZL,RCL}). Invasion reproduction numbers, (RZL,inv) and (RCL,inv), are derived to characterise the ability of either virus to invade an established infection. Global stability of the equilibria is established using Lyapunov functions. We investigate three therapeutic protocols: antiviral treatment blocking viral entry, treatment reducing viral production, and IL-2 therapy enhancing CTL responses. Sensitivity analysis of (RZL) and (RCL) is performed, and numerical simulations support the stability results. Simulations indicate that combined antiviral and immune-based interventions suppress co-infection by reducing viral replication and enhancing immune-mediated clearance.

42936464.titulo: Concurrent varicella and dengue infection in an adolescent female: diagnostic and clinical challenges in an endemic setting.
42936464.autores: Gabot JKS, Sengson RFR, … Han SM (4 autores)
42936464.resumo:
Varicella-zoster virus (VZV) infection and dengue virus infection are common viral illnesses in tropical regions. However, concurrent infections are rarely reported and may present significant diagnostic challenges because of overlapping clinical manifestations, including fever, rash, and hematologic abnormalities.
We report a laboratory-confirmed co-infection with VZV and dengue virus in a previously healthy 17-year-old female patient from Quezon City, Philippines. She initially presented with a 3-day history of fever and a generalized pruritic vesicular rash and was treated for varicella with oral acyclovir.
