Despite antiviral therapy, persistent high-grade fever, epigastric abdominal pain, leukopenia (2.8 × 10⁹/l), and thrombocytopenia (85 × 10⁹/l) prompted further investigation on the fourth day of illness. Diagnostic testing confirmed acute dengue infection by positive nonstructural protein 1 antigen and dengue immunoglobulin M test results, while VZV polymerase chain reaction testing of vesicular fluid confirmed varicella. The patient received supportive dengue management alongside continued acyclovir therapy. Clinical symptoms improved, with resolution of fever by the sixth day of illness, normalization of hematologic parameters, and progressive crusting of lesions. She was discharged without complications.
This case highlights the importance of considering dengue co-infection in patients with apparent varicella who develop persistent fever, abdominal pain, leukopenia, or thrombocytopenia in dengue-endemic settings. Early laboratory confirmation is essential to distinguish overlapping clinical features, guide appropriate management, and prevent missed or delayed diagnoses.

42932652.titulo: circEPSTI1 regulates miR-942-5p-SERPINE1-AKT1 signaling axis to enhance dengue infection and is suppressed by Tiplaxtinin.
42932652.autores: Das N, Krishnamoorthy P, … Kumar H (11 autores)
42932652.revista: Proceedings of the National Academy of Sciences of the United States of America
42932652.resumo: Circular RNAs (circRNAs) have recently been identified as crucial regulators of gene expression in various diseases. Their role in dengue remains unexplored. In this study, circEPSTI1 induction was observed in peripheral blood mononuclear cells and plasma of dengue patients. The induction of circEPSTI1 is interferon-dependent and enhances DENV infection by sponging the expression of miR-942-5p. The antiviral role of miR-942-5p is mediated by bidirectional inhibition through targeting conserved genomic sequences of the DENV genome of different subtypes across NS1, NS3, and NS5 and the host AKT1 signaling pathway. RNA-seq analysis of DENV-infected circEPSTI1 knockdown A549 cells identified SERPINE1 and AKT1 signaling pathways to be dysregulated significantly. circEPSTI1 relieves the inhibition of miR-942-5p over DENV genomic RNA and the host SERPINE1 to activate AKT1 signaling. The activation of AKT1 signaling facilitates cell survival and enhances DENV replication. The expression of SERPINE1 and circEPSTI1 was upregulated in Dengue patients, and pharmaceutical inhibition of SERPINE1 through Tiplaxtinin inhibits the DENV replication by reducing the expression of circEPSTI1. Overall, our result demonstrates the therapeutic potential of Tiplaxtinin by targeting the circEPSTI1-miR-942-5p-SERPINE1-AKT1 axis in dengue treatment.

42950018.titulo: Dengue virus controlled human challenge reveals that preexisting immunity shapes viral replication and broadly protective responses.
42950018.autores: Odio CD, Aogo RA, … Katzelnick LC (27 autores)
42950018.resumo: Dengue is the canonical viral disease for which immune history is a determinant of protective versus pathogenic responses and immunogenicity. Yet, because of limitations in animal models and clinical presentation after peak viremia, how preinfection and early immune responses affect dengue outcome is not confirmed. We conducted a phase 1 clinical trial with 45 healthy adults to test whether secondary infection challenge with a heterotypic, full-length, attenuated virus increases viremia and immunogenicity compared with primary and tertiary infection. Viremia was associated with more, but still mild, clinical signs and symptoms, and secondary infection resulted in greater viremia, neutralizing antibodies, and protective T cell responses. However, those whose baseline antibodies most efficiently increased dengue virus replication in an in vitro assay experienced delayed inflammatory and adaptive immune activation, the highest viremia, strong acute immune responses, and waning of potent CD8+ T cells and antibodies. In contrast, higher baseline antibodies against the nonstructural protein 1 of multiple serotypes predicted early interferon and balanced immune activation, viremia control, and development of enduring, potent B and T cells, revealing how vaccines can induce broad, long-lasting protection. Last, individuals with potent and neutralizing antibodies and IFN-γ+ T cells at baseline experienced minimal viral replication. Together, these findings demonstrate that controlled human challenge with dengue virus can delineate coordinated versus dysregulated acute immune responses and their effects on immunogenicity, informing therapeutic and vaccine strategies for dengue and other viral diseases.

42947633.titulo: A Live Attenuated Dengue Virus Vaccine (Dengvaxia) is Suppressed in Individuals with Immunity to Serotype 4.
42947633.autores: Adams C, Hein LD, … de Silva AM (12 autores)
42947633.resumo:
Dengvaxia® was the first live attenuated tetravalent dengue virus (DENV) vaccine to be tested and approved for use in people. While Dengvaxia was designed to be tetravalent, in humans, the vaccine performed like a monovalent DENV4 vaccine because the DENV4 vaccine virus replicated better than other vaccine serotypes. Dengvaxia® was safe and efficacious in children who were DENV-immune at baseline and contraindicated for use in DENV-naïve children.
When Dengvaxia® was rolled out as a pediatric vaccine in the Philippines in 2016, we established a prospective cohort to assess vaccine performance by baseline dengue serostatus. Here we report on how baseline monotypic immunity to each serotype (reflecting one past DENV infection) impacted Dengvaxia® responses.
We observed that in children with baseline immunity to DENV1, 2 or 3, the vaccine stimulated a secondary serotype cross-neutralizing Ab response, which likely explains the overall favorable performance of the vaccine in seropositive children enrolled in phase 3 trials. We observed a high frequency (61%) of vaccine suppression among DENV4 monotypic immune children.
Our results confirm the replication dominance of the DENV4 vaccine component in Dengvaxia® and directly implicate pre-existing DENV4 immunity in the suppression of the vaccine. Our results have broader implications for evaluating the performance of other DENV vaccines in seropositive individuals.

42929563.titulo: Structure-Guided Design of a Subnanomolar Dengue Virus NS4B Inhibitor.
42929563.autores: Laorsatiankul P, Baig MH, … Haider S (10 autores)
42929563.revista: Journal of chemical information and modeling
42929563.resumo: Dengue virus nonstructural protein 4B (NS4B) is an essential regulator of viral replication but remains structurally unresolved, limiting drug discovery. Here, we combine modeling, ligand-based design, and experimental validation to enable structure-guided inhibition of NS4B. Comparative models across all four serotypes reveal a conserved transmembrane binding pocket consistent with resistance mutations. Docking of JNJ-series inhibitors defines key interaction features that guide the development of predictive field-based 3D-QSAR models (R = 0.91, Q = 0.89). Prospective screening of bioisosteric and in-house compounds identifies BNJ-495 as a candidate broad-spectrum inhibitor with predicted activity across all four dengue serotypes. Experimental validation confirms potent activity against dengue virus serotype 2 (IC50 = 0.17 nM) with a high selectivity index (∼37,000). Conserved binding interactions across serotypes support broad-spectrum potential. This study establishes a general framework for targeting structurally elusive viral membrane proteins.

42929545.titulo: Synergistic Effects of pH and Temperature on Dengue Virus Envelope Dimers: Insights from Microsecond Molecular Dynamics Simulations.
42929545.autores: Ropón-Palacios G, Crespi LGF, … de Araujo AS (5 autores)
42929545.revista: Journal of chemical information and modeling
42929545.resumo: Dengue pathogenesis depends on a conformational rearrangement of the envelope glycoprotein (pE) induced by low pH. However, how pH and temperature cooperate to destabilize the dimeric form of the pE, a fundamental step that enables the formation of the fusion-active trimer, remains unclear. Here, we investigate this synergy for Dengue serotypes of greatest medical relevance, DENV-2 and DENV-3. All-atom molecular dynamics simulations were performed on the microsecond scale, at 28 °C, 37 °C, and 40 °C under pH 5, 6, and 7 using CHARMM36m force fields and complemented by extended coarse-grained molecular dynamics simulations for the DENV-2 system at 37 °C and pH 5, and for the DENV-3 system at 28 °C and pH 5, and at 37 °C and pH 7. Our simulations suggest that increasing the temperature from 28 to 37 °C tends to expand the conformational space at neutral pH, potentially weakening dimer integrity through modulation of the interfacial interaction network. Acidification appears to amplify this effect in a serotype-specific manner: in our simulations DENV-2 required pH 5, while DENV-3 responded at pH 6. Additionally, distance and principal component analyses revealed an asymmetric dissociation pathway, termed the "compensatory embrace", observed in both all-atom and coarse-grained models. Structural analyses further highlighted the differences in histidine distribution between the serotypes. Moreover, interaction mapping at 37 °C identified candidate interfacial contacts that may act as pH-sensitive latches, maintaining stability at pH 7 but breaking upon acidification. Collectively, these results suggest a potential hierarchy of physicochemical triggers that may contribute to the conversion of dimer into fusion-competent monomers. These interfacial hotspots and the "compensatory embrace" constitute structurally informed targets that, pending validation under native virion conditions, may guide the rational design of antivirals and immunogens, underscoring the value of long-time scale molecular dynamics simulations as a hypothesis-generating tool in drug discovery.

42929539.titulo: Dengue virus-2 triggers Epstein-Barr virus replication in primary B cells by co-opting the IRE1-XBP1 signaling axis.
42929539.autores: Deng X, Deng R, … Xu P (10 autores)
42929539.resumo: The intricate interplay between co-infecting viral pathogens within a host can significantly influence disease outcomes. Dengue virus (DENV), a globally prevalent arbovirus from the Flaviviridae family, and Epstein-Barr virus (EBV), a ubiquitous human herpesvirus, share extensive geographical overlap, yet their potential interactions remain largely uncharacterized. This study elucidates a novel molecular mechanism whereby DENV-2 infection triggers disruption of EBV latency. We systematically demonstrate that DENV-2 infection consistently induces EBV lytic gene expression and viral replication in diverse cellular contexts, including epithelial cell lines and, critically, in primary human B lymphocytes-the principal reservoir of latent EBV. Mechanistically, we establish that the substantial burden of DENV-2 protein synthesis and replication induces profound endoplasmic reticulum (ER) stress, activating the unfolded protein response (UPR). Through pharmacological inhibition and genetic knockdown, we dissect the three UPR branches and identify the IRE1-XBP1 signaling axis as the indispensable pathway for this phenomenon. DENV-2 infection promotes the endoribonuclease activity of IRE1, leading to the unconventional splicing of XBP1 mRNA into its transcriptionally active isoform, XBP1s. Depletion of IRE1 or XBP1 attenuated DENV-induced BZLF1 expression, whereas ectopic XBP1s expression increased BZLF1 transcription. Our findings delineate a precise virus-host-virus signaling model in which an acute RNA virus engages a cellular stress pathway to promote entry into the EBV lytic program and viral genome amplification. This provides a new paradigm for understanding the pathobiology of dengue fever and the complex dynamics of the human virome.IMPORTANCEThis research uncovers a previously unrecognized molecular dialog between two of the world's most common viral pathogens. By demonstrating that dengue virus infection can awaken dormant Epstein-Barr virus, this study provides a mechanistic basis for the long-suspected but poorly understood complications arising from viral co-infections. We pinpoint a specific cellular stress pathway, the IRE1-XBP1 axis of the unfolded protein response (UPR), as the critical molecular switch. This discovery is significant because it not only explains how an acute viral illness can trigger the reactivation of a latent, potentially oncogenic virus but also opens new avenues for therapeutic intervention. Understanding this intricate interplay could lead to novel strategies for managing severe dengue and other diseases where viral co-infection is a contributing factor to pathogenesis.

42946742.titulo: mRNA-1273 SARS-CoV-2 vaccination in people with HIV: an immune correlates analysis of CD4 + T cell responses in the multicenter CoVPN 3008 observational study.
42946742.autores: Khuzwayo S, Zhang B, … Andersen-Nissen E (93 autores)
42946742.resumo: T cell correlates of COVID-19 risk are poorly defined, particularly in people with HIV (PWH). CoVPN 3008 ( NCT05168813 ) Part A was a prospective 14,002-participant cohort study that administered one or two doses of mRNA-1273 COVID-19 vaccine, depending on baseline SARS-CoV-2 serostatus, in participants (83% PWH) in sub-Saharan Africa. Participants self-monitored for prespecified COVID-19 symptoms, defined by Centers for Disease Control and Prevention symptom criteria. Previous work showed that protection from COVID-19 was superior for hybrid versus vaccine-induced immunity, and that neutralizing antibody titers inversely associated with COVID-19 risk. In the present work, we measured T cell responses to Spike and Nucleocapsid at baseline and 4 weeks post last-vaccination (Peak) in a case-cohort study and assessed them as correlates of risk. In Hybrid Group PWH (n = 22 cases), COVID-19 risk over 6 months decreased with increasing Peak Spike BA.4/5-specific CD4 + T cell responses, from 15.8%, 4.7%, and 0% risk at 0.1%, 0.2%, and 0.3% IFN-γ and/or IL-2 response magnitude, respectively. Including baseline Spike-specific neutralizing antibody titer and Peak CD4 + T cell functionality score in the same model increased the association's strength (overall p < 0.001). Thus, CD4 + T cell responses are an independent correlate of COVID-19 risk among PWH with pre-existing SARS-CoV-2 immunity.

42943986.titulo: Protein-Protein Interaction-Guided Peptides Interfere with Early Zika Virus Entry-Associated Events.
42943986.autores: Rodríguez-Salazar CA, Recalde-Reyes DP, … Giraldo MI (5 autores)
42943986.resumo: Zika virus (ZIKV) remains a public health concern because of its association with neurological complications and congenital disease, yet no specific antiviral therapy has been approved. Since the envelope (E) protein mediates viral attachment and early entry-associated membrane events, it represents an attractive antiviral target. Here, we used a protein-protein interaction-guided strategy to design peptides to interfere with predicted interfaces between the ZIKV E protein and cellular receptors involved in attachment. After in silico filtering and preliminary screening, six peptides (PZ1-PZ6) were selected. These peptides showed heterogeneous physicochemical profiles, low cytotoxicity and hemolytic activity under the tested conditions, and docking-predicted interactions with functional E protein regions. In HTR-8/SVneo cells, antiviral activity depended on the timing of exposure, with greater reductions in infectious titers during co-treatment and post-treatment. All peptides also reduced titers in anti-adsorption assays, supporting interference with viral attachment or early entry-associated events. Consistently, DiOC18 fluorescence signals were reduced in a peptide-specific manner, particularly for PZ3 and PZ6. Nuclease protection assays showed no extensive exposure of the viral genome, whereas transmission electron microscopy revealed ultrastructural alterations without generalized particle disruption. Overall, PZ1-PZ6 are promising protein-protein interaction-guided anti-ZIKV peptide candidates with activity against early viral entry-associated events.

42943976.titulo: Antiviral Sesquiterpene Lactones from Laurus nobilis L.: Inhibition of Hepatitis C Virus and Dengue Virus Replication.
42943976.autores: Amen Y, Elsbaey M, … Zoidis G (8 autores)
42943976.resumo: Natural products remain indispensable scaffolds in antiviral drug discovery, particularly against high-burden viral pathogens. In this study, two major sesquiterpene lactones, dehydrocostus lactone (1) and costunolide (2), were isolated from Laurus nobilis L. leaves and evaluated for their antiviral potential against hepatitis C virus (HCV) and dengue virus (DENV). The structures of both compounds were confirmed by HRMS and 1D NMR spectroscopic analyses. In subgenomic replicon assays, the molecules inhibited HCV replication in the low-micromolar range (EC50=2.34 μM for 1 and 2.06 μM for 2) with favorable selectivity indices. In full-length HCV reporter systems, costunolide (2) displayed enhanced anti-HCV potency, reduced viral RNA and NS5A protein levels, and enhanced the suppressive effect of the clinically approved NS5A inhibitor, daclatasvir. Furthermore, costunolide (2) exhibited cross-flaviviridae activity, suppressing DENV replication (EC50=5.89 μM in replicon cells; EC50=1.27 μM post-infection in infectious virus assays), and demonstrated cooperative suppression of viral propagation along with reduced glutathione. Mechanistically, these results highlight the critical role of the sesquiterpene lactone core, and the observed enhanced combined activity between costunolide and reduced glutathione is consistent with a possible contribution of the NRF2/glutathione antioxidant axis to its anti-DENV action. Overall, this study highlights L. nobilis as a previously underexplored source of antiviral sesquiterpene lactones and establishes costunolide (2) as a promising lead against HCV and DENV, warranting further investigation across additional Flaviviridae members.

42931365.titulo: Efficacy, Immunogenicity, Safety, and Evidence Independence of CYD-TDV and TAK-003 Dengue Vaccines in Children and Adolescents: A Systematic Review and Meta-Analysis.
42931365.autores: Sanchez-Guanilo JP, Contreras CA, Arce-Huamani MA
42931365.resumo: Background/Objectives: The efficacy and safety profiles of CYD-TDV and TAK-003 are established, but multiple publications may derive from the same randomized trial population and therefore not represent independent evidence. We evaluated efficacy, immunogenicity, and safety while distinguishing independent trials from overlapping follow-up reports and interpreting absolute effects within each programme. Methods: We conducted a PRISMA 2020 systematic review and meta-analysis of randomized trials and follow-up reports from five databases. Outcomes included virologically confirmed dengue, hospitalization, severe dengue, serotype-specific efficacy, immunogenicity, and safety. Risk ratios (RRs) with 95% confidence intervals (CIs) were calculated; immunogenicity and safety were synthesized narratively. RoB 2 and GRADE were applied. Results: Nine reports were included. CYD-TDV reduced virologically confirmed dengue (RR = 0.41; 95% CI: 0.35-0.48) and hospitalization (RR = 0.41; 95% CI: 0.25-0.67). Across two independent CYD-TDV trials, absolute reductions were 23.2 virologically confirmed dengue cases per 1000 participants (NNV = 44) and 12.0-50.0 hospitalizations per 1000 (NNVs = 84-20). In the primary TIDES report, TAK-003 reduced virologically confirmed dengue (RR = 0.28; 95% CI: 0.22-0.35) and hospitalization (RR = 0.10; 95% CI: 0.05-0.18), with absolute reductions of 23.6 and 12.9 per 1000 (NNVs = 43 and 78). Later TIDES reports extended follow-up of the same population. Conclusions: Both vaccines reduced dengue outcomes within their respective trial programmes. Absolute effects should be interpreted according to baseline risk and trial context, not as direct between-vaccine comparisons. The synthesis distinguishes extended follow-up from independent replication.

42945296.titulo: Factors associated with the optimal uptake of intermittent preventive treatment in pregnancy with sulfadoxine-pyrimethamine: The experiences of postpartum women attending child welfare clinics in three rural districts in the Western Region of Ghana.
42945296.autores: Amugi G, Agudey DT, … Chinbuah S (9 autores)
42945296.resumo:
Intermittent preventive treatment in pregnancy with sulfadoxine-pyrimethamine (IPTp-SP) is a key preventive strategy. However, optimal uptake remains inconsistent despite high antenatal care (ANC) attendance. This study assessed factors associated with optimal IPTp-SP uptake and explored the experiences of postpartum women in rural Ghana.
A convergent parallel mixed-method study was conducted among 1,155 postpartum women attending child welfare clinics in Jomoro, Prestea-Huni Valley and Ellembelle districts of the Western Region of Ghana. Quantitative data were collected using structured questionnaires and analysed using descriptive statistics and chi-square tests. Qualitative data from in-depth interviews and focus group discussions were analysed thematically to explore women's experiences and perceptions.
Among the 1,155 women enrolled, 812 (70.3%) took three or more doses of IPTp-SP (IPTp3-SP). Knowledge of malaria in pregnancy was high, with 92.7% correctly identifying its mode of transmission and 91.7% identifying ways of preventing malaria during pregnancy. Factors independently associated with IPTp3-SP included age 10-19 years compared with 20-29 years (aOR 2.17, 95% CI 1.21-3.88), gravidity of three compared with one (aOR 2.67, 95% CI: 1.58-4.50), and gravidity of four compared with one (aOR 1.83, 95% CI: 1.02-3.28). Lower odds were observed among uninsured women (aOR 0.36, 95% CI: 0.20-0.64), single women (aOR 0.64, 95% CI: 0.42-0.97), and cohabiting women (aOR 0.52, 95% CI: 0.34-0.79). ANC attendance showed a strong association with IPTp3-SP: women attending <4 ANC visits had lower odds of receiving IPTp3-SP than those attending 10 or more visits (aOR 0.08, 95% CI: 0.04-0.15). Nausea, dizziness, weakness, abdominal discomfort, vomiting and difficulty chewing the tablets affected their experiences and, for some women, willingness to continue treatment.
IPTp-SP uptake was relatively high. Predictors of optimal uptake include age, education, marital status, gravidity, health insurance status, and number of ANC visits. Women with fewer ANC visits were less likely to receive three or more doses. Reported side effects posed barriers to adherence. Strengthening ANC attendance and counselling on IPTp-SP expected side effects may improve completion of recommended doses.

42936869.titulo: De novo assembly of complete Plasmodium falciparum isolate genomes using PacBio HiFi sequencing technology.
42936869.autores: Nyarko PB, Quenu M, … Claessens A (11 autores)
42936869.resumo: Plasmodium falciparum possesses a highly structured genome with extensive sequence diversity concentrated in Variant Surface Antigen (VSA) families. These genes-var, rif, and stevor-play key roles in immune evasion and pathogenesis and are difficult to assemble using short-read sequencing technologies. Here, we applied PacBio HiFi long-read sequencing to generate high-quality de novo genome assemblies from 43 P. falciparum parasite cultures originating from community cases in The Gambia. Parasites were culture-adapted, cloned by limiting dilution where possible, and sequenced using high molecular weight DNA extracts. Assemblies from single-genotype lineages were constructed using hifiasm, producing complete chromosomal-length scaffolds with high base accuracy without requiring short-read polishing. We recovered full repertoires of var, rif, and stevor genes and classified them into known subgroups. Together, our results demonstrate that PacBio HiFi sequencing enables accurate assembly of complex P. falciparum genomes from natural infections. This work provides a valuable genomic resource for future studies of parasite evolution, transmission dynamics, and antigenic diversity, and suggests that VSA repertoires can serve as reliable proxies of genetic relatedness across infections.

42931187.titulo: Twenty-Year Trends in Malaria Epidemiology, Importation Dynamics, and Surveillance in Oman: A Retrospective National Surveillance Study.
42931187.autores: Ahmed M, Alharbi B, … Al Kiyumi R (4 autores)
42931187.resumo:
Malaria remains a major vector-borne disease worldwide. Oman interrupted endemic malaria transmission in 2010, but imported infections and occasional locally acquired cases continue to require sustained surveillance. This study evaluated national malaria epidemiology and surveillance patterns across the complete 2005-2024 period.
We conducted a retrospective observational analysis of aggregated malaria surveillance indicators reported by the Oman Ministry of Health and linked national surveillance sources. The analytical series comprised 20 consecutive annual observations (2005-2024). Indicators included Annual Parasite Incidence (API), Slide Positivity Rate (SPR), Annual Blood Examination Rate (ABER), blood slides examined, case origin, surveillance approach, Plasmodium species distribution, and 2024 governorate-level case counts. Descriptive analyses, linear temporal models, robust Poisson rate models, regression diagnostics with Newey-West sensitivity analyses, and a 2024 population-referenced geographic analysis were performed.
Across all 20 years, 17,080 malaria cases were reported; 16,905 (98.98%) were imported, 174 (1.02%) were autochthonous, and one case was unclassified by origin. API declined from 0.217 per 1000 population in 2005 to 0.064 in 2024. ABER and annual blood-slide examination volume declined, whereas SPR increased over time. The temporal slope for blood slides examined was strongly negative (standardized β = -0.907, p < 0.001). The annual testing-volume-SPR association was inverse and statistically significant in the restored 20-year series (B = -0.00000147, 95% CI -0.00000254 to -0.00000040, p = 0.010; R2 = 0.317); the association remained significant with Newey-West lag-1 standard errors (p = 0.019). Among the two principal species, the relative annual rate of P. falciparum increased (aRR = 1.142, 95% CI 1.068-1.221, p < 0.001), whereas that of P. vivax decreased (aRR = 0.952, 95% CI 0.919-0.987, p = 0.007). In 2024, crude reported case rates varied across governorates, but these rates combine imported and locally acquired cases and therefore do not represent local transmission incidence.
Surveillance during 2005-2024 was characterized by persistent predominance of imported malaria, sparse autochthonous cases, changing species composition, and declining testing-volume indicators. The findings support continued diagnostic readiness and surveillance for imported infection and possible re-establishment, without implying effectiveness of any specific intervention.

42931180.titulo: Evolution of Neuroparasitic Infections in the South of Madrid Region, Spain: A Hospital-Based Study.
42931180.autores: Antón-Berenguer V, Ligero-López J, … Rubio Muñoz JM (10 autores)
42931180.resumo: Parasitic infections of the central nervous system (CNS) constitute a diverse group of diseases, many of which the World Health Organization classifies as neglected tropical diseases. This study aimed to analyze trends in diagnosis, clinical profile, and epidemiology of these infections through a retrospective review of cases at a secondary hospital in southern Madrid, Spain, from January 1992 to December 2024. Among the 74 patients diagnosed, 58 (78.4%) had neurotoxoplasmosis (NT), 14 (18.9%) neurocysticercosis (NC), and the remaining two cases were cerebral malaria and disseminated amoebiasis with CNS involvement. Diagnosis primarily relied on neuroimaging, which suggested differences in parasite locations within the CNS. All NT patients were HIV-associated immunocompromised, whereas all NC patients were immunocompetent. NT incidence has declined substantially since the late 20th century, following the introduction of highly active antiretroviral therapy, which has also reduced recurrences and mortality. Conversely, NC shifted from a locally endemic disease to an imported one, with all cases diagnosed after 2001 involving patients from Latin America, reflecting both the success of Taenia solium control measures in Spain and the impact of migration. These findings underscore the importance of epidemiological surveillance and control strategies tailored to at-risk populations and the demographic shifts associated with migration.

42942752.titulo: Synthesis, Characterization and Structural Elucidation of Biocompatible Hydroxychloroquine-Zinc Oxide Hybrid Nanoclusters as Synergistic Antiplasmodial Agents.
42942752.autores: Rani S, Kumar B, … Manuja A (4 autores)
42942752.resumo: Background: The increasing emergence of antimalarial drug resistance and safety concerns associated with conventional therapies necessitates the development of improved compounds. In this study, we report the synthesis of hydroxychloroquine-zinc oxide hybrid nanoclusters (HCQ-ZnONPs) by integrating a bioactive organic ligand (hydroxychloroquine) with a bioactive metal oxide nanocluster (ZnONPs). Methods: Structural and physicochemical characterization was performed using proton nuclear magnetic resonance (1H NMR), fourier-transform infrared spectroscopy (FT-IR), mass spectrometry, X-ray diffraction (XRD), transmission electron microscopy (TEM), field emission scanning electron microscopy (FE-SEM), energy-dispersive X-ray analysis (EDAX), dynamic light scattering (DLS), and zeta potential. Molecular docking against Plasmodium falciparum dihydrofolate reductase-thymidylate synthase (PfDHFR-TS) was performed to investigate potential ligand-target interactions. Drug loading and HCQ release were evaluated at pH 7.4. We also assessed in vitro cytocompatibility, nitric oxide estimation, total antioxidant capacity, anti-inflammatory and antimalarial activities. Results: The physicochemical characterization supported the successful formation of HCQ-ZnONPs. In the proposed model of HCQ-ZnONPs, a quinoline nitrogen of the HCQ molecule interacts with an exposed Zn2+ site on the surface of a ZnONPs cluster. The HCQ-ZnONPs exhibited a drug loading of 21.4% and showed approximately 48.4% cumulative HCQ release over 24 h at pH 7.4. To the best of our knowledge, this is the first report of an HCQ-ZnONPs nanocluster system. Biological evaluation demonstrated synergistic in vitro antimalarial activity, indicating enhanced efficacy compared with the parent drug, suggesting that this arises from the integration of HCQ and ZnO nanoclusters while maintaining favorable cytocompatibility in Vero cells. The oxidative stress and anti-inflammatory potential of the hybrid complex was also assessed, highlighting its multifunctional biological profile that may be advantageous for mitigating malaria-associated oxidative stress and inflammatory responses. Molecular docking against PfDHFR-TSfurther supported favorable ligand-target interactions and provided additional insight into the potential molecular basis of the observed biological activity. Conclusions: Collectively, the experimental, theoretical, and mathematical analysis suggests the successful formation of HCQ-ZnONPs with promising anti-inflammatory and antimalarial efficacy, establishing this hybrid nano system as a potential candidate for next-generation antiplasmodial therapy.

42931448.titulo: São Tomé and Príncipe on the Verge of Eliminating Lymphatic Filariasis as a Public Health Problem: Evidence from IDA Impact Assessment Surveys.
42931448.autores: Bakajika D, Rosário A, … Cano J (13 autores)
42931448.resumo: Accelerated efforts to eliminate lymphatic filariasis (LF) as a public health problem have been supported by the introduction of the triple-drug regimen of ivermectin, diethylcarbamazine and albendazole (IDA) in endemic settings. In São Tomé and Príncipe, nationwide mass drug administration (MDA) with diethylcarbamazine and albendazole was implemented in 2018, followed by IDA in 2019 and 2020. This study assesses progress towards elimination using post-MDA impact assessment surveys conducted after cessation of treatment. Cross-sectional surveys were conducted among adults aged 20 years and older in 2022 and again between December 2024 and January 2025. Circulating filarial antigen (CFA) was detected using the filarial test strip (FTS). Individuals who tested positive were examined for microfilaremia using nocturnal calibrated thick blood smear microscopy. MDA coverage data were obtained from national programme records, and morbidity was assessed by clinical screening during the surveys. Three rounds of nationwide MDA achieved high epidemiological coverage (86.4% in 2018, 74.2% in 2019 and 80.0% in 2020). The impact assessment surveys conducted in 2022 evaluated 14,132 adults, with 21 individuals (0.15%) testing positive for CFA, while the follow-up survey conducted between December 2024 and January 2025 assessed 14,653 adults and detected seven positive cases (0.05%). No microfilariae were detected among the 28 antigen-positive individuals examined using nocturnal calibrated thick blood smears. Clinical screening during the surveys identified 190 cases of lymphoedema and nine cases of hydrocoele. Infection indicators remain well below WHO decision thresholds, suggesting that LF transmission is unlikely to be sustained. São Tomé and Príncipe appears to be close to eliminating LF as a public health problem. However, strengthening morbidity management services will be essential to support the preparation of the national elimination dossier.

42934756.titulo: Harnessing omics to refine taxonomic classification in the malaria vector Anopheles gambiae species complex: a review.
42934756.autores: Milugo TK, Kwi P, … Amambua-Ngwa A (5 autores)
42934756.resumo: The malaria vector Anopheles gambiae s.l. (Diptera: Culicidae) is predominant in sub-Saharan Africa, where it plays a crucial role in transmitting malaria parasites to humans. Hitherto considered a single species, advances in cytogenetics and genomics have unveiled members of the complex as separate species. Whilst these species are morphologically indistinguishable, they are genetically distinct exhibiting significant differences in their ecological interactions and behavior. For example, they display considerable variation in their response to vector control measures and capacity to host malaria parasite, contributing differentially to malaria transmission. Consequently, precise taxonomic identification might help guide control programs against them. However, current approaches used in An. gambiae taxonomic systematics differ in accuracy and sensitivity, making it difficult to correctly delimit species boundaries. In this review, we discuss available taxonomic approaches utilized in An. gambiae complex whilst providing a framework for future taxonomic efforts. We also examine the process of naming a new species within the complex and detail the complexities of existing nomenclature approaches, as well as the prospective challenges they present, while advocating for an alternative approach. We conclude by providing a perspective on the use of a robust integrated approach in classifying and naming species of the An. gambiae complex.

42934655.titulo: Insecticide resistance intensity in Anopheles gambiae s.l. populations from Nioro and Ndoffane health districts, Senegal.
42934655.autores: Diallo S, Diop M, … Niang EHA (13 autores)
42934655.resumo:
Malaria remains a major public health concern in sub-Saharan Africa. In Senegal, the increasing resistance of Anopheles gambiae sensu lato (s.l.) to main public health insecticides threatens the effectiveness of long-lasting insecticide-treated nets (LLINs) and indoor residual spraying (IRS). This study aimed to assess insecticide resistance intensity and to determine the distribution of kdr and Ace-1 resistance mutations in wild An. gambiae s.l. populations from Nioro and Ndoffane districts (Kaolack region).
Anopheles larvae were collected between September and November 2018 and reared under insectary conditions. Adult females were subjected to World Health Organization (WHO) susceptibility assays using five insecticides: three pyrethroids, one carbamate and one organophosphate. Resistance intensity assays were conducted at 5 × and 10 × diagnostic concentrations. Species within the An. gambiae complex and the East-kdr (1014S), West-kdr (1014F) and Ace-1 (G119S) were identified using Polymerase Chain Reaction (PCR) technique.
A total of 1830 females An. gambiae s.l. were tested. Widespread resistance to pyrethroids and organophosphates was observed in both districts, while in Ndoffane complete susceptibility to bendiocarb was recorded and in Nioro resistance was observed. Anopheles arabiensis was the predominant species (> 90%), followed by An. gambiae s.s. and An. coluzzii. The frequencies of East-kdr and West-kdr mutations were higher in Ndoffane (40.4% and 30.8%) than in Nioro (10.6% and 13.1%). The Ace-1 (G119S) mutation was detected exclusively in the heterozygous state across all the study populations.
The studied vectors exhibit multiple insecticide resistance mechanisms, likely driven by combined selection pressures from agricultural and public health insecticide use. Strengthening entomological surveillance and implementing integrated resistance management strategies are essential to preserve the effectiveness of malaria vector control interventions in Senegal.

42934639.titulo: Epidemiology of malaria and district-level factors associated with malaria elimination in Sumatra region, Indonesia: a retrospective analysis of surveillance data.
42934639.autores: Lestari KD, Surendra H, … Elyazar IRF (15 autores)
42934639.resumo:
As transmission declines, malaria becomes more spatially and demographically concentrated. This study investigated individual-level malaria characteristics and district-level factors associated with elimination in all 154 districts in Sumatra, Indonesia.
We analysed individual-level data of 13,386 reported malaria cases from 2019 to 2021. P. falciparum and P. vivax were confirmed by microscopy or rapid diagnostic test, while probable P. knowlesi was defined as microscopically identified P. knowlesi. Cases were classified as imported if they reported travel to endemic region within 2-4 weeks. Multivariable logistic regression with province as a random effect was used to examine individual-level factors associated with imported cases, and district-level socioeconomic and environmental factors associated with elimination. Spatial clustering of indigenous cases was assessed using Global Moran's I and SaTScan.
Among reported cases, 71.8% (9,617) were P. vivax, 18.4% (2,467) P. falciparum, and 2.8% (369) probable P. knowlesi. Of 11,390 investigated cases, 8,748 (76.8%) were indigenous, 1,741 (15.3%) imported, and 901 (7.9%) unclassified. Imported cases were associated with older age (adjusted odds ratio 1.79, 95%CI 1.42-2.25 for 15-24 years old, and 1.97, 1.59-2.46 for 25-64 years old, compared to < 15 years old), males (1.70, 1.43-2.03), mobile and migrant population-related occupations (1.46, 1.22-1.76), diagnosed at hospitals or clinics (2.32, 1.85-2.91), infected with P. falciparum (1.48, 1.22-1.80), and hospitalised (15.29, 12.66-18.46). At the district level, a higher human development index (1.15, 1.01-1.34), lower historical annual parasite incidence (0.46, 0.29-0.69), and fewer endemic neighbours (0.78, 0.67-0.89) were associated with a higher likelihood of elimination. Spatial analysis revealed clustering tendencies, with localised clusters for P. falciparum, P. vivax, and probable P. knowlesi.
Dynamics of imported malaria, heterogeneous clusters of local transmission, and lower district-level human development index challenged elimination efforts. This highlights the need for strengthened surveillance and targeted interventions.

42928299.titulo: Molecular characterization of antimalarial resistance and hrp2/3 deletions in Plasmodium falciparum strains from Mtwara, Tanzania (2021-2024).
42928299.autores: Thapradit P, Pagornrat W, … Imwong M (10 autores)
42928299.resumo:
Malaria remains a significant public health challenge in sub-Saharan Africa and Southeast Asia, with Plasmodium falciparum responsible for the majority of infections and deaths, particularly among children aged < 5 years. In Tanzania, the widespread use of antimalarial drugs, such as sulfadoxine-pyrimethamine for preventive therapy and artemisinin-based combination therapies as first-line treatment, has prompted concerns about the emergence and spread of drug resistance. The prolonged use of these drugs may have influenced resistance patterns, varying over time. Moreover, some P. falciparum samples have been reported as rapid diagnostic test (RDT)-negative despite microscopic confirmation of P. falciparum infection, raising questions about whether such false-negative results are due to poor-quality RDT kits or genetic deletions in the parasite.
This study investigated drug resistance dynamics and potential false-negative RDT results in P. falciparum by analyzing molecular markers in pfdhps, pfdhfr, pfkelch13, and pfhrp2/3, with the 18S rRNA gene used as a housekeeping control to verify DNA quality and confirm true parasite positivity.
Molecular analysis revealed a decline in the triple pfdhfr mutation paired with double pfdhps mutations, alongside an increase in mixed dhfr-dhps haplotypes (χ2 = 28.94, p < 0.001), indicating ongoing genetic diversification under drug pressure. Wild-type parasites were predominant (56-76%), and most pfkelch13 mutations were located in the non-propeller region, with no validated or candidate mutations associated with artemisinin-resistance detected. P. falciparum-infected samples that were RDT-negative showed a high frequency of both complete and partial deletions in pfhrp2 and pfhrp3, potentially explaining RDT inconsistencies and false-negative results.
P. falciparum remains the dominant species in this high-transmission region, showing a persistently high rate of antifolate resistance. Significant associations between triple pfdhfr and double pfdhps resistance markers were observed between 2021 and 2024. The continued susceptibility to artemisinin emphasizes the need for ongoing molecular surveillance and monitoring of hrp2/hrp3 deletions to support malaria control strategies in Tanzania.

42928273.titulo: Malaria among migrant populations in the Greater Mekong Subregion: a scoping review of evidence and implications for malaria elimination.
42928273.autores: Aung PL, Zay Ya K, … Sattabongkot J (8 autores)
42928273.revista: International journal for equity in health
42928273.resumo:
Countries in the Greater Mekong Subregion (GMS) have made substantial progress toward malaria elimination, with a regional goal of achieving elimination by 2030. However, residual transmission persists, particularly among migrant and mobile populations in border and forested areas, who often experience increased exposure and limited access to healthcare and preventive interventions. This scoping review aimed to synthesize evidence on malaria epidemiology, healthcare access, prevention practices, and health system challenges among migrant and mobile populations in the GMS.
A scoping review was conducted following PRISMA-ScR guidelines. Two electronic databases (PubMed and Scopus) were searched from inception to March 2026. Studies reporting on malaria among migrant or mobile populations in GMS countries were included. Two reviewers independently screened studies and extracted data. Findings were synthesized narratively and organized into six thematic domains.
A total of 847 records were identified, of which 52 studies met the inclusion criteria. Malaria burden among migrant and mobile populations was generally low but highly heterogeneous, with persistent transmission concentrated in border and forested areas and evidence of asymptomatic and submicroscopic infections indicating hidden reservoirs of transmission. Across the included studies, migrant and mobile populations experienced intersecting structural vulnerabilities, including cross-border mobility, precarious employment, legal and administrative barriers, language barriers, and limited access to health services, that contributed to delayed diagnosis and treatment, inconsistent uptake of preventive measures, and reliance on informal or cross-border healthcare. Preventive practices often remained suboptimal because of occupational and mobility-related constraints. Existing interventions, including community-based services and mobile health approaches, showed promise but remained limited in coverage and evaluation, underscoring persistent challenges for surveillance, service delivery, and cross-border coordination.
Migrant and mobile populations remain a critical challenge to malaria elimination in the GMS. Residual transmission is sustained by asymptomatic infections, structural barriers to healthcare access, suboptimal preventive practices, and high mobility. Achieving malaria elimination by 2030 will require tailored and equitable strategies that strengthen surveillance, expand flexible and accessible service delivery, and enhance cross-border collaboration for migrant and mobile populations.

42945251.titulo: A voltage-gated porin PPE1 regulates secretion and drug resistance in Mycobacterium tuberculosis.
42945251.autores: Yadav M, C A NF, … Gokhale RS (13 autores)
42945251.revista: Proceedings of the National Academy of Sciences of the United States of America
42945251.resumo: Drug resistance in Mycobacterium tuberculosis (Mtb) remains a formidable clinical hurdle, compounded by the fact that the pathways by which antibiotics penetrate its multilayered cell envelope remain incompletely mapped. We identify PPE1 as a voltage-gated outer-membrane porin that mediates the secretion of kupyaphores while also facilitating the uptake of the frontline anti-tubercular drug isoniazid (INH). Genome-wide association analysis of 38,038 clinical isolates links ppe1 mutations with INH resistance, highlighting its clinical relevance. Consistent with this, the Mtb Δppe1 mutant shows increased tolerance to INH, accompanied by markedly reduced intracellular accumulation of INH compared with the wild-type strain. The Δppe1 strain exhibits attenuated infection, impaired growth, and reduced virulence in a murine infection model. Electron microscopy, molecular modeling, and single-channel electrophysiology reveal that PPE1 assembles into an unusual pentameric α-helical channel, distinct from classical β-barrel bacterial porins. Together, our findings identify PPE1 as a key determinant of mycobacterial membrane permeability that coordinates metallophore secretion and also antibiotic influx. This work uncovers a previously unrecognized mechanism governing Mtb physiology, virulence, and drug susceptibility, providing a potential target for therapeutic intervention.

42948590.titulo: Ginsenoside Rd alleviates atherosclerosis by inhibiting adipocyte ferroptosis in perivascular adipose tissues.
42948590.autores: Fu X, Liu C, … Li X (6 autores)
42948590.resumo:
Ginsenoside Rd (Rd) is an active ingredient in Panax ginseng Meyer and can be absorbed into the adipose tissue. Here, we aimed to investigate the impact of Rd on atherosclerosis (AS) and explore the mechanism.
We constructed an AS model by feeding ApoE-/- mice with a standard Western high-fat diet, treated with Rd, and combined RORC and TIGAR adipocyte-specific adeno-associated virus infection. An inflammatory adipocyte model (3T3-L1) was induced by LPS, and a lipid accumulation model in adipocytes was induced by palmitic acid. We investigated the role of the Rd-mediated RORC/TIGAR axis in adipocyte inflammation, oxidative stress, and ferroptosis through lentiviral vectors and the ferroptosis activator erastin. The interactions between RORC and TIGAR were examined. Next, the degree of lipid peroxidation and ferroptosis within perivascular adipose tissues (PVAT) in mice and 3T3-L1 cells was assessed.
Rd improved PVAT dysfunction and alleviated endothelial inflammation in AS mice. Rd targeted and inhibited RORC expression in adipocytes within the PVAT of mice. The transcription factor RORC occupied the TIGAR promoter to repress TIGAR transcription. Reactivation of RORC reversed the therapeutic benefit of Rd on AS, and reactivation of TIGAR also alleviated AS exacerbated by RORC. Rd reached therapeutic benefits by inhibiting RORC expression in adipocytes within PVAT, weakening its inhibitory effect on TIGAR, and further inhibiting adipocyte ferroptosis.
Rd targets RORC to activate TIGAR expression and block adipocyte ferroptosis in PVAT, thereby inhibiting AS.

42950033.titulo: Lipid-sensing GPR183-KRAS signaling mediates TH17 autoimmunity and identifies fluvoxamine repurposing in uveitis.
42950033.autores: Zhang C, Liu X, … Su W (13 autores)
42950033.resumo: Autoimmune uveitis (AU) is a leading cause of irreversible blindness driven by pathogenic T helper 17 (TH17) cell-mediated inflammation, yet current therapies are limited by efficacy and side effects, with immunometabolic mechanisms remaining poorly defined. By integrating single-cell RNA sequencing and multilayered metabolomic profiling in patients with AU and experimental AU models, we identified the lipid-sensing G protein-coupled receptor GPR183 as a key immunometabolic regulator in pathogenic CD4+ T cells. Upon activation, GPR183 modulates intracellular signaling via suppression of cyclic adenosine monophosphate-cAMP-dependent protein kinase activity and promotion of son-of-sevenless-dependent KRAS activation, which in turn elicits copper overload-induced mitochondrial oxidative stress, structural impairment, and metabolic rewiring toward glycolysis, thereby promoting TH17 cell pathogenicity. For clinical translation, virtual screening of Food and Drug Administration-approved drugs coupled with molecular docking and microscale thermophoresis validation identified fluvoxamine (FLV) as a direct GPR183 antagonist. In in vivo and in vitro uveitis and colitis models, FLV attenuated GPR183-KRAS signaling, dampened pathogenic TH17 cell responses, and alleviated tissue inflammation. These findings delineate a unique GPR183-KRAS-mitochondrial damage axis governing TH17-driven autoimmunity and support repurposing FLV as a translatable therapeutic approach for AU and other autoimmune inflammatory disorders.

42949343.titulo: Dietary Fiber Improves High-Fat Diet-Induced Hyperglycemia by Modulating Intestinal ILC3-Mediated Immunity through the SCFA-FFAR2 Pathway.
42949343.autores: Mou Y, Long F, … Zhou J (8 autores)
42949343.revista: Journal of agricultural and food chemistry
42949343.resumo: Dietary fiber intake is associated with improved glycemic control in high-fat diet-induced hyperglycemia, yet the immunological mechanisms linking gut microbiota-derived metabolites to host defense remain poorly defined. Here, we investigated whether dietary fiber ameliorates these metabolic disorders by modulating intestinal group 3 innate lymphoid cells (ILC3s) via short-chain fatty acids (SCFAs) and their receptor FFAR2. In a 12-week fiber-supplemented high-fat diet mouse model, fiber alleviated hyperglycemia, insulin resistance, and intestinal barrier dysfunction. Mechanistically, fiber increased cecal SCFAs (especially propionate), which activated colonic ILC3s in an FFAR2-dependent manner. FFAR2 triggered ERK and STAT3 phosphorylation and directly bound STAT3 to facilitate its phosphorylation, boosting IL-22 transcription. SCFA-activated ILC3s strengthened epithelial barrier integrity via elevated tight-junction proteins. Collectively, our findings demonstrate that dietary fiber restores gut barrier function through the SCFA-FFAR2-ERK/STAT3-IL-22 axis in ILC 3s, highlighting ILC3-expressed FFAR2 as a potential therapeutic target for high-fat diet-related metabolic disorders.

42937463.titulo: Powerhouses of lethality: mitochondria in macrophage antimicrobial activity.
42937463.autores: McFadden MJ, O'Meara TR, O'Riordan MX
42937463.resumo: Macrophages employ multiple strategies to dispatch phagocytosed microbes, including bombardment with toxic compounds and radicals, or the deprivation of key nutrients. The lethality of macrophages depends on their ability to regulate levels of microbicidal effectors and proper targeting of these effectors to the phagosome, where many intracellular pathogens are detained. Mitochondria play important roles in establishing an antimicrobial phagosomal environment in macrophages, playing roles in both the production and targeting of these effectors. In response to infection, the mitochondrial network undergoes dramatic structural and functional perturbations that modulate macrophage microbicidal potential. As central coordinators of cellular metabolism, mitochondria control the abundance of metabolites that can either be toxic to ingested microbes or necessary for their growth. Mitochondria are also prolific producers of reactive oxygen species (ROS), which play direct roles in killing microbes and serve as signaling molecules to coordinate antimicrobial responses. While mitochondria are also known to play extensive roles in regulating cytokine production and proinflammatory responses, this review will focus on highlighting mechanisms by which mitochondria manipulate the macrophage microbicidal milieu.

42934110.titulo: [LGALS3 is an efferocytosis-related biomarker and potential traditional Chinese medicine therapeutic target for diabetic kidney disease complicated with heart failure].
42934110.autores: Hu D, Guo H, … Nie X (7 autores)
42934110.revista: Nan fang yi ke da xue xue bao = Journal of Southern Medical University
42934110.resumo:
To explore the immune efferocytosis mechanisms of diabetic kidney disease (DKD) complicated with chronic heart failure (CHF) in light of the glucose heart kidney axis and predict the "same treatment for different diseases" strategy using traditional Chinese medicine (TCM).
DKD and CHF transcriptome data from public databases were integrated to construct a core gene set using differential expression and weighted gene co-expression network analysis (WGCNA). The hub genes were intersected with an efferocytosis-related gene set, validated with external datasets, and functionally enriched. The Coremine Medical database and molecular docking were used to predict the regulatory TCMs, their properties, and affinities between the active ingredients and their targets. Clinical serum samples were collected form patients with DKD, CHF, and DKD+CHF and healthy individuals for detecting galectin 3 (LGALS3) levels.
Fifty comorbidity core genes were identified, which were enriched mainly in the PI3K Akt, TNF, AGE RAGE, and oxidative phosphorylation pathways. LGALS3 was identified as a key efferocytosis-associated hub gene with differential expression in the validation set. The prediction results included 216 TCMs predominantly exhibiting cold or warm properties with bitter, sweet or pungent flavors and liver, lung, spleen and kidney meridian tropisms. Molecular docking suggested strong binding between the key ingredients (e.g., quercetin) and LGALS3. Serum LGALS3 levels were significantly higher in patients with DKD+CHF than in those with DKD or CHF alone or healthy controls (all P<0.001). After adjusting for covariates, comorbid status remained independently and positively associated with LGALS3 (β=51.20, P<0.001), exceeding the independent contribution of NT proBNP.
DKD-CHF is associated with inflammatory/metabolic abnormalities and impairment of efferocytosis-mediated immune clearance. LGALS3 is a critical node connecting inflammatory pathways to target organ efferocytosis dysfunction. The predicted TCMs highlight the TCM therapeutic principles of "supplementing Qi, clearing the heat and resolving stasis" and may regulate efferocytosis and the immunometabolic microenvironment by targeting LGALS3.

42942044.titulo: Beyond Targeted Delivery: The Emerging Immunomodulatory Landscape of Antibody-Oligonucleotide Conjugates.
42942044.autores: Wang Y, Wang S, Wang H
42942044.resumo: Antibody-oligonucleotide conjugates (AOCs) are usually viewed as delivery vehicles that carry nucleic-acid payloads to defined cell populations for gene silencing or gene regulation. Existing reviews concentrate on delivery systems, tumour-directed therapy and extrahepatic oligonucleotide delivery, while the intrinsic immunomodulatory activity of AOCs has received far less attention. Conjugation couples antibody-mediated targeting with the innate immune-stimulating activity of the payload, a property that most current AOCs seldom exploit. This review repositions AOCs as active immune regulators. Three emerging immunoregulatory applications are examined in detail: vaccine-adjuvant construction, neutrophil-driven innate immune activation, and immunometabolic reprogramming. Structure-activity relationships linking AOC design to immune potency are summarized, and their immune mechanisms are distinguished from those of free oligonucleotides and unconjugated antibodies. Based on preclinical and in vitro evidence, AOCs act as multifunctional immunomodulators rather than passive cargo carriers. Two sources of immune activity are distinguished: direct immunostimulation by the conjugated payload, and effects secondary to targeted delivery. These findings still await clinical confirmation. Key barriers to translation, including conjugation efficiency, mechanistic gaps and manufacturing bottlenecks, are discussed. Prospective applications include engineered vaccines, anti-infective innate therapy, tumour microenvironment remodelling and autoimmune intervention, pending further validation. This review provides a conceptual framework for developing next-generation AOC-based immune adjuvants and precision immunotherapeutics.

42942991.titulo: Beyond Neuroinflammation: Targeting the Microbe-Barrier-Brain Axis Through Precision Nutrition in Neurological Long COVID (Neuro-PASC).
42942991.autores: Velázquez De Castro-Bono A, Castro-Luna G, Guil-Guerrero JL
42942991.resumo: Post-acute Neurological Sequelae of SARS-CoV-2 infection (Neuro-PASC) contribute substantially to Long COVID-related disability, with cognitive impairment, chronic fatigue, dysautonomia, and neuropsychiatric symptoms among its most debilitating manifestations. Although its pathogenesis remains incompletely understood, evidence implicates persistent immune activation, intestinal barrier dysfunction, microbiota dysbiosis, microbiome-derived metabolic alterations, mitochondrial dysfunction, and neuroimmune interactions in sustaining neuroinflammation and neurological impairment. This narrative review examines precision nutrition as a potential pathway-oriented strategy for Neuro-PASC. We synthesise evidence linking the gut microbiota, intestinal permeability, immunometabolic pathways, mitochondrial function, and neurological outcomes, while evaluating nutritional interventions targeting these mechanisms. We focus on candidate biomarkers, including serum zonulin, fatty acid-binding protein 2 (FABP2), faecal short-chain fatty acids (SCFAs), and the kynurenine-to-tryptophan ratio, which may support patient stratification and personalised nutritional strategies. We also propose a stepwise framework involving dietary stabilisation, functional foods, targeted supplementation, and microbiome-based interventions, alongside practical considerations for post-exertional symptom exacerbation, dysautonomia, and mast cell-related symptoms. Finally, we identify priorities for future research, including multi-omics integration, artificial intelligence, digital health, and biomarker-stratified randomised controlled trials. Because current evidence remains predominantly observational and mechanistic, precision nutrition should be considered a complementary strategy requiring rigorous clinical validation.

42943606.titulo: c-Myc Links TGF-β Signaling to Metabolic Control of HIV Reactivation in OM10.1 Cells.
42943606.autores: Harrison-Gleason J, Kim J, Martinelli E
42943606.resumo: Antiretroviral therapy (ART) suppresses HIV replication but does not eliminate persistent viral reservoirs, which can rapidly reseed viremia following treatment interruption. We previously showed that blockade of transforming growth factor beta (TGF-β) signaling in vivo promotes SIV latency reversal and is associated with reversal of cellular metabolic quiescence. Here, using the provirally infected promyelocytic OM10.1 cell line, we investigated the cell-intrinsic mechanisms through which TGF-β regulates HIV reactivation. TGF-β inhibited proviral reactivation following stimulation with distinct latency-reversing agents, and this effect was reversed by pharmacologic inhibition of TGF-β signaling. TGF-β reduced HIV transcription without suppressing TNF-α-induced NF-κB activation, suggesting inhibition through an alternative mechanism. Bulk RNA sequencing revealed broad suppression of c-Myc-associated pathways, oxidative phosphorylation, and mTORC1 signaling. Functional metabolic profiling confirmed marked reductions in both glycolytic and mitochondrial ATP production and decreased mitochondrial membrane polarization. Consistent with a functional link between metabolism and viral reactivation, mitochondrial uncoupling strongly inhibited HIV expression. Finally, MYC overexpression completely rescued HIV transcription and partially restored p24 production in TGF-β-treated cells. Together, these findings identify a cell-intrinsic mechanism through which TGF-β restrains HIV reactivation by imposing a metabolically quiescent state, mediated at least in part through suppression of c-Myc.

42941263.titulo: Lactate-Driven Biphasic Reprogramming of Macrophage Immune Responses.
42941263.autores: Guo Q, Ren P, … Fang C (10 autores)
42941263.resumo: Lactate is a metabolic substrate, an extracellular signaling molecule, and a precursor for protein lactylation, with diverse effects on macrophage immunity. Evidence from infection, tissue injury, efferocytosis, and cancer indicates that lactate-associated pathways can amplify inflammation, support resolution and tissue repair, or sustain immune suppression. These outcomes depend on the timing, cellular source and compartment, chemical formulation and pH, transport and receptor engagement, and the chemistry and targets of lactylation. In this narrative review, we critically synthesize the biochemical foundations of lactate metabolism and lactyl-group donation and examine the mechanisms underlying these distinct macrophage responses. We distinguish model-specific biphasic responses from a universal sequence of early inflammation followed by resolution, and separate reparative programs from impaired antimicrobial or antitumor immunity. We also evaluate evidence for histone and non-histone lactylation, emphasizing the limits of metabolic perturbations and chromatin associations for establishing site-specific causality. This framework identifies experimental variables that should be controlled and supports context-selective investigation of lactate-related therapeutic targets in inflammatory diseases and cancer.

42942941.titulo: Dietary Vitamin Intake and Cognitive Performance in Adults with Long COVID: The BioICOPER Study.
42942941.autores: Arjol D, Arroyo-Romero S, … BioICOPER Investigators Group (11 autores)
42942941.resumo: Background: Long COVID (LC) is associated with persistent cognitive symptoms, frequently described as brain fog, and with inflammatory, immunometabolic, and energetic mechanisms potentially involved in cognitive functioning. Vitamins participate in biological processes relevant to brain function, but the relationship between habitual dietary vitamin intake and cognitive performance in LC remains poorly studied. Objective: To analyze the relationship between dietary vitamin intake and cognitive performance in adults with LC, considering both objective performance and self-reported cognition. Methods: A cross-sectional study was conducted in 304 adults with LC. Vitamin intake from foods and beverages was estimated using the EVIDENT seven-day dietary record, previously compared with a validated food-frequency questionnaire. Objective cognitive performance was assessed using normative scores from the Montreal Cognitive Assessment (MoCA) and the Memory Index Score (MIS), as well as MoCA domains and items. Self-reported cognition was assessed using the 30-item Memory Failures of Everyday Questionnaire (MFE-30) and the cognitive subscale of the Modified Fatigue Impact Scale (MFIS). Primary global associations were examined using multiple linear regression with HC3 robust standard errors, whereas bounded MoCA domains were analyzed using proportional-odds ordinal regression and binary item-level outcomes using logistic regression. Benjamini-Hochberg correction was applied within prespecified families of contrasts. Results: No associations between vitamin intake and global normative cognitive performance remained significant after false discovery rate (FDR) correction. Median MoCA and MIS scores were 24.00 (IQR, 21.00-26.00) and 11.00 (IQR, 9.00-13.00), respectively. Normative MoCA and MIS scores showed medians of -0.32 (IQR, -0.82 to 0.19) and -0.32 (IQR, -0.76 to 0.14), respectively. Most participants (95.1%) met the dietary reference value for vitamin B3. In secondary ordinal analyses, higher vitamin B3 intake was associated with better MoCA language performance in the fully adjusted model (OR per 1 SD = 2.18, 95% CI 1.45-3.27, p < 0.001, q = 0.0116). No associations remained significant after FDR correction for everyday cognitive complaints, cognitive fatigue, or MoCA Memory and MoCA Multiple scores. Conclusions: In adults with LC, the primary analyses did not identify FDR-significant associations between habitual dietary vitamin intake and global normative cognitive performance. The secondary vitamin B3-language association requires independent confirmation and does not establish a cognitive benefit of higher intake or supplementation. These findings require confirmation in longitudinal studies incorporating nutritional biomarkers, information on supplementation, and broader neuropsychological assessment.

42948128.titulo: Immunometabolic reprogramming of macrophages and neutrophils in acute pancreatitis: from metabolic stress to amplification and endogenous braking.
42948128.autores: Ai Y, Zhang L, … Yao S (8 autores)
42948128.resumo: Acute pancreatitis (AP) progression involves both the initiating acinar injury and immune responses that sustain or contain subsequent damage. This review integrates evidence on metabolic regulation in macrophages and neutrophils to examine its links to inflammatory effectors, clearance, and tissue protection. Glycolytic regulation can support inflammatory activation, while non-AP neutrophil studies show how substrate allocation supports oxidant production and neutrophil extracellular trap (NET) release. Metabolite signaling also participates in macrophage efferocytosis, repair-associated responses, and tissue antioxidant defense. Contrasting lactate effects in acinar injury and macrophage repair indicate that metabolic changes must be interpreted through their effects on particular cells and functions. We propose an integrated amplification-braking framework that connects metabolically supported inflammatory effectors to continued generation of injury-derived stimuli, and clearance, antioxidant, and repair functions to damage containment. These functions can coexist without receiving equivalent metabolic support, and protective braking is distinct from generalized immunosuppression. Evidence differs across cells and experimental systems; metabolic regulation of inflammatory activation does not by itself establish metabolic control of NET-mediated injury in AP. The framework provides a basis for evaluating whether metabolic interventions can limit damaging activity while preserving protective functions, but it is not a validated clinical model. Pairing metabolic changes with specific cellular functions and subsequent injury is central to testing these relationships.

42940128.titulo: The Aldosterone-Immune Axis in Primary Aldosteronism: Linking Adrenal Pathogenesis to Systemic Inflammation and Target-Organ Damage.
42940128.autores: Zaidi NE, Azizan EA, Ali A
42940128.resumo: Primary aldosteronism (PA) is the most common endocrine cause of secondary hypertension and is increasingly recognised as a systemic disorder extending beyond haemodynamic dysregulation. Accumulating evidence suggests that chronic autonomous aldosterone excess promotes maladaptive immune activation, establishing an aldosterone-immune axis that may contribute to cardiovascular, renal, and metabolic injury independently of blood pressure elevation. In some patients, glucocorticoid co-secretion may further amplify tissue-specific mineralocorticoid receptor (MR) signalling. Human and experimental studies indicate that aldosterone modulates both innate and adaptive immunity. Patients with PA demonstrate altered monocyte transcriptional profiles, enhanced vascular inflammatory activity, and increased pro-inflammatory cytokine signalling in monocyte-derived macrophages compared with blood-pressure-matched essential hypertension controls. Experimental models further show that sustained aldosterone exposure promotes macrophage M1 polarisation, dendritic cell activation, Th17 expansion, and regulatory T-cell suppression. These inflammatory changes are accompanied by oxidative stress, endothelial dysfunction, fibroblast activation, and extracellular matrix remodelling across cardiovascular and renal tissues. Emerging evidence is also consistent with a role for trained innate immunity, whereby prolonged aldosterone exposure may induce persistent epigenetic and metabolic reprogramming of monocytes and macrophages. Whether such reprogramming persists after biochemical correction by adrenalectomy or MR antagonism in human PA has not yet been directly demonstrated and remains an important open question. If confirmed, these mechanisms may help explain the partial irreversibility of target-organ damage despite successful treatment. This review synthesises current evidence linking adrenal somatic pathogenesis to systemic immune dysregulation and target-organ injury in PA. We propose that PA should be viewed not solely as a hypertensive disorder, but as a chronic fibro-inflammatory endocrine disease with important implications for early diagnosis, risk stratification, and targeted therapy. Future prospective human studies are needed to confirm the mechanistic hierarchy proposed and to identify the immunological targets most amenable to therapeutic intervention.

42931425.titulo: Advancing Tuberculosis Vaccination: Immunological Insights and Emerging Strategies for Improved Protection.
42931425.autores: Zhang Z, Sanchez C, … Chacon J (8 autores)
42931425.resumo: Tuberculosis (TB) remains one of the leading causes of infectious disease mortality worldwide despite widespread Bacille Calmette-Guérin (BCG) vaccination and decades of control efforts. The limited and variable efficacy of current vaccination strategies, particularly against adult pulmonary disease, highlights the need for a deeper understanding of the host immune mechanisms that determine protection against Mycobacterium tuberculosis. While traditional approaches to TB vaccine development have largely focused on pathogen-specific immunity and clinical efficacy, emerging evidence suggests that successful TB control may depend equally on the strategic modulation of host immune responses. This narrative review examines the immunological basis of TB vaccination, emphasizing how contemporary vaccine platforms reshape both innate and adaptive immunity. We discuss the roles of trained immunity, T-cell function, immune memory, and mucosal immune responses in mediating protection, as well as the mechanisms by which M. tuberculosis evades immune surveillance. The review further explores next-generation vaccine technologies, including protein-adjuvant, viral-vectored, live-attenuated, and mRNA-based vaccines, highlighting their distinct immunological targets. Particular attention is given to mucosal immunity, systems vaccinology, and the ongoing search for reliable correlates of protection, which collectively offer new opportunities to improve vaccine design and evaluation. Finally, we examine host-directed immunomodulatory approaches, immune-engineering strategies, and precision vaccinology as emerging paradigms for TB prevention. By reframing TB vaccines as instruments for immune reprogramming rather than solely pathogen-specific interventions, this review provides an integrated perspective on how advances in immunology may accelerate progress toward global TB control and the goals of the WHO End TB Strategy.

42940119.titulo: Glucocorticoid Receptor Alpha as an Integrative Regulator of Host Defense: A Systems-Level Review and Framework for Immune Regulation and Homeostatic Correction.
42940119.resumo: Current concepts recognize that effective host defense depends on coordinated interactions among innate and adaptive immunity, inflammatory signaling, immunometabolic regulation, and multiple complementary adaptive biological processes. However, far less attention has focused on the regulatory systems that integrate these diverse responses across the evolving phases of the host response. This Review proposes that glucocorticoid receptor alpha (GRα) functions as a systems-level integrative regulator that may contribute to the integration of immune signaling, antimicrobial competence, mitochondrial bioenergetics, inflammatory regulation, and other adaptive processes across partially overlapping adaptive phases of homeostatic correction. A central premise is that these phase-specific actions are shaped by dynamic changes in chromatin accessibility and transcription-factor interactions, providing a molecular basis for differential GRα regulation throughout the adaptive response. Rather than functioning solely as a transcriptional regulator of inflammation, GRα influences biological processes involved in pathogen sensing, NF-κB/AP-1 signaling, immunometabolic adaptation, innate and adaptive immune responses, endothelial and epithelial barrier integrity, lymphatic function, tissue repair, and the transition from early host defense to inflammatory resolution and restoration of physiological homeostasis. These integrated biological processes are organized within the proposed Priming, Modulatory, and Restorative phases of homeostatic correction. By synthesizing evidence across multiple physiological systems, this Review provides a biologically plausible model for understanding how GRα-associated regulatory mechanisms may contribute to immune effectiveness, disease tolerance, host-defense outcomes, and adaptive recovery during infection and critical illness. The proposed model generates testable hypotheses to guide future mechanistic investigation and the development of precision therapeutic strategies.

42936064.titulo: From emergency myelopoiesis to trained immunity? Reframing post-stroke myeloid reprogramming along the brain-bone marrow axis.
42936064.resumo: Ischemic stroke rapidly mobilizes myeloid cells from anatomically distinct bone-marrow niches, while emerging evidence indicates that severe cerebral injury can also leave a durable imprint on hematopoiesis. These observations have encouraged the use of the term trained immunity in stroke biology, but acute myeloid expansion is not equivalent to innate immune memory. In this Mini review, we distinguish acute myeloid activation, myelopoietic responses consistent with emergency myelopoiesis, and central trained immunity involving hematopoietic stem and progenitor cells (HSPCs). We use an operational four-feature framework-persistence, progenitor involvement, epigenetic or metabolic reprogramming, and functional recall-to grade the strength of current evidence. We consider a sequential transition from emergency myelopoiesis to trained immunity as one testable possibility rather than an established pathway, while allowing for parallel or independent mechanisms. The key unresolved questions are where durable memory is stored, when acute hematopoietic adaptation becomes stabilized, and which outputs are maladaptive versus reparative. Resolving these boundaries is essential before marrow-directed immunomodulation can be translated to patients with ischemic stroke.

42935806.titulo: Obesity-driven inflammation and immune dysregulation in cancer development and progression.
42935806.autores: Pandey P, Struder JF, … Altwegg KA (7 autores)
42935806.resumo: Obesity increases the risk and progression of at least 13 types of cancer. Although the epidemiologic links between excess adiposity and these cancers are well documented, the biological mechanisms linking obesity to carcinogenesis and tumor progression remain incompletely understood. White adipose tissue in obesity is a source of inflammatory and immunosuppressive signals that act systemically, driving metabolic, inflammatory, and immune dysfunction whose consequences differ across tumor types. As adipose tissue expands and adipocytes enlarge, the blood supply becomes inadequate, leading to hypoxia, fibrosis, lipolytic stress, macrophage recruitment, and chronic low-grade inflammation. These obesity-induced perturbations generate endocrine, cytokine, lipid, and metabolic signals that act systemically, within the tumor microenvironment (TME), and/or cell-intrinsically to activate oncogenic and tumor-promoting pathways. The same signals reshape innate and adaptive immunity, promoting tumor-permissive macrophage states and myeloid-derived suppressor cell expansion, while the effector arms weaken as antigen presentation, natural killer cell and T cell function all decline. This review synthesizes current evidence linking obesity-associated inflammation and immune dysregulation to cancer initiation, progression, and treatment responses across multiple obesity-related cancers. Emphasis is placed on adipose tissue inflammation, myeloid cell biology, T cell immunometabolism, endocrine-inflammatory crosstalk, and the relationship between obesity and immunotherapy. Finally, we discuss translational opportunities for preventing or intercepting obesity-related cancers, including weight loss achieved through lifestyle, surgical, or pharmacologic approaches, with an emphasis on GLP-1 receptor agonists given their substantial efficacy, rapid clinical uptake, and potential to reshape obesity-related cancer prevention and survivorship strategies. Defining the metabolic, immune, and inflammatory phenotypes that drive obesity-associated cancer risk and progression will be essential for developing more precise, mechanism-based strategies for prevention, treatment, and survivorship care.

42935734.titulo: Metabolic stress and macrophage efferocytosis in osteoarthritis: mechanisms and therapeutic implications.
42935734.autores: Wu H, Yuan D, … Liu S (4 autores)
