42935734.resumo: Metabolic disturbances contribute to osteoarthritis through mechanisms that extend beyond increased mechanical loading, yet their effects on inflammatory resolution remain incompletely understood. Macrophage efferocytosis-the recognition, engulfment, and degradation of apoptotic cells-provides a potential link between metabolic stress and persistent synovitis. This Mini Review examines how obesity and hyperglycemia disrupt synovial macrophage clearance and evaluates the rationale for therapeutic restoration. Human observations and experimental osteoarthritis studies implicate reduced growth arrest-specific 6 signaling and hyperglycemia-associated CD11b lactylation in defective apoptotic-cell recognition and uptake. Complementary evidence from other inflammatory conditions identifies membrane trafficking, mitochondrial adaptation, and lysosomal cargo processing as additional determinants of clearance competence. Importantly, glycolysis and lactate have context-dependent effects: although lactylation can impair recognition, adaptive lactate signaling supports repeated engulfment and expansion of pro-resolving macrophages. This distinction challenges indiscriminate glycolytic inhibition and favors interventions matched to the affected clearance step. Defective efferocytosis may amplify synovitis through persistence of cellular debris and loss of resolution-promoting signals, thereby creating an environment unfavorable to cartilage homeostasis. Emerging receptor-directed, metabolic, and intra-articular delivery strategies offer opportunities to restore clearance, but clinical validation remains necessary. Translation will require identification of susceptible macrophage populations, functional assessment of the complete efferocytic process, and demonstration that clearance recovery mediates meaningful improvements in joint structure and symptoms.

42935714.titulo: Lactate dynamics at the Pseudomonas aeruginosa-host interface: bacterial metabolism, host defense, and emerging links to histone lactylation.
42935714.autores: Jian Y, Wu Z, … Wang K (7 autores)
42935714.resumo: At the Pseudomonas aeruginosa-host interface, lactate is both a host immunometabolic product and a preferred bacterial carbon source. Its local concentration reflects host production, bacterial utilization, transport, and clearance rather than inflammation alone. P. aeruginosa uses D- and L-lactate through stereospecific, conditionally regulated systems. It preferentially consumes lactate in human burn-wound exudate, and this capacity contributes to early intracellular survival in macrophages. Lactate-associated acidity also increases bacterial vesicle release and quinolone signaling, weakening antimicrobial-peptide activity independently of chromatin modification. On the host side, bacterial L-lactate utilization and virulence-factor-associated suppression of epithelial glycolysis lower epithelial lactate and histone H3 lysine 18 lactylation (H3K18la). These changes are linked to disrupted RNA regulation and impaired ciliary clearance. In macrophages, the quorum-sensing signal 2-aminoacetophenone (2-AA) reprograms bioenergetics, autophagy, and lipid metabolism, promoting tolerance and intracellular persistence. A separate hypothesis connecting 2-AA to increased macrophage lactate and H3K18la is supported only by a supplement abstract and requires full-length validation. Histone lactylation is therefore an emerging extension of this biology. This narrative review follows two linked strands: bacterial lactate utilization and lactate-associated changes in host defense. It distinguishes established metabolic effects from proposed lactylation-dependent mechanisms and considers potential therapeutic directions and their trade-offs. These include targeting bacterial lactate utilization, airway acidity, host transport or modification enzymes, and 2-AA-associated tolerance. Any benefit must be assessed against the possibility of supplying bacterial nutrients or worsening host injury.

42941767.titulo: Cachexia and Sarcopenia in Patients with Coexisting Chronic Obstructive Pulmonary Disease and Pulmonary Tuberculosis.
42941767.resumo: Malnutrition, loss of muscle mass, and reduced muscle strength are common but underrecognized conditions in tuberculosis (TB) and chronic obstructive pulmonary disease (COPD). These abnormalities may persist after completion of TB treatment, and a normal or elevated body mass index does not exclude muscle depletion. Unlike the extensively studied conditions of hyperglycemia and obesity, the catabolic end of the spectrum of metabolic disturbances in coexisting TB and COPD remains insufficiently investigated. This narrative review focuses on cachexia and sarcopenia in patients with coexisting TB and COPD (TB-COPD). It examines the roles of systemic inflammation, immunometabolic remodeling, mitochondrial dysfunction, disturbances in protein metabolism and endocrine regulation, and ceramide signaling. Because direct evidence in TB-COPD is scarce, findings from TB or post-tuberculosis lung disease without confirmed COPD and from COPD alone are used as indirect evidence, and the level of evidence is indicated for each mechanism. The diagnostic approach is organized around current clinical guidelines and includes assessment of nutritional status, diagnosis of malnutrition using the Global Leadership Initiative on Malnutrition (GLIM) criteria, identification of sarcopenia using European Working Group on Sarcopenia in Older People 2 (EWGSOP2) or Asian Working Group for Sarcopenia (AWGS) criteria, pulmonary function testing to distinguish post-tuberculosis airflow obstruction from COPD, and evaluation for reversible causes of muscle weakness. The main treatment approaches are correction of malnutrition, pulmonary rehabilitation, and treatment of the underlying respiratory disease. The effectiveness of interventions is assessed through changes in muscle strength, physical performance, body weight, and body composition. The evidence base for patients with coexisting TB and COPD remains limited; most studies have investigated each disease separately. The efficacy of pharmacological agents targeting the molecular mechanisms of muscle wasting has not been established in this population. Priorities for future research include prospective assessment of muscle function in TB-COPD cohorts and the development of personalized strategies for nutritional and rehabilitation support.

42941761.titulo: Beyond Histocompatibility: Donor Tissue Immune States and Their Role in Heart Transplantation.
42941761.autores: Urbanowicz T, Kowalewski M, … Raffa GM (4 autores)
42941761.resumo: Heart transplantation transfers not only donor alloantigens and functional myocardium but also a pre-existing tissue environment shaped by resident immune, vascular, stromal, and parenchymal populations. This review examines the hypothesis that the biological state of donor tissue influences subsequent recipient immunity and contributes to heterogeneity in allograft outcomes. Donor-resident macrophages, endothelial cells, fibroblasts, extracellular matrix, and tissue-resident lymphocytes constitute an immunologically active myocardial niche that encounters ischemia-reperfusion injury and recipient immune effectors immediately after implantation. Experimental and human studies demonstrate the dynamic coexistence and replacement of donor- and recipient-derived immune populations, with recipient cells acquiring phenotypes within the graft microenvironment. We distinguish transient donor-tissue activation from genuine tissue immune memory, which would require persistence of an exposure-induced molecular or functional state and an altered response to a subsequent challenge. Potential mechanisms include trained innate immunity, epigenetic and metabolic reprogramming, endothelial inflammatory memory, and persistent stromal-immune interactions. We propose that allograft biology be investigated at the level of the donor-recipient immune pair and outline longitudinal single-cell, spatial, and cell-of-origin approaches to test this concept in human heart transplantation.

42929808.titulo: The Vaginal Microbiome-Mitochondria Axis: Implications for Genital Tract Infections.
42929808.autores: Agoni L, Pericolini E, … De Seta F (5 autores)
42929808.resumo: The vaginal microbiome influences epithelial and immune homeostasis through microbial metabolites, virulence factors, and other molecular signals, yet intracellular mechanisms translating microbial activity into host responses remain largely unexplored. Here, we propose the vaginal microbiome-mitochondria axis as a functional framework linking microbial activity to host-cell metabolism, redox signaling, immunity, and cell fate. We integrated evidence from vaginal microbiology, mitochondrial biology, mucosal immunology, and immunometabolism, distinguishing direct observations in the female genital tract from mechanistic evidence obtained in other host-microbe systems. Available evidence indicates that microbial products relevant to vaginal homeostasis and dysbiosis can modulate mitochondrial bioenergetics, reactive oxygen species generation and redox signaling, membrane potential, dynamics, and quality control pathways, while mitochondrial responses can influence epithelial integrity and antimicrobial and inflammatory functions. We further propose that the balance between mitochondrial adaptation and dysfunction may contribute to resolution or persistence of vaginal disorders and that incomplete mitochondrial recovery could contribute to an incomplete microbial ecosystem-host reset and recurrence. Although direct vaginal evidence remains limited, this framework identifies mitochondria as a potentially important functional interface between microbial ecology and host response and generates testable hypotheses for investigating whether mitochondrial homeostasis contributes to durable resolution of vaginal dysbiosis and infection.

42939855.titulo: Lipidomic Remodelling and Low Sperm Quality Associated with High-Fat Diet-Induced Gut Microbial Dysbiosis in Mice.
42939855.autores: Pan M, Scarlata E, … O'Flaherty C (5 autores)
42939855.resumo: Infertility affects one in six couples worldwide, with male infertility contributing to ~50% of cases. Rising obesity rates have been linked to impaired male fertility, potentially through alterations in the gut microbiota; however, underlying mechanisms remain poorly understood. We characterized gut microbiome composition and lipidomic profiles in stool, serum, and testis samples. We assessed sperm quality in C57BL6 male mice fed a 45% fat diet (high-fat diet, HFD) or a 10% fat diet (normal diet, ND). We analyzed the gut microbiota by 16S rRNA sequencing. We measured short-chain fatty acids by gas chromatography. We performed untargeted lipidomic profiling of stool, serum, and testis using UPLC-MS/MS. CASA and cytochemical and immunocytochemical analyses assessed sperm quality and oxidative stress markers. HFD-fed mice exhibited gut microbiota dysbiosis characterized by an increased Bacillota/Bacteroidota ratio, altered bacterial community composition, increased acetic acid, and reduced butyric acid. Lipidomic analyses revealed distinct stool, serum, and testis lipid profiles, including increased abundance of gut microbiota-associated lipids containing odd-chain fatty acyl groups in HFD-fed mice. These alterations were accompanied by reduced sperm motility, impaired acrosomal integrity, epididymal sperm maturation and sperm capacitation, and elevated oxidative and nitrosative stress. Collectively, these findings support a gut-testis-epididymis axis in which altered gut microbiota-derived lipids contribute to oxidative stress and reduced sperm quality.

42931408.titulo: Off-Target Effects of Recombinant Zoster Vaccine: Clinical Benefits, AS01B Adjuvant Immunobiology, and Observational Evidence.
42931408.autores: Tang J, Balaji S, Oon HH
42931408.resumo: Background/Objectives: The recombinant zoster vaccine (RZV), Shingrix®, has shown great efficacy in protecting against herpes zoster. However, emerging evidence suggests that this RZV might provide benefits that extend beyond preventing varicella zoster virus (VZV) reactivation. Specifically, this scoping review explored the literature to investigate the reported non-zoster, off-target effects of the Shingrix® RZV, and the possible mechanistic explanations for these effects. Methods: Keyword searches of PubMed database were conducted, along with manual searches of other relevant journals and reference lists of primary articles. Results: Evidence from the included studies demonstrated relationships between administration of RZV vaccination and reduced risk of dementia, Alzheimer's disease and major adverse cardiological events (MACEs), while also conferring geroprotective effects. Mechanistic studies identified two possible causes, namely VZV suppression and AS01B adjuvant immunoregulation. Prevention of herpes zoster resulted in reduced risk of associated cognitive impairment and vasculopathy, reducing incidence of dementia and MACE. AS01B adjuvant was also linked to persistent monocyte reprogramming, and enhanced innate immune response and memory, known as "trained immunity", which provided a plausible explanation for the observed off-target effects. Adverse events because of RZV administration were rare but included Guillain-Barré syndrome (GBS), autoimmune encephalitis and autoimmune flares occurring after vaccination. However, there is insufficient evidence to indicate a causal relationship between RZV administration and these rare immune-mediated adverse effects, and post-marketing surveillance still support a favourable safety profile. Conclusions: Current evidence suggests that RZV administration confers numerous off-target benefits via VZV suppression and the immunomodulatory effects of the AS01B adjuvant. As clinical evidence remains observational, further investigation of the pleiotropic effects of RZV should be carried out to explore its role in reducing all-cause mortality.

42947523.titulo: Prophylactic Soraphen A Treatment Attenuates Western Diet-Exacerbated IMQ-Induced Psoriasiform Inflammation.
42947523.autores: Kao YS, Kommoss KS, … Sparwasser T (12 autores)
42947523.resumo: Psoriasis is a T-cell-mediated inflammatory disease amplified by metabolic stress. Acetyl-CoA carboxylase 1 (ACC1)-dependent fatty acid synthesis is required for IL-17-producing T cells. Here, we asked whether short-term systemic administration of soraphen A (SorA), a dual ACC1/2 inhibitor, modulates imiquimod (IMQ)-induced psoriasiform inflammation under normal diet (ND) and Western diet (WD) conditions. Female C57BL/6J mice were fed ND or WD for 12 weeks prior to daily intraperitoneal injections of SorA or vehicle for 10 days, followed by 5 days of topical IMQ to induce psoriasiform dermatitis. Disease severity was assessed by macroscopic, histological, transcriptional, and flow cytometric readouts. Prophylactic SorA administration had no measurable effect in ND-fed mice. In WD-fed mice, prophylactic SorA reduced erythema, back skin thickening, and epidermal hyperplasia, whereas scaling remained unchanged. Selected histological skin readouts were numerically lower, whereas the qPCR panel showed no statistically significant differences. In skin-draining lymph nodes, IL-17A+ CD4+ and CD8+ T-cell frequencies and numbers were significantly reduced, whereas γδT17 cells did not differ significantly. Hepatic steatosis scores were unchanged, but hepatic neutrophil infiltration was reduced. Under the present prophylactic regimen, systemic SorA administration was associated with modest attenuation of WD-exacerbated IMQ-induced psoriasiform inflammation. These findings support further preclinical evaluation of ACC-targeted immunometabolic interventions in metabolically aggravated psoriasiform inflammation.

42932696.titulo: Closing the Automation Gap in HPV-Based Cervical Cancer Screening: Independent External Validation of an AI Model for Dual-Stain Triage.
42932696.autores: Lahrmann B, Keil A, … Grabe N (20 autores)
42932696.resumo:
Primary human papillomavirus (HPV) screening has enabled scalable molecular detection in cervical cancer prevention, but downstream triage of HPV-positive individuals remains dependent on manual p16/Ki-67 dual-stain (DS) cytology interpretation. Although DS is guideline-endorsed and biologically well-defined, scalable implementation is limited by reader-dependent variability and lack of standardized automation.
We developed Cytoreader-Fusion, a transparent, ensemble-based AI system for automated slide-level DS classification within HPV-based screening workflows that produces well-calibrated probabilistic outputs. The model was trained on 1919 cases and evaluated under blinded honest-broker oversight on 9006 cases across four independent cohorts, including a fully independent post-lock external validation cohort (EXVC; n=4996). All preprocessing steps, aggregation rules, and decision parameters were prespecified and irreversibly locked prior to validation. Performance was evaluated against independently ascertained histologically confirmed cervical intraepithelial neoplasia grade 3 or worse (CIN 3+) (or anal intraepithelial neoplasia grade 3 or worse [AIN 3+]) end points rather than cytologic concordance. A single unified classifier was applied across both ThinPrep and SurePath preparations without platform-specific retraining.
Cytoreader-Fusion demonstrated stable and reproducible slide-level classification across imaging variability, preparation platforms, and clinical settings. Across blinded screening and referral cohorts, sensitivity and specificity were higher than atypical squamous cells of undetermined significance or worse (ASC-US+) Papanicolaou (Pap) cytology in HPV-based screening populations and comparable to or exceeded manual DS interpretation. In the fully independent post-lock cohort (n=4996), the locked system achieved a sensitivity of 88.3% (90% UI, 85.3%-91.3%) and a specificity of 54.4% (90% UI, 52.9%-55.9%) for detection of CIN 3+, without any model retraining, threshold tuning, or configuration adjustment after lock. Operating characteristics remained consistent across cohorts and preparation platforms.
This study establishes a high-stringency validation framework for clinically deployable artificial intelligence in population-based cancer screening. By combining prespecified algorithm locking, independent blinded evaluation under honest-broker supervision, end point-based validation against histologically confirmed disease, and cross-platform generalization, Cytoreader-Fusion demonstrates robust and scalable automation of DS triage within HPV-based screening programs. (Funded by the U.S. National Cancer Institute and others.).

42944114.titulo: Integrating Host Transcriptomics and Metagenomics in the Periparturient Dairy Cow: From Molecular Signatures to Host-Microbiome Interfaces.
42944114.autores: Ma Q, Tharwat M, … Khan MZ (6 autores)
42944114.resumo: The periparturient or transition period-roughly three weeks before to three weeks after calving-compresses the most severe metabolic, endocrine and immunological demands of the production cycle into a few weeks and accounts for most clinical disease and involuntary culling in dairy herds. Conventional surveillance relies on downstream indicators-non-esterified fatty acids, β-hydroxybutyrate, calcium and acute-phase proteins-that document failed adaptation without resolving its regulatory origins. Two omics platforms now close that gap. Transcriptomics shows that the liver, adipose tissue, mammary gland, endometrium, rumen epithelium and circulating leukocytes each execute a distinct, temporally ordered program organized around lipid mobilization, gluconeogenesis, endoplasmic reticulum stress, redox defense and inflammatory resolution, layered over a regulatory tier of non-coding RNAs. Metagenomics shows in parallel that rumen, hindgut, uterine, vaginal, teat-apex and colostrum communities are restructured by parturition and by the dietary shift into lactation, with reproducible dysbiotic signatures accompanying ketosis, fatty liver, metritis, endometritis and intramammary infection. Critically, the two layers are mechanistically coupled: microbial short-chain fatty acids, secondary bile acids, purine derivatives and amino acids reprogram hepatic and immune cell transcription, while host lipolysis, inflammation and mineral demand reshape community structure. This review synthesizes both groups of literature within a single framework, formalizes five host-microbiome interfaces supported by paired measurements and identifies the biomarker, nutritional and genetic-selection opportunities that emerge only when host and microbial evidence are read together.

42931155.titulo: Microbial Dysbiosis, Infection, and Immunometabolic Signaling in Polyendocrine Metabolic Ovarian Syndrome (Formerly PCOS).
42931155.autores: Nevins A, Stansbury N, … Zhong G (4 autores)
42931155.resumo: Polyendocrine metabolic ovarian syndrome (PMOS), recently proposed as a new name for polycystic ovary syndrome (PCOS), is a heterogeneous endocrine-metabolic disorder characterized by hyperandrogenism, ovulatory dysfunction, and variable ovarian morphology. Low-grade inflammation is common, but its initiating and sustaining factors differ among phenotypes. Microbial communities have emerged as potential modifiers of this inflammatory and metabolic environment. Human studies generally identify differences in gut microbial community structure between affected and unaffected women, although no universal taxonomic signature has been reproduced across regions, phenotypes, or analytic platforms. Mechanistic studies implicate altered intestinal barrier signaling, microbial metabolites, bile acid-interleukin-22 pathways, and immune-cell polarization; however, several influential pathways remain supported principally by animal models. Evidence for lower genital tract dysbiosis is more limited, and apparent associations may reflect hormonal state, menstrual irregularity, adiposity, medications, sexual exposures, or sampling methods. Evidence that specific infections cause PMOS/PCOS is sparse and inconsistent. Small serologic studies involving Chlamydia species and Helicobacter pylori do not establish temporality or causality. This review distinguishes dysbiosis from infection, evaluates human and experimental evidence, and proposes a bidirectional microbial-immune-metabolic-ovarian framework. A focused hypothesis involving interleukin-12-STAT4 signaling is also examined because it provides a specific, testable framework linking microbial or sterile inflammatory signaling to ovarian dysfunction. STAT4 can promote inflammatory T-helper-1 programs and granulosa-cell apoptosis in non-PCOS models, while estrogen can enhance STAT4 activation; nevertheless, direct human PMOS/PCOS evidence is currently absent, and the proposed pathway should not be interpreted as an established disease mechanism. Future studies require deep phenotyping, longitudinal multi-omics, compartment-specific sampling, standardized analysis, and mechanistic validation before microbiome-directed or immune-directed interventions can enter clinical care.

42928264.titulo: Itaconate-based hydrogels for immunomodulation and infection control: design strategies, biomedical applications, and translational challenges.
42928264.autores: Wang M, Wang J, … Yang H (6 autores)
42928264.resumo: Itaconate is a bioactive immunometabolite with anti-inflammatory, antioxidant, and antimicrobial properties. Its unsaturated dicarboxylic structure allows for versatile polymerization and chemical functionalization. These characteristics make it a promising building block for bioactive hydrogels. However, current research on itaconate-based hydrogels is fragmented across immunology, polymer chemistry, and biomedical engineering, with a lack of a unified design framework. In this review, we summarize the biological properties of itaconate and its derivatives relevant to biomaterial design, including immunomodulatory effects and antimicrobial activity. We categorize itaconate-based hydrogels into two main strategies: those directly fabricated from itaconate or its analogues, and those loaded with itaconate or itaconate derivatives such as 4-octyl itaconate (4-OI) and dimethyl itaconate (DMI). We explore the relationships between composition, crosslinking chemistry, responsiveness, biological functions, and therapeutic applications in drug delivery, tissue repair, inflammatory diseases, and anti-infective therapy. We also highlight critical limitations, including insufficient structure-function comparisons, overreliance on small-animal models, limited mechanistic validation, and challenges in manufacturing, stability, biosafety, and clinical translation. This review presents a conceptual framework for the rational design of itaconate-based hydrogels and outlines key priorities for advancing these materials toward clinical translation as bioactive and immunomodulatory hydrogel platforms.

42934422.titulo: NLRC3 deficiency exacerbates high-fat diet-induced enteric nervous system injury and colonic motility dysfunction in mice via activating NF-κB signaling pathway.
42934422.autores: Wang Y, Li Y, … Li YQ (6 autores)
42934422.revista: Cellular and molecular life sciences : CMLS
42934422.resumo: A high-fat diet (HFD) induces low-grade intestinal inflammation, thereby causing structural and functional impairments of the enteric nervous system (ENS). Nucleotide oligomerization domain (NOD)-like receptor (NLR) containing a caspase activation and recruitment domain 3 (NLRC3) participates in key pathophysiological processes related to inflammation, immunity, and proliferative diseases. However, the function of NLRC3 within the ENS remains to be clarified. This investigation was designed to characterize NLRC3 expression and distribution within the ENS and to elucidate its mechanism in modulating ENS injury. An HFD-induced low-grade colonic inflammation model was established in NLRC3 gene knockout (Nlrc3-/-) mice and wild-type (WT) C57BL/6J mice. The influence of NLRC3 on ENS architecture and motor function was assessed using morphological evaluation, molecular biological assays, and colonic motility analyses. The findings demonstrated that NLRC3 was primarily distributed within the cytoplasm of ENS neurons in mice, with HFD decreasing NLRC3 expression in enteric neurons. Relative to WT mice, HFD-treated Nlrc3-/- mice developed more pronounced ENS injury, characterized by enteric glial cells proliferation and activation, enteric neuronal loss accompanied by structural disruption, and a further delay in colonic transit function. NLRC3 deficiency exacerbated HFD-induced ENS injury and enteric neuronal apoptosis via nuclear factor-κB signaling pathway activation. These observations establish NLRC3 as a key negative regulator of neuroinflammatory responses in the ENS. As a negative regulatory pattern recognition receptor that links innate immunity with ENS signaling, NLRC3 may represent a promising therapeutic target.

42931812.titulo: Post-acute infection: before we forget it again.
42931812.resumo: Long COVID did not invent the post-acute phase of infection; it made it impossible to ignore. Acute infections are still often framed as time-limited events that end in recovery, deterioration or death, but this view fails to capture patients who remain biologically and clinically unwell after the acute infection has passed. The problem extends beyond SARS-CoV-2. Post-acute morbidity has been described after influenza, Epstein-Barr virus infection, Q fever, sepsis, and other infections, yet definitions, coding systems, and clinical pathways remain fragmented. We argue that post-acute infection should not be organized only by the initiating pathogen. Such pathogen-centric labels may be clinically tidy, but they risk producing heterogeneous cohorts, diluted biomarker signals, and disease-specific silos that obscure shared mechanisms of incomplete recovery. Instead, the field needs a second axis: the host-recovery state. Persistent inflammation, immune remodelling, loss of tolerance, antigenic stimulation, endothelial dysfunction, mitochondrial impairment, and tissue injury may represent overlapping immunometabolic failure modes across infections. Defining these states over time could help transform post-acute infection from a residual clinical label into a mechanism-informed framework for research, biomarkers, and care.

42936124.titulo: A modular in vitro multienzyme cascade for the sustainable synthesis of high-value vidarabine 5'-monophosphate from adenosine.
42936124.autores: Su W, Zhang X, … Liu Y (9 autores)
42936124.resumo: Nucleoside analogues such as vidarabine (Ara-A) are vital therapeutics but are often limited by poor pharmacokinetics. Its phosphorylated form, vidarabine 5'-monophosphate (Ara-AMP), offers improved solubility and is used as a clinical alternative, although it can be dephosphorylated to Ara-A in vivo. Here, we report a modular multienzyme cascade for the sustainable synthesis of Ara-AMP directly from adenosine. The cascade integrates three functional modules: a core module (PNP, PPM, and RpiA) for the conversion of adenosine to Ara-A, a driver module (dNKδ20) for the selective phosphorylation of Ara-A to Ara-AMP, and a support module (PPK) for ATP regeneration from low-cost ADP and polyphosphate. The use of dNKδ20, a mutant deoxyribonucleoside kinase with high selectivity for Ara-A over adenosine, is critical for minimizing the formation of AMP byproduct, which would otherwise complicate downstream processing. Under optimized conditions, the cascade achieved an 80.2% conversion of 1 mM adenosine to Ara-AMP in 4 h using 0.05 mM ADP. The modular design was also applicable to guanosine and inosine, affording the corresponding arabinosyl nucleotides, albeit with lower yields. This work establishes a sustainable biocatalytic platform for nucleoside analogues, exemplifying how enzyme promiscuity, thermodynamic driving, and cofactor recycling enable green pharmaceutical manufacturing.

42933978.titulo: Microtubules coordinate cellularization in a coenocytic relative of animals.
42933978.autores: Araújo M, Olivetta M, … Dudin O (9 autores)
42933978.resumo: Cellularization is the coordinated division of a multinucleate cell into many cells, a common life cycle transition across eukaryotes. In the best-studied model of this process, Drosophila melanogaster, cellularization requires actin and microtubule networks, as well as membrane vesicle delivery to drive the synchronous invagination of plasma membrane furrows. To identify unifying principles, we investigate cellularization in the ichthyosporean Sphaeroforma arctica, a close relative of animals with a multinucleate life cycle stage. Using live-cell imaging, ultrastructure expansion microscopy, and volume electron microscopy, we define the membrane, microtubule, and actin dynamics that accompany cellularization. Using pharmacological inhibitors and centrifugation, we show that the microtubule network positions nuclei evenly at the cortex, thereby specifying furrow positioning. Disrupting microtubules perturbed nuclear position, furrow spacing, and the efficiency of furrow ingression, leading eventually to cells of variable size and nuclear content. Our findings indicate that the microtubule network sets the spatial framework within which actomyosin and membrane delivery drive cellularization and establish S. arctica as a tractable model for comparative studies of this eukaryotic life cycle strategy.

42950046.titulo: Presynaptic filopodia form kinapses and promote convective membrane flow to sustain synchronous neurotransmitter release.
42950046.autores: Jain A, Dong R, … Ivanova D (13 autores)
42950046.resumo: Synaptic plasticity is the principal mechanism by which neural circuits compute and adapt. Presynaptic plasticity is traditionally regarded as a transient adaptation of the synaptic vesicle fusion and recycling machinery, whereas the role of structural remodeling of synaptic boutons remains unclear. Here, we demonstrate a mechanical coupling between presynaptic structural remodeling and synaptic efficacy. We find that dynamic presynaptic filopodia emerge during active synaptic transmission and deform synaptic boutons while forming transient contacts with postsynaptic structures, which we term neuronal kinapses. Filopodia formation is activity dependent and occurs in intact circuits and human brain. Mechanistically, filopodial growth induces convective in-plane membrane flow toward the filopodium, accelerating release site clearance, a process associated with sustained release probability during repeated synaptic vesicle fusion. As a result, filopodia formation favors an increase in synchronous over asynchronous neurotransmitter release. These results indicate that presynaptic structural remodeling can alter the spatial organization of neurotransmission and, through the membrane flow it generates, modulate its temporal precision.

42949396.titulo: Pressure Engineering through Silica Nanoconfinement for Melting Point Elevation of Gold Nanoparticles.
42949396.autores: Choi CW, Choi JH, … Choi SY (5 autores)
42949396.resumo: Au nanoparticles (NPs) are inherently thermally unstable at elevated temperatures because their large surface-to-volume ratio promotes melting, migration, and coalescence. Here, we demonstrate that silica (SiO2) nanoconfinement thermodynamically elevates the melting point (Tm) of Au NPs through confinement-induced compressive pressure. Atomic-resolution in situ heating scanning transmission electron microscopy (STEM) combined with local Fourier crystallinity mapping reveals that bare Au NPs lose crystallinity at 1,000 °C, whereas SiO2-encapsulated Au cores (Au@SiO2) remain crystalline. Accordingly, in situ heating TEM shows bare Au NPs progressively merge while Au@SiO2 remain structurally isolated. Temperature-dependent lattice-parameter measurements reveal significantly suppressed thermal expansion of confined Au cores, corresponding to an estimated compressive stress of 4-5 GPa. Finite-element simulations support this estimate, showing that SiO2 shell shrinkage generates several-GPa core pressure, with thicker shells producing higher pressure and greater Tm elevation. These findings establish nanoconfinement-induced pressure as a general thermomechanical strategy for stabilizing metallic NPs under extreme thermal environments.

42949345.titulo: Dual-Phosphorylated Pumpkin Seed Protein Pickering Emulsions: Structural Evolution, Interfacial Regulation, and Coffee Creamer Application Quality.
42949345.autores: Huang J, Wang D, … Chen J (6 autores)
42949345.revista: Journal of agricultural and food chemistry
42949345.resumo: Pumpkin seed protein (PSP) was modified with sodium tripolyphosphate (STP) and sodium trimetaphosphate (STMP) to improve Pickering emulsions. Phosphorylation increased with STMP content but plateaued at high ratios. Mass spectrometry identified phosphorylated Ser and Thr residues, while 31P NMR indicated multiple phosphorus environments. Modification altered protein conformation and surface charge, reduced particle size, and improved dispersion without major subunit degradation. Although emulsifying activity decreased, emulsion stability increased; mixed-phosphate treatments generally produced finer droplets and better resistance to centrifugal destabilization than single-phosphate treatments. A 4:1 STP/STMP ratio combined small droplet size with favorable wettability and interfacial adsorption, whereas higher STMP content did not consistently improve overall performance. In coffee beverages, increasing emulsion incorporation intensified phase separation and altered color and flavor. At a 1:9 emulsion-to-coffee ratio, phosphorylated PSP emulsion improved perceived body and smoothness while retaining coffee aroma, outperforming commercial creamer in balance and supporting its potential use as a plant-based food.

42946931.titulo: Design, Characterization and In Vivo Evaluation of Rifaximin-Loaded Chitosan Nanoparticles for Potential Colonic Drug Delivery in Irritable Bowel Syndrome.
42946931.resumo: This study aimed to develop rifaximin (RFX) loaded chitosan (CS)-tripolyphosphate (TPP) nanoparticles for potential colonic delivery as a drug delivery system for the management of irritable bowel syndrome (IBS). Nanoparticles were prepared using the ionotropic gelation method and optimized by varying stirring speed, TPP concentration, and polymer-to-drug ratio. The optimized formulation (F41) exhibited a particle size of 262.4 ± 24.3 nm, a polydispersity index (PDI) of 0.389 ± 0.033, a zeta potential of + 9.91 ± 0.94 mV, and an encapsulation efficiency (EE%) of 94.75 ± 0.04%. In vitro release studies demonstrated nearly complete drug release within 36 h, which was faster compared to other formulations (52-64 h). Scanning electron microscopy (SEM) confirmed spherical morphology, while differential scanning calorimetry (DSC) and Fourier transform infrared spectroscopy (FT-IR) analyses indicated successful drug encapsulation without chemical interaction. In vivo evaluation using a chronic restraint stress (CRS) induced IBS model showed that F41 significantly improved physiological parameters, including reduced fecal water content (20.655 ± 23.494%), increased body weight gain (22.716 ± 3.903%), and a decreased disease activity index (p < 0.05). These findings indicate that, the optimized nanoparticle system demonstrated favorable physicochemical properties, sustained drug release, and improved therapeutic outcomes. Owing to the cationic nature of CS, the system may also provide enhanced interaction with colonic mucus, potentially contributing to prolonged local residence. These findings suggest that the developed formulation represents promising approach for potential colonic delivery of RFX in IBS management; however, further studies are required to directly evaluate its mucoadhesive properties and underlying mechanisms.

42946190.titulo: Revitalizing simultaneous nitrification, endogenous denitrification and phosphorus removal under carbon starvation: Redox mediator-modulated electron transfer and metabolic coordination.
42946190.autores: Chen H, Chai Z, … Zheng M (6 autores)
42946190.resumo: The simultaneous nitrification, endogenous denitrification and phosphorus removal (SNEDPR) process provides a resource-efficient paradigm for synergistic nutrient removal. However, its efficacy can be severely constrained by limited electron-donor availability and inefficient intracellular electron transfer under low carbon-to-nitrogen (C/N) ratios. Herein, we demonstrate that anthraquinone-2-sulfonate (AQS) serves as an effective redox mediator to alleviate these electron-transfer limitations. Under severe carbon-limited conditions, with an influent C/N ratio of 3.24±0.11, supplementation with 0.3 mmol/L AQS successfully restored the deteriorated system, recovering total inorganic nitrogen (TIN) removal efficiency to 96.57±0.87% while sustaining robust phosphorus removal (96.47±2.68%). Batch kinetic assays showed that AQS increased electron transfer system activity (ETSA) by over 100%, accompanied by enhanced nitrification-related activity, endogenous denitrification and phosphorus uptake. Integrated metagenomic and metatranscriptomic analyses further revealed transcriptional responses consistent with an electron-shuttling role of AQS, including enhanced ETC-associated electron-transfer potential and increased transcription of downstream denitrification enzymes. ATP synthase-related transcription was also enhanced, indicating an increased potential for PMF-coupled cellular energy conservation. Consequently, increased transcription was observed for key functional genes involved in nitrification (amoABC, nxrAB), denitrification (narGHI, napAB, nirKS, nosZ), and polyphosphate synthesis (ppk). Furthermore, AQS-amended operation was associated with microbial community succession toward a more specialized consortium, in which comammox, Thauera and Candidatus Accumulibacter clade ⅡC were associated with nitrification, endogenous denitrification, and denitrifying phosphorus removal, respectively. Although practical translation will require effective retention or recovery of soluble AQS, these findings demonstrate the potential of AQS-enhanced SNEDPR under carbon-limited conditions and provide multi-omics evidence linking improved nutrient removal with increased electron-transfer activity and coordinated microbial metabolic responses.

42946042.titulo: Effects of Irrigation Protocols on Dentin-Root Interface Integrity and Sealer Penetration after Minimally Invasive versus Conventional Instrumentation: An Ex Vivo Analysis.
42946042.autores: Scardini IL, Masiero AV, … Teixeira FB (5 autores)
42946042.resumo:
This study compared the effects of ultrasonic activation (UA), laser-activated irrigation (LAI), and the GentleWave® system (GW) on root dentin and sealer penetration (SP) after minimally invasive (MI) and conventional (CT) instrumentation techniques.
One hundred extracted human mandibular premolars were allocated according to the instrumentation technique. Forty teeth (n=20) were analyzed for root dentin morphology using scanning electron microscopy (SEM), and 60 teeth (n=30) were assessed for SP using confocal laser scanning microscopy (CLSM). For SEM analysis, specimens were further subdivided by irrigation protocol, including a negative control group (n=5). For SP evaluation, teeth were subdivided by irrigation protocol (n=10) and obturated with EndoSequence® BC Sealer labeled with 0.003% Fluo-3. Data were analyzed using the Kruskal-Wallis test and Dunn's post hoc test (p < 0.05).
No significant differences in smear layer (SL) scores were found between CT and MI when the same irrigation technique was compared. In CT-prepared teeth, the control group exhibited higher SL than the irrigation groups, except in the middle third, where the results were comparable to those of UA. In MI-prepared teeth, GW showed lower SL scores than LAI in the cervical third (p < 0.05). In the apical third of MI-prepared canals, GW and LAI were associated with greater sealer penetration area and maximum depth than UA (p < 0.05). Dentin erosion was observed in 15 of 120 (12.5%) imageswith 10 images from the UA group and 5 from the LAI group. No erosion was observed in the GW group.
Under the experimental conditions evaluated, no morphological signs of dentin erosion were observed with the GW protocol, and GW and LAI were associated with greater apical SP than UA following MI instrumentation. Because the protocols differed in irrigant volume, exposure time, and sequence, these findings cannot be attributed specifically to the activation technologies.

42937039.titulo: 3D Reconstruction of Nanoparticle Distribution in Tumor Spheroids With Volume Electron Microscopy.
42937039.autores: Bottone D, Gerken LRH, … Herrmann IK (12 autores)
42937039.resumo: Spatially resolved characterization of nanomaterial (NM) distribution within cellular ultrastructure is essential for understanding NM fate and activity in biological systems. Volume electron microscopy (vEM) is uniquely positioned to address this challenge, yet fully documented quantitative pipelines that simultaneously segment NMs and cellular structures remain scarce. Here, an end-to-end analytical pipeline is presented based on the example of serial block-face scanning electron microscopy (SBF-SEM) data of tumor spheroids containing nanoparticles (NPs). A hybrid segmentation strategy is adopted, comprising a fine-tuned Cellpose-SAM model for cells and nuclei, and an empirical Bayes approach for AuNPs. The fine-tuned model outperforms both the pre-trained baseline and the benchmark experiments in Amira, and shows good generalization to 2D EM datasets of varying sample types, suggesting potential as a general-purpose segmentation model for electron microscopy. Full 3D reconstruction of NP distributions reveals preferential clustering in the perinuclear region, with a median nucleus-to-NP distance of 2.57 μ m  and NM uptake spanning several orders of magnitude across cells. Furthermore, morphological analysis of segmented cells and nuclei using 3D shape descriptors and local curvature metrics provides quantitative access to features inaccessible from single sections. Together, these results establish a reproducible, open framework for the joint quantitative analysis of NM distribution and cellular morphology in vEM data.

42935442.titulo: Engineering zero thermal expansion over a wide temperature range in PbTiO3-based ferroelectrics.
42935442.autores: Pan Z, Ye M, … Long Y (11 autores)
42935442.resumo: Thermal expansion mismatches in precision optics, aerospace, and electronics can lead to delamination and fatigue, driving urgent demand for zero thermal expansion (ZTE) materials. At present, the majority of single-phase ZTE materials only function effectively below 500 K, limiting potential applications in many critical fields. Herein, we employ high-pressure and high-temperature synthesis to develop (1 - x)PbTiO3-xBi(Cu3/4W1/4)O3 perovskite ferroelectrics, utilizing spontaneous volume ferroelectrostriction to achieve an ultrawide ZTE regime from 300 to 725 K. In situ synchrotron X-ray diffraction tracks the lattice contraction and phase stability, while transmission electron microscopy provides insights into atomic-scale A/B-site cation displacements and tetragonal distortions. First-principles calculations reveal that polar ferroelectric-active Bi3+, Cu2+, and W6+ ions synergistically reorganize electron density to reinforce ferroelectric distortion, while Cu-derived van Hove singularities near the Fermi level dominate the density of states and govern the elastic anomalies linked to the ultrawide ZTE behaviors. This study extends the scope of high-temperature ZTE materials and establishes a ferroelectric-active ion-doping strategy to engineer thermal expansion.

42933572.titulo: Inositol hexakisphosphate kinase 1 regulates polyphosphate synthesis by maintaining V-ATPase-dependent secretory granule acidification.
42933572.resumo: Polyphosphate (polyP), a linear polymer of orthophosphate residues, is enriched in secretory granules in specialised mammalian cell types including platelets and mast cells. Although polyP released during activation and degranulation of these cells has been shown to promote blood clotting and inflammation, little is known about the mechanisms governing polyP synthesis in these granules. In mice, the loss of IP6K1, an enzyme that catalyses the production of 5-InsP7, has been shown to result in depletion of platelet polyP and impaired hemostasis. Here, we use the rat mast cell line RBL-2H3 as a model to study the regulation of polyP synthesis in secretory granules. By monitoring real-time polyP synthesis in isolated mast cell granules, we demonstrate that ATP is the substrate fuelling granule polyP production. By the use of inhibitors, we show that accumulation of polyP in granules requires an intact transmembrane proton gradient maintained by vacuolar H+ATPase (V-ATPase). In RBL-2H3 cells, depletion of IP6K1 led to a substantial reduction in cellular polyP levels and defective accumulation of polyP, serotonin, and tryptase inside granules. Cells with reduced IP6K1 showed a profound loss of granule acidification, correlating with downregulated levels of V1 subunits of V-ATPase. Adding back active or catalytically inactive IP6K1 rescued the expression of V-ATPase V1 subunits, reversed granule deacidification, and restored polyP levels in IP6K1-depleted cells. Together, these data unveil a role for IP6K1 in maintaining granule pH and thereby supporting polyP synthesis in mammals.
42933572.metodo: Ensaios enzimáticos de IP6K combinados a ensaios fluorimétricos com DAPI e extração de polifosfato de cadeia curta/longa.
42933572.implicacao: Mostra a regulação da síntese de polifosfato pela via da IP6K1 e V-ATPase lisossomal, conectando acidificação de vacúolos/acidocalcisomos com homeostase de fosfato.

42933517.titulo: Microstructure-driven opacity of semi-permeable membranes in push-pull osmotic tablets and its impact on manufacturability and drug release.
42933517.autores: Lee HD, Punia A, … Lallow E (10 autores)
42933517.resumo: Push-pull osmotic pump tablets provide controlled, zero-order drug release through water diffusion across a semi-permeable membrane and extrusion of the drug in the active layer through a laser-drilled orifice. The membranes must be mechanically robust to channel the internal osmotic pressure towards drug extrusion. The study reports an instance in which the solvent coating produced opaque cellulose acetate/PEG3350 semi-permeable membranes. This reduced the visual contrast between the push and pull layers-creating a potential risk for accurate laser drilling-and led to incomplete dissolution of investigational drug MK-8189 after 24 h. Scanning electron microscopy, light microscopy, differential scanning calorimetry, nanoindentation, x-ray micro-computed tomography, and dissolution testing were used to identify the origin and impact of the opacity. Results showed that opacity was driven by coating-induced membrane porosity, rather than phase separation. Although both presentations retained the zero-order release kinetics, the opaque membranes were more porous and mechanically weaker-exhibiting a three-fold increase in the number of pores, a statistically significant increase in pore size distribution, and a 26% reduction Young's Modulus than the transparent membranes. During dissolution, the softer opaque membranes deformed substantially, increasing internal tablet volume and reducing the fraction of swelling capacity available to drive the drug extrusion. Consequently, opaque tablets plateaued at ∼85% drug release, whereas transparent tablets achieved complete release. By understanding the edges of failure for the solvent coating process, optimization of the air-to-spray ratio, product temperature, and pattern air pressure eliminated the microstructural porosity.

42933403.titulo: Amyloid-mediated RNA uptake by sperm for embryonic delivery.
42933403.autores: Mallen WS, Zabello N, … Fitzpatrick AWP (13 autores)
42933403.resumo: Seminal fluid (SF) RNA is essential for embryonic development, but the mechanism by which extracellular RNA is transferred from SF to sperm remains unclear. Here, we identify a role for functional amyloid fibrils in SF that bind and traffic RNA to mammalian sperm and, upon fertilization, to the zygote. We show that highly cationic peptides in SF phase separate with RNA to form amyloid fibrils. Cryo-electron tomography (cryo-ET), volume electron microscopy (volume EM), and fluorescence live-cell imaging reveal that these amyloid fibrils are internalized by mammalian sperm. Furthermore, biophysical and in vitro fertilization (IVF) experiments show that amyloid-bound RNA reaches the zygote, where molecular chaperones can control RNA dissociation from amyloid fibrils. Our work uncovers a mechanism for RNA trafficking from SF to the zygote, establishing amyloid fibrils as potential tools for RNA delivery during fertilization.
42933403.metodo: Criotomografia eletrônica (Cryo-ET) e microscopia eletrônica de volume (volume EM).
42933403.implicacao: Visualiza por Cryo-ET e volume EM a translocação de RNA mediada por fibrilas amilóides, inspirando estratégias biomiméticas de entrega de dsRNA em invertebrados.

42931877.titulo: Characterization and anticancer activity of green-synthesized and highly stable ginger-derived silver nanoparticles: In vitro and in vivo studies.
42931877.autores: Elghaznawy MM, El Sadda RR, Saad EA
42931877.resumo: Ginger (Zingiber officinale) is a common spice with therapeutic potential due to its bioactive compounds and was used for the green synthesis of ginger-derived silver nanoparticles (G-AgNPs). The cytotoxic, antioxidant, and pro-apoptotic effects of the synthesized G-AgNPs were evaluated against HepG-2, MCF-7, and WI-38 cell lines. Gas chromatography-mass spectrometry (GC-MS) analysis identified 36 phytochemicals, with major components including α-zingiberene (37.88%), β-sesquiphellandrene (15.65%), 6-gingerol (10.68%), α-farnesene (8.04%), β-bisabolene (7.83%), α-curcumene (6.96%), 8-gingerol (0.96%), and 6-shogaol (0.95%). Characterization of G-AgNPs using ultraviolet-visible spectroscopy (UV-Vis), Fourier-transform infrared spectroscopy (FT-IR), zeta-potential analysis (- 46.17 ± 1.42 mV), and transmission electron microscopy (TEM) revealed spherical nanoparticles with an average diameter of 10.44 nm. Cytotoxicity assays demonstrated greater inhibition of HepG-2 and MCF-7 cell viability than of WI-38 cells, with IC₅₀ values of 1.20 ± 0.03 µM (4.51 ± 0.11 µg/mL) and 1.49 ± 0.05 µM (5.60 ± 0.19 µg/mL), respectively, compared with 2.49 ± 0.07 µM for WI-38 cells. Treatment with G-AgNPs significantly increased caspase-3-associated protein levels in both HepG-2 (13.81 ± 0.35 ng/mg protein) and MCF-7 (42.83 ± 1.47 ng/mg protein), and decreased Bcl-2 expression (HepG-2: 2.12 ± 0.14 ng/mg protein; MCF-7: 3.17 ± 0.03 ng/mg protein). However, given the known deficiency of functional caspase-3 in MCF-7 cells, the observed increase likely reflects caspase-3-immunoreactive protein rather than active enzyme. Antioxidant evaluation demonstrated free radical scavenging activity (IC₅₀ = 28.96 µg/mL), comparable to ascorbic acid (IC₅₀ = 14.03 µg/mL), along with significant CT- DNA intercalation. In vivo, treatment of Ehrlich ascites carcinoma (EAC)-bearing mice with G-AgNPs significantly reduced abdominal circumference, ascitic fluid volume, and viable tumor cell counts while increasing the percentage increase in lifespan by 93.3%. G-AgNPs also improved liver and kidney function, increased hepatic GSH, SOD, TAC, and catalase levels relative to untreated EAC-bearing mice, reduced oxidative stress markers (MDA and NO), and ameliorated liver histopathological alterations, with fewer adverse effects than cisplatin. The findings indicate that G-AgNPs possess potential anticancer activity and preliminary differential cytotoxicity toward HepG2 cells compared with non-cancerous cells. Further toxicological and in vivo investigations are required to establish their safety and therapeutic applicability.

42929629.titulo: Lighting Up upon Phosphate Binding: Supramolecular Assembly of Ir(III) Complexes for Luminescent Sensing and Molecular Logic Gate.
42929629.autores: Ghosh R, Rashid A, … Ghosh P (8 autores)
42929629.resumo: Inorganic phosphates and polyphosphates are vital to biological function, and their dysregulation is linked to metabolic and renal disorders, driving the need for selective, sensitive, and reversible luminescent probes for their detection. Here, we report three bis-heteroleptic Ir(III) complexes (IC1-IC3) bearing imidazole-functionalized ancillary ligands that show selective "switch-on" emission toward phosphate (H2PO4-) and pyrophosphate (HP2O73-) over competing anions, driven by C-H···O hydrogen bonding between imidazole donors and phosphate oxygens. Variable-temperature studies (80-300 K) reveal long-lived phosphorescence (τ = 1.4 μs at 80 K) governed by restricted intramolecular motion and a large singlet-triplet gap. Emission analysis shows mixed 3MLCT character for IC1/IC2, while nitro-substituted IC3 displays combined 3MLCT/3LLCT character. The interaction of IC1 with H2PO4- gives a 1:2 binding stoichiometry (K = 8.0 × 105 M-1) and detection limits of 35.4 nM and 16.3 nM for H2PO4- and HP2O73-, respectively. NMR and DLS studies indicate that phosphate binding triggers hydrogen-bond-mediated supramolecular aggregation, rigidifying the excited state and enhancing emission, while Zn2+ reversibly quenches this response, enabling switch-on/switch-off behavior applicable to molecular logic gate. Phosphate binding extends IC1's excited-state lifetime from 91.68 to 357.66 ns. These Ir(III) complexes thus emerge as a tunable platform for selective, reversible phosphate sensing.

42928641.titulo: Depth-Aware Machine Learning for 3D Reconstruction of Fibrous Porous Electrodes by FIB-SEM Tomography.
42928641.autores: Bozal-Ginesta C, Bissattini Alessi C, … Battaglia C (7 autores)
42928641.resumo: Quantitative three-dimensional reconstruction of porous polymers with sub-micrometer feature sizes is central to understanding and designing electrochemical interfaces and membranes. However, focused ion beam-scanning electron microscopy tomography combined with conventional segmentation techniques cannot readily reconstruct complex disordered morphologies such as fibers. Standard segmentation workflows misclassify out-of-plane material as in-plane material, distorting the reconstructed pore network, fiber connectivity, and interface area. Here, we introduce an annotation-free, depth-aware machine-learning framework that combines monocular depth estimation, trained on macroscale images, with unsupervised clustering to separate in-plane polymer cross-sections from subsurface contributions in serial FIB-SEM tomography images. Applied to copper-coated electrospun poly(vinylidene fluoride-co-hexafluoropropylene) fiber mats, the approach produces 3D reconstructions that preserve fibrous morphology more faithfully than conventional supervised and unsupervised segmentation. Quantitative validation against capillary flow porometry, pycnometry, and high-resolution wide-angle X-ray computed tomography demonstrates improved agreement across pore cross-section diameter, fiber volume ratio, and Cu depth decrease metrics. This work establishes depth-aware segmentation as a transferable strategy from real-scale to nanoscale imaging, requiring no labeled training data and enabling accurate 3D segmentation and reconstruction from SEM images. This approach opens a path toward more reliable structure-property relationships in disordered porous polymer materials.

42939250.titulo: Nanoscale Characterization of Microscopically Layered Bone in the Russian Sturgeon Pectoral Fin Spine: A 3D FIB-SEM Study.
42939250.revista: Animals : an open access journal from MDPI
42939250.resumo: Dermal bone, the earliest known form of bone, develops without a cartilage precursor and persists in extant fish species. The pectoral fin spine (PFS) is a dermal bone located at the leading edge of the pectoral fin of sturgeons, where it is exposed to loading associated with locomotion. The peripheral region and dermal osteons of the PFS both appear layered at lower magnification; however, collagen organization in load-bearing fish skeletal elements remains incompletely characterized at the nanoscale. The aim of this study is to characterize the 3D nanostructure of the layered peripheral and osteonal bone forming the PFS in Russian sturgeons using focused ion beam-scanning electron microscopy (FIB-SEM). In the dermal osteons, bone forms concentric layers around a central canal at lower magnification, and at the nanoscale, the calcified collagen fibrils within these layers have preferential orientations that change in a clockwise-anticlockwise fanning pattern, consistent with lamellar bone. In contrast, the examined peripheral bone, which also appears layered at low magnification, is composed mainly of unidirectional calcified collagen fibrils aligned with the long axis of the PFS. Within the examined peripheral volumes, no comparable nanoscale lamellar pattern was detected, and the predominant fibril organization was consistent with parallel-fibered bone. Groups of voids associated with unidentified fibrillar material were also observed in the examined peripheral volumes; the voids were oriented approximately normal to the long axis of the PFS. We conclude that regions appearing layered at lower magnification can differ markedly at the nanoscale, and that the lamellar organization seen in dermal osteons raises questions about its evolutionary origin.

42942706.titulo: Bromide Sequestration Using a Low-Cost Hybrid Composite of Calcium, Activated Carbon, Kaolin, and Starch.
42942706.resumo: Bromide in source waters promotes the formation of toxic brominated disinfection byproducts during chlorination and ozonation, necessitating efficient, affordable pretreatment materials. This study developed a low-cost hybrid composite, denoted Calcium-Activated Carbon-Kaolin-Starch (CAKS) composite, from kaolin, activated carbon, a calcium precursor and starch through starch-assisted consolidation followed by calcination under nitrogen. The synthesized material was characterized by Fourier-transform infrared spectroscopy, X-ray diffraction, nitrogen adsorption-desorption analysis, scanning electron microscopy, and energy-dispersive X-ray spectroscopy. CAKS exhibited a heterogeneous mesoporous structure with a Brunauer-Emmett-Teller surface area of 212.5 m2 g-1, a pore volume of 0.384 cm3 g-1, and an average pore diameter of 7.2 nm. Batch adsorption experiments showed that bromide uptake was strongly dependent on solution pH, adsorbent dosage, contact time, initial concentration, agitation speed, temperature, and the presence of competing ions. Maximum removal of approximately 97.3% was achieved at pH 5, close to the apparent point of zero charge of 5.5. Adsorption was rapid during the first 60 min and approached equilibrium after 90-120 min. The experimental adsorption capacity increased with increasing bromide concentration, reaching approximately 40.0 mg g-1 at an initial bromide concentration of 200 mg L-1. Equilibrium data were best described by the Langmuir model, which yielded a model-estimated maximum adsorption capacity of 81.30 mg g-1. Kinetic data were described best by the pseudo-second-order model, although film diffusion and intraparticle diffusion also contributed to the overall uptake process. Equilibrium data indicated heterogeneous adsorption behavior, while thermodynamic analysis suggested that bromide adsorption was thermodynamically favorable under the investigated conditions. Regeneration with 0.1 M Sodium hydroxide and reuse over five adsorption-desorption cycles was also evaluated. Results were obtained under controlled laboratory conditions.

42943818.titulo: Interfacial Engineering of Fe3O4/Biochar via CMC Bridging for Durable Lithium/Sodium-Ion Storage.
42943818.autores: Li H, Yang Z, … Xia H (5 autores)
42943818.resumo: The development of cost-effective and durable anode materials derived from renewable biomass is essential for practical lithium- and sodium-ion batteries (LIBs/SIBs). However, conventional strategies for integrating high-capacity metal oxides with biomass carbon often suffer from weak oxide-carbon adhesion, nanoparticle aggregation, and large volume changes during cycling. To overcome these limitations, we present an interfacial engineering approach in which carboxymethyl cellulose (CMC) serves as a molecular bridge to anchor Fe3O4 nanoparticles in situ onto ginkgo branch-derived biochar (GBC). The abundant hydroxyl and carboxyl groups of CMC simultaneously guide uniform Fe3O4 nucleation and create a molecular bridge that mediates interfacial chemical interactions that facilitate charge transfer while accommodating volume strain. Structural and compositional analyses confirm the formation of CMC/Fe3O4/GBC with well-dispersed nanocrystals, a hierarchically porous architecture, and magnetic responsiveness. As an anode, CMC/Fe3O4/GBC delivers 256 mAh/g at 2000 mA/g in SIBs, substantially higher than that of bare GBC and unmodified Fe3O4/GBC. Comparable durability is observed in LIBs, where the composite retains 297 mAh/g after 2000 cycles at the same rate. Kinetic studies using cyclic voltammetry, galvanostatic intermittent titration technique, and electrochemical impedance spectroscopy reveal that CMC bridging enhances pseudocapacitive contribution and accelerates ion diffusion. Post-cycling X-ray photoelectron spectroscopy and transmission electron microscopy further confirm the preserved electrode integrity. These results establish a scalable interfacial modification strategy for biomass-derived magnetic composites toward durable alkali-ion storage.

42940186.titulo: Antitumor Activity of a Bupleurum chinense-Derived Vesicle-like Particle Preparation in MOC1 Oral Squamous Cell Carcinoma Models.
42940186.autores: Li S, Zhang G, … Ge W (7 autores)
42940186.resumo: Background/Objectives: This study evaluated the antitumor activity of a Bupleurum chinense-derived extracellular vesicle-like particle (BC-EVLP) preparation in MOC1 oral squamous cell carcinoma (OSCC) models. Methods: Fresh roots were processed by differential centrifugation, filtration, ultracentrifugation, and sucrose density-gradient separation. The preparation was characterized by transmission electron microscopy, nanoparticle tracking analysis, and total protein measurement. Cellular association, viability, ROS-associated fluorescence, mitochondrial membrane potential, and Annexin V-FITC/PI staining were assessed. Cell viability was also compared after exposure to equal added volumes of the preparation or pre-gradient ultracentrifugation supernatant. Female C57BL/6 mice bearing syngeneic MOC1 tumors received peritumoral treatment every 3 days for 14 days, followed by tumor histology. Results: The preparation contained nanoscale vesicle-like structures, with median and mean particle diameters of 162.0 and 191.9 nm. DiI-associated fluorescence was detected in MOC1 cells after 4 h. Treatment reduced cell viability and was associated with increased DCF fluorescence, a lower JC-1 red/green ratio, and increased Annexin V-positive fractions. The BC-EVLP preparation reduced cell viability more than the supernatant at equal added volumes, although the higher-volume supernatant treatment retained partial activity. High-dose treatment attenuated tumor growth in vivo, and representative tumor sections showed less densely cellular areas. Conclusions: The BC-EVLP preparation exhibited antitumor activity in the tested MOC1 models. The active constituents and the relative contributions of vesicular and non-vesicular components remain unresolved.

42942687.titulo: Sustainable Hybrid Flame-Retardant Architectures for LDPE: Effects of Waste-Derived Cellulose, SiO2, and APP/ADA.
42942687.autores: Ruiz-Martínez ARY, Cabrera-Álvarez EN, … Contreras-López D (6 autores)
42942687.resumo: This study evaluates the flame retardant efficiency of hybrid systems based on natural cellulose extracted from agricultural wastes (pecan nutshell and guayule), combined with azodicarbonamide (ADA), porous silicon dioxide (SiO2) scaffolds, and ammonium polyphosphate (APP), incorporated into low-density polyethylene (LDPE). The waste-derived cellulose fractions were isolated via alkaline extraction and steam explosion, yielding microfibrils that preserved native lignin fractions. Porous SiO2 particles were modified through the adsorption of ADA and APP, which in turn decorated the surface of the cellulose particles. Hybrid LDPE composites containing 20 wt% of total additives were melt-compounded and characterized. Thermogravimetric analysis (TGA) revealed an early intumescent activation that promoted robust charring, achieving final char residue yields up to 9.5 wt% for the pecan nutshell composite. Horizontal UL-94 and cone calorimeter tests demonstrated the complete elimination of hazardous flaming melt-dripping across all formulated hybrid systems, accompanied by a significant reduction in the burning rate to 18.3 mm/min and a 45% reduction in PHRR for the pecan nutshell-derived compound, consistent with a protective contribution of the multifunctional particles in the condensed phase, significantly outperforming its commercial nanocellulose counterparts. Cone calorimetry highlighted a drastic flattening of the peak heat release rate (PHRR) kinetics of composites. FTIR, TEM and TGA analyses confirmed the formation of a APP-ADA-loaded SiO2 particle scaffold ("grenade-like" morphology), with combustion-residue FTIR and SEM/EDS supporting a protective contribution in the condensed phase.

42942665.titulo: Upcycling Used Tyre Rubber into Carbon Adsorbents: Effect of Physical Activation on Porous Structure and Comparative Evaluation for p-Chlorophenol Removal.
42942665.autores: Troca-Torrado C, Alexandre-Franco MF, … Gómez-Serrano V (5 autores)
42942665.resumo: The porous architecture of carbons derived from polymeric waste is largely governed by the physical activation atmosphere. In this work, used tyre rubber (UTR) was converted into carbonaceous adsorbents by pyrolysis followed by physical activation in air, CO2 or steam. The influence of the activation route on porous structure, surface chemistry and adsorption performance was systematically investigated. The materials were characterised by N2 adsorption at -196 °C, mercury intrusion porosimetry, scanning electron microscopy (SEM), FT-IR spectroscopy and point-of-zero-charge (pHpzc) measurements. The resulting materials were evaluated for the removal of p-chlorophenol from aqueous solution and comparatively assessed against three commercial carbon materials. Steam activation proved to be the most effective treatment, increasing the BET surface area from 64 to 344 m2 g-1 and the micropore volume from 0.05 to 0.23 cm3 g-1 while generating a hierarchical micro-/mesoporous structure that significantly enhanced pore accessibility and mass transport. Among the UTR-derived carbons, the steam-activated sample exhibited the highest equilibrium p-Cp uptake and adsorption kinetics approaching those of a commercial activated carbon despite its lower specific surface area. Kinetic and equilibrium analyses demonstrated that adsorption performance depends not only on the extent of microporosity but also on pore accessibility and network connectivity, highlighting the critical role of transport mesoporosity in facilitating molecular diffusion towards adsorption sites. The adsorption results are consistent with an important contribution from accessible microporosity, while π-π interactions between p-chlorophenol and aromatic carbon domains may also contribute. These findings demonstrate that tailoring porous structure through physical activation provides an effective strategy for transforming UTR into high-performance carbon adsorbents and establishes robust processing-structure-property relationships that can guide the rational design of waste-derived carbon adsorbents.

42941069.titulo: Effect of Build Orientation on the Electrical, Thermal, and Mechanical Properties of PA12 Fabricated by Selective Laser Sintering.
42941069.autores: Huang L, Tu S, … Li H (5 autores)
42941069.resumo: Selective laser sintering (SLS) provides a promising route for the rapid fabrication of polymeric insulating components with complex geometries. However, its layer-by-layer manufacturing process inherently introduces structural anisotropy, which may significantly affect the electrical, thermal, and mechanical properties of the printed materials. In this study, polyamide 12 (PA12) specimens fabricated by SLS at different printing orientations were systematically investigated for dielectric properties, volume resistivity, DC and AC breakdown strength, tensile properties, and thermal conductivity. Scanning electron microscopy and X-ray microscopy were further employed to characterize the microstructure and clarify the origin of the anisotropic behavior. The results show that SLS-printed PA12 exhibits pronounced orientation-dependent properties. As the printing angle increases from 0° to 90°, the volume resistivity and DC breakdown strength generally decrease. In contrast, the relative permittivity generally increases with printing angle, whereas the AC breakdown strength and dielectric loss exhibit more complex non-monotonic variations. The tensile strength and elongation at break both gradually decrease with increasing printing angle. The thermal conductivity varies only slightly across different orientations but increases overall with printing angle. Microstructural observations reveal numerous interlayer pores, incompletely sintered regions, and heterogeneous interfaces with a distinct layered distribution. These heterogeneous interlayer structures affect the transport of charge, heat, and load, thereby contributing to the anisotropic electrical, thermal, and mechanical properties of SLS-printed PA12. These findings provide a basis for optimizing the printing orientation and structural design of SLS-printed PA12 for high-voltage insulation applications.

42943734.titulo: Polyphosphate-Functionalized PGMA-Grafted Mesoporous Silica Nanoparticles for Selective U(VI) Removal from Aqueous Solutions.
42943734.autores: Alshammari AS, Alosime EM, Basfar AA
42943734.resumo: Uranium(VI) contamination in aquatic environments poses significant environmental and public health concerns, creating a need for efficient and selective adsorbents. In this study, polyphosphate-functionalized poly(glycidyl methacrylate)-grafted mesoporous silica nanoparticles (PP-PGMA/MSNs) were successfully synthesized and evaluated for U(VI) removal from aqueous solutions. A key novelty of this work lies in the incorporation of phosphate-rich functionalities onto PGMA-grafted MSNs prepared via ATRP, together with the systematic investigation of their effects on U(VI) adsorption equilibrium and selectivity in multi-metal systems. Fourier-transform infrared spectroscopy (FTIR), Brunauer-Emmett-Teller (BET), scanning electron microscopy (SEM) and thermogravimetric analysis (TGA) confirmed the successful incorporation of phosphate-containing functional groups onto the MSN surface. The adsorbent exhibited rapid adsorption, reaching equilibrium within 120 min, with optimum performance observed at pH 4-6. A maximum U(VI) removal efficiency of 73.81% was achieved at an initial concentration of 10 mg L-1, while the maximum adsorption capacity reached 114.94 mg g-1. Equilibrium data were well described by the Langmuir isotherm model (R2 = 0.9697), indicating predominantly monolayer adsorption on relatively homogeneous adsorption sites. Despite a substantial reduction in surface area following functionalization, the material maintained a high adsorption capacity, suggesting that uranium uptake is governed primarily by interactions at phosphate-containing active sites. Furthermore, the adsorbent exhibited preferential affinity toward U(VI) in multi-metal systems containing Cr, Ni, Cu, Zn, Cd, and Pb ions, demonstrating enhanced selectivity toward uranyl species. The adsorption behavior suggests that phosphate functionalities serve as the primary binding sites through surface complexation and coordination interactions. These findings demonstrate the potential of PP-PGMA/MSNs as selective adsorbents for U(VI) removal from complex aqueous systems and environmental remediation applications.

42943702.titulo: Electrospun Carbon Nanofiber-TiN Composite Interlayers for Improved Cycling Stability and Rate Capability of Lithium-Sulfur Batteries.
42943702.autores: Niu C, Liu H, Chao Z
42943702.resumo: Lithium-sulfur (Li-S) batteries offer a high theoretical energy density of 2600 Wh·kg-1 and a theoretical specific capacity of 1675 mAh·g-1; however, their practical application is severely hindered by the shuttle effect of soluble lithium polysulfides, the intrinsic electronic insulating nature of sulfur and Li2S, and the substantial volume variation during charge/discharge processes. In this study, titanium nitride (TiN) powder was first prepared, and a carbon nanofiber/titanium nitride (CNF@TiN) composite nanofiber membrane was subsequently fabricated by electrospinning followed by pre-oxidation/carbonization treatment and employed as a functional interlayer between the separator and sulfur cathode. X-ray diffraction (XRD) and high-resolution transmission electron microscopy (HRTEM) showed that the obtained TiN possessed a well-crystallized face-centered cubic structure. Scanning electron microscopy (SEM), transmission electron microscopy (TEM), and energy-dispersive X-ray spectroscopy (EDS) revealed that TiN particles were relatively uniformly dispersed and anchored within the three-dimensional interconnected CNF network. X-ray photoelectron spectroscopy (XPS) analyses of the composite and the TiN powder confirmed the presence of Ti-N bonding, revealed N/O-containing functional groups on the carbon scaffold, and indicated only a thin oxidized layer on the TiN particle surface. Nitrogen adsorption-desorption analysis confirmed the porous character of the fibrous interlayers. Electrochemical tests showed that the cell equipped with the CNF@TiN interlayer delivered an initial discharge specific capacity of 1205 mAh·g-1 at 0.1 C and retained a reversible capacity of approximately 1010 mAh·g-1 after 100 cycles. At 0.2 C, the initial discharge specific capacity was approximately 1065 mAh·g-1, and approximately 875 mAh·g-1 was retained after 300 cycles, corresponding to a capacity retention of 82.2% and an average capacity decay of approximately 0.059% per cycle. Rate capability, cyclic voltammetry (CV), electrochemical impedance spectroscopy (EIS), and galvanostatic charge-discharge measurements indicated that the CNF@TiN interlayer favors reversible sulfur-species conversion and improved interfacial reaction kinetics. The enhanced performance can be attributed to the physical confinement, electron-transport, and structural-support functions of the CNF network, together with the polar TiN interface, whose presence is consistent with restricted polysulfide migration and facilitated interfacial conversion. This work provides a feasible strategy for designing multifunctional interlayers integrating electrical conductivity, physical confinement, and interfacial regulation for Li-S batteries.

42943051.titulo: Chemical and Biological Mobilization of Soil Phosphorus by ppk-Expressing Transgenic Rice (Oryza sativa L.).
42943051.autores: Yang S, Wang M, … Yang L (12 autores)
42943051.resumo: Phosphorus (P) availability in alkaline soils is constrained by the immobilization of legacy P, particularly through calcium phosphate precipitation. We used a confined soil-plant microcosm to examine how expression of the polyphosphate kinase gene (ppk) is associated with legacy P utilization in rice (Oryza sativa L.). We compared ppk-expressing transgenic rice (ETR) carrying single-copy (ETRS) and double-copy (ETRD) insertions with their isogenic wild type (WT), without P fertilization. Both transgenic lines had higher root organic acid release and acid phosphatase activity on day 30 and greater plant P acquisition by day 60 than WT; soil pH declined to a greater extent. On day 30, transgenic roots released more oxalate and malate, and their exudates mobilized more soil P than WT exudates in a separate incubation assay. These traits corresponded to greater depletion of the operationally defined HCl-P and NaOH-P pools. Bacterial profiles and PICRUSt2 predictions were descriptive because one pooled library per genotype precluded tests of genotype effects. Diffusive gradients in thin films (DGT) measurements revealed greater rhizosphere labile P in the ETRD early in plant growth, followed by a decline as plant P concentrations increased. This pattern was consistent with an early increase in P supply followed by plant-driven depletion. Net P acquisition in ETRD was 2.55 times that in WT, and ETRD exhibited 53% greater root biomass, while ETRS showed intermediate responses.
