Collectively, these results link enhanced plant P acquisition to greater P release in exudate incubation assays and higher acid phosphatase activity within this confined system.

42941008.titulo: The Impact of Intra-Burst Energy Distribution on Volume Removal and Surface Quality in Laser Ablation of Stainless Steels Using Ultrashort Pulsed Lasers.
42941008.autores: Obergfell D, Soldera F, … Lasagni AF (4 autores)
42941008.resumo: Stainless-steel alloys are widely used in applications requiring high corrosion resistance and mechanical durability. For embossing tool fabrication, high-volume material removal with high surface quality is essential. Laser-based ablation offers an alternative to micromilling by enabling material removal without mechanical contact, thereby eliminating cutting tool wear and facilitating the fabrication of complex geometries. However, productivity must be increased without degrading surface quality, which plays a critical role in embossing tool wear behavior and lifetime. This study investigates the ablation efficiency and surface quality of AISI 304, AISI 420, and AISI 316Ti stainless steels using a 250 fs pulsed laser. Different fluence levels and burst configurations, including MHz, GHz, and Bi-burst, are examined, focusing on the influence of intra-burst energy distribution on material removal rate and surface quality. Surface morphology and roughness are characterized by optical, confocal, and scanning electron microscopy. The results show that removal rate, ablation efficiency, and surface roughness are strongly affected by the intra-burst energy distribution (positive or negative slopes). The highest removal rate of 5.74 mm3 min-1 was obtained using MHz bursts, whereas GHz bursts enabled surface roughness values Sa below 1 µm. Negative energy slopes generally reduced surface roughness in isolated MHz and GHz burst modes, while Bi-burst processing provided smooth surfaces over a wider range of slope conditions. All alloys followed similar trends, with AISI 316Ti exhibiting greater susceptibility to microhole formation under certain burst conditions.

42945293.titulo: In situ multimodal imaging reveals compartmentalization of reovirus replication factories.
42945293.autores: Ďurinová E, Bily T, … Tuma R (7 autores)
42945293.resumo: Avian reovirus (ARV) belongs to Reoviridae family of viruses with segmented dsRNA genomes. ARV is responsible for significant economic losses to the poultry industry by causing tenosynovitis and chronic respiratory disease in chickens. ARV virion exhibits an outer protein shell enclosing an inner core, which contains 10 unique dsRNA segments and multiple copies of viral polymerase. ARV assembly takes place in so-called viral factories (VFs). They are cytoplasmic membrane-less inclusions, which accumulate viral proteins and RNA and assist capsid assembly, genome packaging and replication. VFs also provide protection from the host cell defence mechanisms by sequestering viral RNA. Given the dense nature of VFs, little is known about ARV assembly and packaging intermediates. To determine the architecture of VFs across the different length scales and infection course, we employed a wide range of imaging methods. Our data reveal that spherical and fluid VF enriched in viral protein σNS become surrounded by σNS-depleted solid-like compartments at late stages of infection. We demonstrate that confocal Raman microscopy allows label-free imaging of VF composition. Volume electron microscopy, along with electron tomography (ET) and in situ cryo-ET, revealed that the inner phase of VF concentrates viral non-structural proteins and assists assembly of viral cores. The larger, RNA-filled and double-layered particles are assembled at the periphery of the inner fluid phase of VF, forming ordered virion arrays. This suggests that ARV VFs are functionally compartmentalized: the inner fluid phase assists RNA assortment and core particle assembly, whereas the peripheral phase is the site of RNA replication inside viral cores and virion completion.

42935083.titulo: Fragment-Linked Purine Derivatives as Inhibitors of (p)ppGpp Synthetases: Design, Synthesis, and Structure-Activity Relationships.
42935083.autores: Abdalrahman RAM, Erlitz KS, … Koch O (7 autores)
42935083.resumo: The bacterial stringent response, mediated by the alarmone nucleotides (p)ppGpp, plays a central role in persistence of infections, stress adaptation, and antimicrobial tolerance, making (p)ppGpp synthetases attractive targets for novel antibacterial strategies/therapies. In this study, we report the design, synthesis, and biological evaluation of fragment-linked nucleobase derivatives targeting the RelA/SpoT homolog (RSH) enzymes. Guided by structural insights into adenine and guanine binding within small alarmone synthetase (SAS2/RelP), a series of purine-based compounds was developed to simultaneously occupy conserved nucleotide-binding regions. Initial linker-bridged analogues showed limited activity, primarily due to poor solubility, prompting the introduction of ribose-containing derivatives to improve physicochemical properties. Biochemical evaluation using HPLC-based assays revealed selective inhibition of Staphylococcus aureus SAS1, with the most potent compound displaying micromolar activity (IC50 = 1.8 µM), while little or no inhibition was observed for related SAS enzymes. Structure-activity relationship analysis highlights the importance of linker length and nucleobase positioning for enzyme selectivity. These findings establish fragment-linked nucleobase scaffolds as a promising starting point for the development of inhibitors targeting (p)ppGpp biosynthesis and the bacterial stringent response.

42930624.titulo: Comparative Evaluation of En Bloc Staining Protocols for Deep-Learning Segmentation of Dorsal Root Ganglia in SBF-SEM.
42930624.autores: Borisovs V, Bossi M, … Cavaletti G (5 autores)
42930624.resumo: The integration of deep learning algorithms into volumetric electron microscopy can be limited by biochemical sample preparation. En bloc staining protocols, emphasizing heavy-metal contrast, are optimized for the convenience of human visual interpretation. This study evaluates the suitability of three staining protocols for automated segmentation and 3D reconstruction of dorsal root ganglia (DRG): rOTO-based heavy-metal staining (Ellisman), standard transmission electron microscopy (TEM) staining (Palade), and uranyl-free en bloc staining (X-solution). U-Net-based deep learning models were applied to dorsal root ganglia (DRG) samples to segment nuclei, mitochondria, satellite glial cells (SGCs), and the endoplasmic reticulum (ER). Quantitative segmentation performance was evaluated using the Dice similarity coefficient (DSC) and intersection over union (IoU) for each segmented structure group based on the comparison between the automated prediction masks and 30 manually annotated ground truth (GT) sections per staining protocol. Although the Ellisman-stained samples produced strong ultrastructural contrast, more false-positive and false-negative regions were observed for several structures. The Palade protocol provided insufficient membrane contrast to reliably identify the ER in this dataset. In contrast, the uranyl-free protocol produced the highest DSC and IoU values for SGCs and mitochondria and higher ER segmentation scores than the Ellisman protocol.

42946745.titulo: Self-adaptive layered oxide cathodes driven by charge reconfiguration for sodium-ion batteries.
42946745.autores: Li JY, Guo Y, … Xiao Y (18 autores)
42946745.resumo: Layered oxide cathodes have attracted worldwide attention due to environmentally friendliness, structural diversity, and economic benefits. However, poor long-term cycling and unsatisfactory rate performance hinder the practical application. Hence, an oxide cathode with self-adaptive volume has been designed, achieving stable capacity retention of 82% after 1000 cycles at 2 C. The enhanced long-term performance is attributed to its dynamically adjustable volume reducing the acceleration of stress, enabled by a tunable interlayer distance that expands at the beginning of the charging process and then compresses at the highest voltage. Uniform electric field distribution is depicted by 4-dimensional scanning transmission electron microscopy showing even Coulombic interactions between the oxide layers leading to high mechanical integrity. Such self-adaptable behavior originates from the reduced repulsive force between interlayered oxygen due to the charge reconfiguration of intralayer oxygen and transition metal ions. Additionally, the charge compensation behavior is detected by in situ X-ray absorption spectra, which would be beneficial to high-rate performance. The self-adaptive volume change driven by charge reconfiguration provides a pathway toward durable materials for sustainable sodium-ion energy storage.

42929908.titulo: Ambient-Dried Cellulose Nanofibril/H2TiO3 Composite Aerogel for Enhanced Lithium Capture at Seawater-Relevant pH.
42929908.autores: Wang X, Wang J, … Liang D (6 autores)
42929908.resumo: Efficient seawater lithium harvesting requires adsorbents combining high selectivity with scalable, low-energy fabrication. Although H2TiO3 lithium-ion sieves (HTO-LIS) exhibit exceptional Li+ selectivity, their deployment is hindered by strict alkaline requirements and reliance on energy-intensive shaping processes such as freeze-drying. Herein, we report a cellulose nanofibril (CNF) composite aerogel addressing both challenges simultaneously. Ammonium phytate (AP), a bio-derived polyphosphate, serves a dual function: as a green crosslinker for CNF and as an in situ alkalinity generator, creating a localized alkaline microenvironment around immobilized HTO nanoparticles that enables efficient topotactic H+/Li+ exchange at seawater-relevant pH 8 without requiring strongly alkaline bulk conditions. Crucially, the AP-crosslinked CNF skeleton withstands capillary forces during ambient-pressure drying, preserving a hierarchical macroporous network without freeze-drying. The resulting AP-CNF@HTO monolith achieves a Li+ capacity of 19.08 mg g-1 at pH 8, a 128.9% enhancement over pristine HTO, with excellent selectivity against competing ions in real seawater and 88.3% capacity retention after ten cycles. This work demonstrates that rational bio-based crosslinker selection can concurrently solve the alkaline microenvironment and ambient-drying challenges of HTO-LIS composites, offering an ambient-pressure-drying route with reduced reliance on energy-intensive freeze-drying for seawater lithium enrichment.

42936311.titulo: Particle Morphometrics of Glycopyrronium-Formoterol-Budesonide Inhalation Blends Influence Pulmonary Deposition and Bronchodilator Response in Chronic Obstructive Pulmonary Disease (COPD): A Gamma Scintigraphy Study.
42936311.autores: Jain GK, Mishra A, … Madan M (4 autores)
42936311.resumo:
The therapeutic efficacy of inhaled triple-combination therapy in chronic obstructive pulmonary disease (COPD) depends on efficient delivery to peripheral airways. This study evaluated the influence of particle morphometrics on pulmonary deposition and bronchodilator response to glycopyrronium-formoterol-budesonide (GFB) inhalation formulations.
Three commercial GFB formulations (X, Y, and Z) delivered via metered-dose inhaler (MDI) and dry powder inhaler (DPI) were characterized using dynamic light scattering and scanning electron microscopy. In a randomized, open-label pilot study, twenty-four patients with mild-to-moderate COPD inhaled technetium-99m (99mTc) radiolabeled formulations. Regional lung deposition was assessed by planar gamma scintigraphy, and central-to-peripheral (C/P) ratios were calculated. Forced expiratory volume in one second (FEV1) was measured at baseline and 30 minutes post-inhalation.
Significant inter-brand differences in particle morphometrics were observed. Brand X demonstrated a narrow particle distribution (1.3±0.26 µm) with uniform spherical morphology, while brands Y and Z showed relatively broader, polydisperse distributions with irregular particles. MDIs (MIX, MIY, MIZ) consistently outperformed DPIs (DIX, DIY, DIZ), producing greater total lung deposition (23.4% vs 13.7%; P < 0.001) and improved peripheral deposition. Among MDIs, MIX achieved higher intrathoracic deposition (28.8 ± 2.2% vs 19.0-22.5%; P < 0.001) and peripheral deposition (15.8 ± 3.0% vs 9.8-11.5%; P = 0.012), with a lower C/P ratio (0.82 vs 0.96-1.0). Greater spirometric improvement correlated with enhanced deposition, with the MIX producing the highest FEV1 increase (12.8%; P < 0.05).
The findings suggest that particle size distribution, polydispersity, and surface morphology may influence pulmonary deposition and acute spirometric response in COPD. A relatively narrow respirable particle distribution may support more consistent peripheral airway deposition and short-term spirometric response.

42948914.titulo: Ablation of Tnfr1 Gene Impairs Enamel Surface Microhardness and Mineral Composition in Mice.
42948914.autores: Gonçalves JL, Almeida-Júnior LA, … Paula-Silva FWG (7 autores)
42948914.revista: The International journal of developmental biology
42948914.resumo: While the immune response is increasingly suspected to play a role in dental enamel defects, the specific pathways involved remain unclear. This study investigated the effects of Tnfrsf1a (TNF receptor superfamily member 1A) gene ablation on amelogenesis and enamel biomineralization. Male Tnfrsf1a knockout (Tnfrsf1a-/-) and wild-type (C57BL/6) mice (n = 6 per group) were evaluated. Lower incisors were analyzed using visual photography, micro-computed tomography (microCT), scanning electron microscopy (SEM), surface microhardness testing, and energy-dispersive X-ray (EDX) spectroscopy. Protein expression of MMP20, RUNX2, and AMBN was assessed via immunohistochemistry, while in situ zymography quantified MMP gelatinolytic activity. Gene expression was analyzed using RT-qPCR. Tnfrsf1a-/- mice exhibited no macroscopic opacities, though incisors displayed a distinct whitish coloration. While microCT and SEM revealed no significant differences in enamel volume, or prism ultrastructure, the enamel of Tnfrsf1a-/- mice showed significantly lower calcium and phosphorus content and reduced surface microhardness. Molecular analysis revealed that the Ambn gene was significantly upregulated during both the secretion and maturation stages in Tnfrsf1a-/- mice compared to wild-type controls. Ablation of Tnfrsf1a results in enamel color change in mice characterized by altered mineral composition, reduced mechanical hardness, and dysregulated Ambn expression. These findings suggest that TNF signaling acts as a critical modulator during amelogenesis and is essential for achieving the final mineral quality of dental enamel.

42945240.titulo: Regulation of miR-219 and its target RalGPS is essential for synaptic plasticity at the Drosophila neuromuscular junction.
42945240.autores: Aavula K, Heggeness H, … Van Vactor D (5 autores)
42945240.revista: Proceedings of the National Academy of Sciences of the United States of America
42945240.resumo: RNA regulatory mechanisms mediate adaptive responses relying on rapid changes in gene expression. By examining microRNA (miRNA)-mediated control of structural synaptic plasticity, we find miR-219 and five other conserved miRNAs regulate activity-induced morphogenesis at Drosophila glutamatergic synapses. Among miRNA targets downregulated by acute stimulation, the Ral activating factor RalGPS is necessary for presynaptic morphogenesis and is sufficient to block plasticity. We find that RalGPS must be held within a narrow range of expression for structural remodeling to occur. Loss or excess of RalGPS both abolish activity-induced synapse growth. Without altering levels of mature miR-219, stimulation elevates miR-219 loading in Argonaute (Ago1)-containing complexes that mediate miRNA gene silencing. We also find that elevated Protein Kinase A activity suppresses miR-219 association with Ago1 and blocks activity-induced synaptic growth, suggesting that miRNA loading and unloading in neurons are both controlled by activity-dependent regulation of Ago1.

42945237.titulo: Calcium permeability-enhancing mutations in GluRIIC suppress sustained presynaptic homeostatic plasticity triggered by loss of GluRIIA.
42945237.autores: Malak OA, Gray L, … Haghighi AP (10 autores)
42945237.revista: Proceedings of the National Academy of Sciences of the United States of America
42945237.resumo: Presynaptic homeostatic plasticity (PHP) stabilizes neural circuits by adjusting synaptic strength when faced with disturbances in postsynaptic activity. Despite identification of many genes and mechanisms required for PHP, the underlying trigger mechanisms remain elusive. Loss of GluRIIA, one of five glutamate receptor subunits at the Drosophila neuromuscular junction (NMJ), reduces quantal size and synaptic calcium influx and triggers a sustained PHP. Two common features of genetic manipulations that lead to the activation of this form of PHP are a drop in synaptic calcium influx and a reduction in quantal size; however, it is not clear that either of these features is absolutely necessary for PHP. We have generated a glutamate receptor transgene with mutations in the pore, which can largely restore calcium influx in GluRIIA-/- mutant larvae without affecting quantal size. We find that restoration of calcium influx in GluRIIA-/- mutant larvae blocks PHP without any detectable changes in synaptic structure. Our findings, therefore, indicate that a reduction in synaptic calcium influx is necessary for triggering and/or maintenance of the sustained PHP at the NMJ, a model that may be extendable to the vertebrate NMJ and neuron-neuron synapses.

42949131.titulo: Using High-Performance Liquid Chromatography to Study Alterations in Biogenic Amines in Drosophila Models of Brain Disorders.
42949131.autores: Huston NJ, Berry AL, … Hidalgo S (8 autores)
42949131.resumo: Many neuropsychiatric and neurodegenerative disorders are characterized by disruptions in brain neurotransmitters, including alterations in the levels of the biogenic amines (BAs) dopamine (DA) and serotonin (5-hydroxytryptamine; 5-HT), as well as in their release or reuptake. These neurochemical changes correlate with distinct key behavioral phenotypes, such as locomotor deficits, sleep fragmentation, and altered stress responses, among others. Because the principal BA systems interact, disease models frequently show coordinated shifts across multiple amines rather than isolated changes in a single neurotransmitter. Therefore, accurate, simultaneous quantification of several BAs is essential for interpreting behavioral and genetic findings. Drosophila melanogaster offers a genetically tractable system for modeling such disorders and neurotransmitter changes, but BAs occur in fly brain tissue at very low, nanomolar-to-femtomolar concentrations, and the small size of the Drosophila central nervous system makes their detection technically challenging. This study describes a protocol to detect and quantify DA, 5-HT, and octopamine in fly brains using high-performance liquid chromatography coupled with electrochemical detection (HPLC-ECD). HPLC-ECD was applied to detect changes in brain DA and 5-HT in a fly model of Parkinson's disease based on dopaminergic overexpression of human alpha-synuclein. Applying this protocol to the alpha-synuclein Parkinson's disease model reveals significantly elevated dopamine, but unchanged serotonin, relative to controls, consistent with early compensatory dopaminergic mechanisms. This approach provides a sensitive, low-cost, and readily accessible method for multiplexed BA quantification from limited Drosophila tissue. It also enables systematic screening of genetic modifiers and candidate therapeutics targeting monoaminergic pathways relevant to human brain disorders.

42946567.titulo: Organization of neuropeptide signaling: cross-species insights from small model organisms.
42946567.autores: Zandawala M, Filosa A, Beets I
42946567.resumo: Neuropeptides are ancient signaling molecules that modulate neural circuit function and behavior across the animal kingdom. Model organisms such as Caenorhabditis elegans, Drosophila melanogaster, and zebrafish serve as powerful in vivo models for deciphering the organization of neuropeptidergic signaling, owing to their smaller nervous systems, genetic tractability, and the growing availability of neural connectomes. In this article, we review how these organisms have advanced current understanding of neuropeptidergic transmission across three interconnected themes: (i) the roles of peptides in sensory-motor transformations, (ii) the conservation and divergence of peptidergic expression and network architecture across species, and (iii) the diversity of neurotransmission strategies employed by single neurons. Finally, we highlight recent technological innovations as well as open questions that could shape this field in the coming years.

42945321.titulo: foxQ2 marks fast-acting interneurons including dopaminergic neurons of mushroom bodies and central complex in the beetle Tribolium castaneum.
42945321.autores: Pang Y, Klußmann-Fricke B, … Bucher G (8 autores)
42945321.resumo: The brain is one of the most complex animal organs, and the development of the many different neuron types remains enigmatic. A set of brain-specific transcription factors is involved in brain patterning, but their specific contributions mostly remain to be elucidated, including foxQ2II. This transcription factor is conserved in anterior neuroectodermal patterning of most animals, while it has been lost from vertebrates. The contribution of foxQ2II-positive neurons to the adult brain has remained enigmatic. Here, we use our enhancer trap, immunostainings, and our newly established beetle brainbow system to categorize Tc-foxQ2II-positive neurons into nine clusters with different projection patterns. All clusters contain neurons with the fast-activating neurotransmitters acetylcholine and glutamate, while no Tc-foxQ2II-positive neuron is GABA-ergic or serotonin-positive. Interestingly, we found that many dopaminergic neurons were Tc-foxQ2II positive and homologize them with dopaminergic neurons of the PPL2c, PPM1, and PPL1 cluster described in the Drosophila brain. Our results show that Tc-foxQ2II marks subsets of fast-acting interneurons contributing to the higher-order brain centers mushroom bodies and central complex. Taken together, our work expands the known functional range of foxQ2 genes from sensory and neurosecretory cell specification to interneurons involved in the function of higher-order brain centers.

42933601.titulo: Comparative genomics of insect peptide hormones: from annotation artifacts to evolutionary prediction.
42933601.resumo: Insect peptide hormones are central signalling molecules that govern development, metabolism, reproduction and behaviour. Large-scale sequencing efforts have pushed the number of high-quality insect genomes into the hundreds, yet peptide precursor genes are particularly prone to pseudo-loss annotation because the open reading frames encoding mature peptides are extremely short and the mature peptide regions show low sequence conservation. Here we first review how recent methodological advances have uncovered and corrected such spurious gene losses, and we propose an asymmetric framework of evidentiary confidence in which gene presence and gene loss are evaluated against distinct standards. Re-examining the variation landscape of peptide genes after this calibration reveals that both losses and expansions are distributed non-randomly and are tightly linked to life history. On this basis we put forward a neuropeptide co-evolution hypothesis, which holds that major ecological niche transitions, through constraint-release dynamics, jointly drive neuropeptide gene loss, copy-number expansion, remodelling of precursor processing and functional reshaping, and provides a testable framework that moves comparative genomics from phenomenological description toward mechanistic prediction.

42933406.titulo: The antimicrobial peptide pileup promotes enterocyte shedding to maintain gut homeostasis in aging Drosophila.
42933406.autores: Lee JH, Kim SH, … Lee WJ (9 autores)
42933406.resumo: Cellular turnover is a fundamental biological process that counteracts aging by activating stem cells to replace aging cells. This process is especially critical for maintaining the intestinal epithelium, one of the most rapidly renewing tissues in the body. However, the replacement of aging enterocytes cannot be explained solely by the generation of new cells from intestinal stem cells (ISCs); it also requires the complementary process of physically removing aging enterocytes through shedding. Compared with the well-characterized regulation of ISCs, the mechanisms governing enterocyte shedding remain poorly understood. Here, we identify pileup, a novel age-associated antimicrobial peptide (AMP) in Drosophila, as both a genetic marker and a key regulator of enterocyte shedding. Reactive oxygen species (ROS) generated through age-related mitochondrial dysfunction, a process facilitated by Autophagy-related gene 1 (ATG1) kinase, activate hypoxia-inducible factor 1α, which induces pileup expression specifically in aging enterocytes. Pileup then compromises the membrane of these cells and triggers c-Jun N-terminal kinase (JNK) activation, which we propose promotes their shedding. Notably, pileup has three homologs, and loss of all four genes leads to tumorous cell accumulation, gut barrier dysfunction, microbiome dysbiosis, and premature death. Our findings reveal a previously unrecognized role for AMPs in the turnover of aging host cells, extending their classical function beyond microbial defense. This work provides new mechanistic insights into enterocyte shedding and underscores its essential role in preserving gut homeostasis during aging.

42931811.titulo: Heterogeneous responses to embryonic critical period perturbations within the Drosophila larval locomotor circuit.
42931811.autores: Krick N, Davies JJ, … Landgraf M (9 autores)
42931811.resumo: As developing neural circuits become functional, they undergo a phase of heightened plasticity that facilitates network tuning in response to intrinsic and/or extrinsic stimuli. These developmental windows are termed critical periods (CPs) because perturbations during but not outside the CP can lead to lasting changes, such as the formation of sub-optimal or unstable networks. How separate but connected elements within a network might respond differently to a CP perturbation is not well understood. To study this, we used the locomotor network of the Drosophila larva as a model and heat stress as a CP stimulus that has ecological relevance. When embryos experienced heat stress, the subsequent development of their locomotor network was changed, creating larvae with reduced crawling speed and decreased network stability. Developing body wall muscles and central neurons are sensitive to heat stress perturbations during distinct, consecutive phases of embryogenesis. Within the CNS, transient embryonic CP perturbation leads to increased synaptic drive from premotor interneurons to motoneurons, which in turn adopt reduced excitability. In contrast, the peripheral neuromuscular junction maintains normal synaptic transmission, despite significant structural changes. Thus, connected elements respond differentially to a CP perturbation, suggesting a sequence, or hierarchy of network adjustment during the CP.

42940974.titulo: Genetic and Biological Basis of High Royal Jelly-Producing Bees Apis mellifera ligustica: From Larval Signal Perception to Glandular Secretion.
42940974.autores: Wu N, Ao W, … Li J (4 autores)
42940974.resumo: Royal jelly (RJ), the glandular secretion that determines honeybee caste, is also a high-value apicultural product. China supplies about 90% of the world production volume, almost entirely through high RJ-producing bees (RJBs) selected from Apis mellifera ligustica over four decades, or Chinese-selected a. m. ligustica population; these yield up to ten times more RJ per colony than ITBs. Here, we review and assemble the morphological, proteomic, genomic and behavioural evidence for that unusual selection response at four levels. RJ production may be dominated by a heritable polygenic trait whose acceptance and secretion components carry significant genotypic variance, and the selected candidate genomic architecture combines a large inversion with the tandem mrjp cluster. RJB nurses could detect larval volatiles more sensitively, and cross-fostering suggests that larval acceptance depends on the genotype of the nurse bees, not that of the larvae. RJB hypopharyngeal glands develop larger acini, delayed regression and reinforced protein synthesis, whereas mandibular glands up-regulate the fatty-acid pathway that may yield 10-HDA. An expanded nurse-stage neuropeptidome and a remodelled brain membrane proteome may tune larval recognition, water homeostasis and pollen collection. The proposed three coupled feedback loops and outline the experiments needed to test the model.

42940947.titulo: Effect of PBAN on Pheromone Production and Biosynthetic Pathway of the Major Sex Pheromone Component of Proeulia auraria Clarke (Lepidoptera: Tortricidae).
42940947.autores: Reyes-García L, Curkovic T, … Flores-García M (6 autores)
42940947.resumo: Proeulia auraria (Lepidoptera: Tortricidae) is a native Chilean moth and a significant pest of several fruit crops. Its sexual communication relies on pheromones, of which (E)-11-tetradecenyl acetate (E11-14:OAc) is the major component, but the mechanisms regulating its production and biosynthetic pathways are poorly understood. We studied the effect of pheromone-biosynthesis-activating neuropeptide (PBAN) on pheromone production and its biosynthesis through isotopic labeling using deuterated fatty acids, which were topically applied to the pheromone gland. Gas chromatography-mass spectrometry (GC-MS) analysis was then performed. PBAN application increased E11-14:OAc by up to eight times. In labeling experiments with [16,16,16-2H3]hexadecanoic acid (D3-16:acid), the mass spectrum of E11-14:OAc showed a shifted ion at m/z 197 and a natural ion at m/z 194. These results indicated the incorporation of three deuteriums into the terminal methyl group and that chain shortening from palmitic acid to the 14-carbon skeleton occurs through β-oxidation from the carboxyl end. Deuterium incorporation was also detected after D3-18:acid and D3-14:acid application. The findings provide the first direct evidence regarding the precursors and direction of chain shortening in the pheromone biosynthesis of P. auraria. The information contributes to our understanding of its chemical communication and could lay the foundation for the development of pheromone-based control tools.

42939706.titulo: A lnc6100-Mediated ceRNA Network Regulates Dopamine-Dependent Food Wanting in Honeybees.
42939706.autores: Wu Z, Zhu Y, … Su S (8 autores)
42939706.resumo: The honeybee, Apis mellifera, is a highly social and ecologically important pollinator whose foraging activity is essential for colony nutrition and survival. Food wanting is a fundamental motivational state that drives food-seeking and foraging behaviors, yet the molecular mechanisms underlying dopamine-dependent food motivation remain poorly understood. Here, we integrated transcriptomic profiling of honeybee brains (n = 120) with bioinformatic prediction to identify three candidate lncRNAs highly associated with miR-375-3p, a microRNA previously implicated in the regulation of food wanting through the dopamine synthesis pathway. Functional screening using three complementary behavioral assays then identified lnc6100 as a key regulator of food wanting. Mechanistically, dual-luciferase reporter assays confirmed that lnc6100 directly interacts with miR-375-3p. Knockdown of lnc6100 increased miR-375-3p expression, reduced Ddc expression, and decreased brain dopamine levels, indicating that lnc6100 promotes dopamine synthesis through the miR-375-3p/Ddc pathway. Furthermore, inhibition of miR-375-3p rescued the impaired food wanting, restored Ddc expression, and increased dopamine levels in lnc6100-knockdown honeybees. Together, these findings support an lnc6100-miR-375-3p-Ddc regulatory axis through which noncoding RNA interactions regulate dopamine synthesis and food wanting in honeybees. Our study reveals the molecular mechanism by which the upstream noncoding RNA that regulates dopamine-dependent food wanting, providing new insights into lncRNA-based strategies to improve honeybee colony health.

42940927.titulo: Integrative Advances in Honey Bee Gut-Brain Interactions: From Microbiota Dynamics to Behavioral Regulation and Colony Health.
42940927.autores: Xiong T, Hu Z, … Li Y (5 autores)
42940927.resumo: Honey bees provide a tractable model for studying the gut-brain axis in social insects. Unlike mammalian systems, the gut-brain axis in honey bees is jointly shaped by a relatively simple yet functionally specialized microbiota, physiological traits determined by caste differentiation and division of labor, and social interactions within the colony. Accumulating evidence indicates that gut microbes can influence neural function in honey bees through metabolic, immune, and neuroendocrine pathways, thereby affecting cognition, social behavior, immune homeostasis, and other host traits, and ultimately influences colony performance. Conversely, changes in host physiological state and environmental exposures can also reshape the gut microbiota, forming a dynamic feedback circuit between gut status and brain function. Given the high sociality of honey bees, microbial transmission and behavioral interactions among individuals may further amplify gut-brain axis effects and influence overall health of the colony. This review summarizes the establishment and temporal dynamic of the honey bee gut microbiome, the information transfer mechanisms between gut microbes and the host nervous system, and the effects of these interactions on key behaviors (learning, memory, foraging) and colony performance. It also examines major perturbing agents-pesticides, antibiotics, and pathogens-and explores strategies for colony health maintenance from the perspective of the gut-brain axis. Finally, the potential of microbiome-targeted interventions for improving colony health is critically evaluated. This review proposes an integrative framework from microbial dynamics to behavioral regulation and colony health, serving as a reference to promote basic research on the honey bee gut-brain axis and its applied translation for sustainable colony health management. These findings may also provide heuristic value for the study of human gut-brain interactions, neurobehavioral disorders related to microbial dysbiosis, and the development of microbiome-targeted health intervention strategies.

42940653.titulo: Pediatric Anaphylaxis in a Tertiary Pediatric Emergency Department: Observation Duration and Biphasic Reactions.
42940653.autores: Ayar M, Demir Ş, … Çağlar A (4 autores)
42940653.resumo: Background/Objectives: Biphasic reactions are an important consideration during post-treatment observation of children with anaphylaxis; however, real-world pediatric data on observation practices and the timing of these reactions remain limited. This study aimed to describe the clinical characteristics, management practices, observation duration, and occurrence of biphasic reactions among children presenting with anaphylaxis to a tertiary pediatric emergency department (PED). Methods: This single-center retrospective observational study included children aged 0-18 years who presented with anaphylaxis to a tertiary PED between January 2014 and December 2024. Potential cases identified through ICD-10 codes and PED intramuscular adrenaline administration records were reviewed to confirm the diagnosis according to established criteria. Demographic and clinical characteristics, suspected triggers, treatments, observation duration, and biphasic reactions were evaluated. Results: Seventy anaphylaxis episodes in 68 patients were analyzed. The median age was 93.5 months (IQR, 50-156). Food (32.9%) and insect stings (28.6%) were the most common suspected triggers, followed by drug/vaccine-related triggers (18.6%) and allergen immunotherapy (11.4%). Adrenaline was administered in 94.3% of episodes, and intravenous fluid therapy in 50.0%. Central nervous system involvement and age-adjusted hypotension were more frequent among episodes receiving intravenous fluid therapy (p = 0.004 and p < 0.001, respectively). The median PED observation duration was 5.5 h (IQR, 2-8). Biphasic reactions occurred in three episodes (4.3%), all within three hours after initial symptom resolution. Conclusions: In this tertiary PED cohort, adrenaline administration was frequent, and biphasic reactions were uncommon and occurred during the early observation period. Given the small number of biphasic reactions, these findings should be interpreted as descriptive and are insufficient to determine the optimal observation duration.

42935373.titulo: Microsatellite expansion redirects chromatin modifiers to confer insect resistance to Bt bioinsecticides.
42935373.autores: Ouyang C, Sun K, … Guo Z (13 autores)
42935373.resumo: Microsatellites are highly mutable genomic elements, yet their role in adaptive gene regulation in insects remains poorly understood. Here, we show that a tetranucleotide (ATGT) microsatellite expansion in the promoter of ABCC2, a key Bacillus thuringiensis (Bt) toxin receptor gene, epigenetically silences its expression and confers resistance to Bt Cry1Ac toxin in Plutella xylostella (L.). Mechanistically, long repeats (≥27 units) in Cry1Ac-resistant strains preferentially recruit the histone methyltransferase E(z), promoting H3K27me2/3 deposition, chromatin compaction, and transcriptional silencing, whereas short repeats in susceptible strains maintain open chromatin through Tip60-mediated H4K5 acetylation. This repeat expansion alone is sufficient to repress ABCC2, thereby conferring Bt resistance, while repeat length, chromatin state, and associated phenotypes partially revert under relaxed selection. These findings define a previously uncharacterized cis-acting element dynamically orchestrating insecticide resistance-associated gene expression and identify microsatellite-driven chromatin remodeling as a general and plastic regulatory strategy underlying rapid xenobiotic-resistance evolution in insects.
42935373.metodo: ChIP-qPCR para marcas de histonas H3K27me3/H4K5ac e mapeamento genômico fino de repetições em tandem.
42935373.implicacao: Identifica mecanismo epigenético de resistência a Cry1Ac mediado por expansão de microssatélites no promotor de ABCC2, relevante para o monitoramento de resistência em Anticarsia.

42928798.titulo: Which treatment is most effective at reducing the damage caused by the pest box tree moth? A case in a Mediterranean mountain.
42928798.autores: Corominas F, Vilar L, Bou J
42928798.resumo: Boxwood (Buxus sempervirens) is an important element of the European plant landscape. Currently, this species is seriously threatened due to the high impact of the pest box tree moth (Cydalima perspectalis). This lepidopteran is an invasive species of Asian origin that feeds exclusively on the genus Buxus. Management of this pest is necessary, but field trials are lacking. The aim of this study is to provide robust information about the effectiveness of the three major control methods currently available through a case study on a Mediterranean mountain. These treatments include the application of Bacillus thuringiensis and mass capture with sex pheromones in combination with the use of parasitoids of the genus Trichogramma. The experiment was carried out at Pla Boixer, NE Iberian Peninsula. Between 2020 and 2022, damage to boxwood was sampled and analysed at different scales. The results show that Bacillus thuringiensis reduced defoliation by 53%, whereas mass trapping only preserved regrowth with no significant reduction in damage (p > 0.05). Trichogramma releases did not significantly affect damage levels, nor in combination with other treatments. The treatment with B. thuringiensis protected the boxwood from defoliation but its use should be limited to specific cases in which boxwood is highly affected at the regional scale because of its impact on ecosystems and the difficulty of its application. No seasonality was observed in the damage; however, regrowth showed a favourable trend from spring to autumn. These insights should be considered in future management plans for this pest.

42940908.titulo: Expression Profiles of Chitin Deacetylase Genes and Functional Characterization of Key Genes in Spodoptera frugiperda.
42940908.autores: Sun L, Hu Y, … Wu D (8 autores)
42940908.resumo: Chitin deacetylase (CDA) are critical enzyme involved in the growth and molting of insects. Targeting CDA offers a novel approach for developing environmentally friendly, control strategies against the fall armyworm, Spodoptera frugiperda (S. frugiperda). In this study, we performed functional characterization of CDA genes in this agriculturally important pest. A total of seven CDA genes, designated SfCDA1-7, were identified. Quantitative real-time PCR (qRT-PCR) was used to systematically profile the expression patterns of these SfCDA genes across different developmental stages and tissues. The results showed relatively high transcript levels during the third and fifth instar larval stages, with predominant localization in the integument and midgut. Based on these findings, double-stranded RNA (dsRNA) targeting each SfCDA gene was designed, synthesized, and injected into larvae to achieve RNA interference-mediated gene silencing. Knockdown of each SfCDA gene via injection revealed that silencing SfCDA2, SfCDA3, and SfCDA6 resulted in mortality rates of 16%, 13% and 60%, respectively, whereas knockdown of the remaining genes induced no significant larval mortality. SfCDA6 exhibited the most pronounced effect. Subsequently, nanoparticle-mediated feeding was employed to silence SfCDA6, which led to severe molting defects during the late sixth-instar larva-to-pupa transition, characterized by body shrinkage, developmental arrest, and eventual death, with a mortality rate of 53%. Therefore, SfCDA6 represents a highly promising molecular target for controlling S. frugiperda via RNAi-mediated knockdown. This study clarifies the biological functions of chitin deacetylase genes in S. frugiperda molting and development, and identifies SfCDA6 as a novel potential target for RNAi-based pest management.
